### Mixed HTML article text survives recognized-block extraction

An article containing text `Before`, a paragraph `Middle` and text `After`
returned only `Middle`. The flattener emitted its recognized blocks and ignored
all other retained article text whenever any such block existed. A regression
reproduced that loss (`/tmp/cave-html-mixed-red.log`).

The extractor now walks the retained article in document order, collecting text
outside recognized blocks and emitting each outermost block once. It skips that
block's descendants to avoid duplicates. The traversal is iterative; inline
markup keeps adjoining word fragments together. Regression cases use raw text,
spans and nested containers before/after a paragraph, then verify exact URL
content and digest. The existing nested-block, table/definition-label, plain-body,
title and preformatted-whitespace tests remain green. Readability still chooses
which article content is retained; this change does not turn article extraction
into lossless HTML conversion.

### Query identity audit distinguishes fixed binding order from locale sorting

Reviewed `packages/query/src/compile.ts`, `record.ts` and `page.ts` after the
Unicode comparator fixes. Ordinary binding maps use `Object.fromEntries` over
one compiled variable-column map; transitive maps insert the fixed subject and
object slots. Consequently the JSON binding keys used to collapse aliased
transitive answers have consistent field order within a query and do not sort
through locale collation. Computed keys and `Object.fromEntries` retain
prototype-named variables as own properties. Existing query regressions cover
ordinary/transitive `__proto__` bindings and their JSON round trips.

The adjacent shape suggestion comparator has a different contract: its limited
heap deliberately preserves the unlimited sort's stable tie order. Its guide
and existing collation-equivalent-name regression explicitly cover that
behavior. No blanket replacement of display/ranking locale comparisons is
justified by the evaluator or sync identity findings. This is a bounded source
and contract review, not a proof that all query or Unicode behavior is correct.

### Decimal suffix cancellation avoids unnecessary bigint operands

Exact decimal parsing previously built full numerator/denominator bigints even
when trailing coefficient zeros cancelled the scale. It now removes only the
cancellable suffix in text before bigint construction, preserving signs and
the remaining scale. Integer-valued spellings can return integer text directly.
The arithmetic oracle now covers 330 sign/coefficient/exponent combinations,
including long zero suffixes and integer coefficients whose zeros only partly
cancel a negative exponent.

### Linear product chains retain bigint intermediates

### Structured record construction owns its captured semantic claim

After provenance capture, `Record.of` still computed a key and canonical text
from the supplied claim and retained that caller-owned object. Repeated getter
reads could disagree, and later edits to nested terms, values, contexts or tags
could invalidate the returned record's identity. A regression observed four
subject getter reads before the fix (`/tmp/cave-record-claim-capture-baseline.log`).

Construction now structured-clones the semantic claim before key validation and
canonical emission, and returns that captured claim. The regression verifies one
getter read, unchanged record encoding after caller mutations to all those
nested fields, and successful decode of the resulting record. The store guide
documents claim capture and the structured-cloneable constructor input contract.
Returned records remain editable by their owners; this does not freeze them or
replace the constructor's existing semantic checks with exhaustive decoding.

`26.log`). Root and website builds, ten documentation projection tests,
changeset metadata and scoped whitespace checks pass. Full workspace, packed
and production-browser checkpoints predate this capture change. Projection
measurements also predate both the provenance and claim captures, so their

### Filtered-page projection failure retains errors and caller transaction ownership

regressions now cover numeric/valid-time pages with a lone projection failure
and with a simultaneous snapshot-release failure. Projection throws an
unprintable value. A lone failure retains that exact value; a combined failure
preserves it as cause and first aggregate entry, followed by the release error.
Only the page's outer read savepoint is released after projection failure.

The tests stage a claim inside a caller-owned transaction, fail page projection,
restore the injected callbacks, successfully retry inside the same transaction,
and then throw to roll back the caller transaction. A following page is empty,
proving the read did not commit staged work; a fresh append/query succeeds.
For combined failure, the injected callback performs the actual RELEASE before
throwing. This proves error composition and ownership after a reported cleanup
error, not recovery from a genuinely unreleased or unusable SQLite handle.

### Structured comment text round trips document whitespace normalization

Follow-up review of the report line-ending fix confirmed a distinct canonical
text boundary: the parser intentionally removes empty comment edge lines and
trailing whitespace, and treats CRLF as a physical newline. An initial probe
expecting exact trailing empty-line preservation failed; inspection of
combineComment and the parser README confirmed this is documented normalization,
not a new parser defect. No runtime behavior was changed.

A canonical regression now checks structured comments with trailing and leading
empty lines, interior blank paragraphs, CRLF and indented text. It verifies the
normalized comment, unchanged claim key and input object, and stable subsequent
canonical emission. The canonical README explains the boundary and points users
requiring stored byte preservation to exact snapshots. All 61 canonical tests
pass on Node 24.21.0 and Node 26.8.1; root and website builds and changeset
metadata pass. Logs are `/tmp/cave-comment-empty-baseline.log`,
`/tmp/cave-comment-normalization24.log`, `/tmp/cave-comment-normalization26.log`,
`/tmp/cave-comment-normalization-build.log` and
`/tmp/cave-comment-normalization-site.log`. Full workspace integration and the
broader review remain separate open work.

### Report citation comments fold all Markdown line endings

Structured claims can retain CRLF or CR comments. Report citations previously
split comments only on LF, leaving carriage returns inside their Markdown code
spans. A regression reproduced the retained CR in an otherwise successful
report. Citation formatting now folds CRLF, CR and LF into the same slash
separator, keeping footnote definitions on one line without modifying history.

The regression inserts comments through the public structured append API,
checks the report, and compares all stored claim rows before and after rendering
for each line-ending form. The view README documents the presentation rule.
All 125 view tests pass on Node 24.21.0 and Node 26.8.1, along with root and
website builds, nine documentation checks and changeset metadata. Logs are
`/tmp/cave-report-comment-baseline.log`, `/tmp/cave-report-comment24.log`,
`/tmp/cave-report-comment26.log`, `/tmp/cave-report-comment-build.log`,
`/tmp/cave-report-comment-site.log` and `/tmp/cave-report-comment-docs.log`.
The full workspace checkpoint below predates this additional regression and
the preceding backup/CLI tests. Remaining historical serialization boundaries
and the broader review are still open.

CLI commands display that message, so they hid the actionable failure details.

include the safely formatted cause while preserving the existing cause chain.
Simultaneous directory sync and close failures remain visible together.

with both destination and cause in stderr, and confirm that outer cleanup removes

and documentation tests pass on Node 24.21.0 and 26.8.1; root and website builds
and changeset metadata pass. Logs are

### Direct store opens validate access before invoking adapters

Unsupported access modes previously reached SQLite adapters with writable
options and then followed the schema-checking branch. The regression reproduced
an unrelated schema error after adapter opening. Store opening now requires
read-only, no-migrate or migrate before calling the adapter; null and other
unsupported values throw TypeError without coercion. Omitted or undefined
access retains the migrate default.

The shared adapter regression covers invalid strings, null, numbers, booleans,
BigInt, Symbol and an object with a coercion method. Native SQLite and the
website's adapter both record zero open calls and zero coercions, then open
and ingest successfully with corrected access. The store reference documents
the validation boundary.

### Path-based opens reject unsupported intent values

Unknown runtime intent values previously reached the opening branches; an
existing SQLite file used the access mapping's migration fallback. A regression
reproduced an invalid intent opening a database without an error. openAt now

undefined intent retains the documented write default.

coercible object across SQLite, text, memory and missing paths. No coercion or
assembly occurs, existing source bytes remain unchanged, and no missing file

### Path-based opens retain registry and assembly options

openAt previously forwarded an object-rest copy after reading intent. That
silently discarded inherited and non-enumerable registry and assemble options,
allowing text stores to open without requested vocabulary or source assembly.

its declared fields explicitly before selecting the path's opening behavior.

The regression covers both property styles across text, SQLite, memory and
missing paths. Each store receives the custom base registry; text assembly
runs once and can ingest claims using that vocabulary, while the other path
types do not assemble. Source text stays unchanged. The store reference
documents option forwarding independently of property storage style.

### Store-file detection completes short SQLite-header reads

Header detection previously assumed one read supplied all 16 signature bytes.
A regression limiting real reads to three bytes reproduced a valid SQLite
database being misclassified as text. Detection now accumulates bytes at the
correct buffer and file offsets until the header is complete or EOF occurs.

The regression covers a database with a `.cave` name and a 15-byte incomplete
signature with a `.db` name. Six short reads recognize the database; five
chunks followed by EOF reject the incomplete header. Both detection and kind
classification close each descriptor once. Source bytes remain unchanged and
the database opens normally afterward. The store guide documents this behavior.

All 271 store and 74 sync tests passed on Node 24.21.0 and Node 26.8.1.
Workspace and website builds, nine documentation checks, changeset metadata,
scoped whitespace and packed smoke/API checks passed. Logs are
`/tmp/cave-header-short-read-baseline.log`, `/tmp/cave-header-short-read24.log`,
`/tmp/cave-header-short-read26.log` and `/tmp/cave-header-short-read-packed.log`.
The full workspace checkpoint below predates the four latest regressions.

### Text-store loading retains assembly and cleanup failures

Text-store loading previously called store.close in its error handler without
protecting the original failure. A source assembler that registered a failing
cleanup callback and then failed lost its assembly error. The regression
reproduced that loss through both openText and openAt. The handler now throws
an AggregateError containing the load failure followed by the cleanup failure,
with the original load failure as cause and guarded diagnostics for both.

The regression uses real store-owned cleanup callbacks, checks ordinary errors
and unprintable thrown values, and verifies one cleanup attempt, a closed
database, unchanged source bytes and successful fresh replay. The store guide
documents the ownership and recovery contract.

### Public exact comparison avoids an unnecessary difference integer

The public Exact.compare fallback now compares its two cross-products directly,
matching the internal explanation arithmetic approach, instead of allocating
their difference merely to determine its sign. Normalization and validation
of both operands remain ahead of all shortcuts. The existing 5,184-pair signed
fraction oracle verifies ordering, including negative denominators and
equivalent fractions, and retains invalid-operand checks.

The new standalone `scripts/exact-cross-product-bench.mjs` exercises positive
and negative irreducible fractions through 100,000 digits. Seven-sample medians
at that size were 38.46 → 38.19 ms and 38.22 → 38.14 ms on Node 24.21.0,
and 37.64 → 37.80 ms and 37.57 → 37.41 ms on Node 26.8.1. These measurements
do not establish a material speedup. The change removes the intermediate
subtraction; it does not bound general arithmetic work or cross-product size.
Benchmarks ran sequentially before other validation, with logs
`/tmp/cave-exact-products-before24.log`, `/tmp/cave-exact-products-before26.log`,
`/tmp/cave-exact-products-after24.log` and `/tmp/cave-exact-products-after26.log`.

All 131 solver and 78 scenario tests passed on both Node versions. Workspace
and website builds, nine documentation checks, changeset metadata, scoped
whitespace and packed smoke/API checks passed. Validation logs use the
`/tmp/cave-exact-products-` prefix. The full workspace checkpoint below predates
this runtime change and the seven latest regressions.

### Action retraction selects series inside its write reservation

Retraction previously selected current declaration series before starting its
write transaction. A second connection could commit another actor's series in
that gap, leaving a positive series unretracted. The regression reproduced a
report of one retraction instead of two. Selection and the empty-result check
now run inside the same transaction as the retractions.

The two-connection regression checks both a newly committed series and a peer
that has already retracted all series. The former retracts both current series;
the latter reports no current action with complete history unchanged. Both
leave no positive declaration series, and subsequent redeclaration works.
The action reference documents this concurrency and recovery boundary.

### MCP transport failure awaits initialized server cleanup

A gated cleanup regression exposed a remaining race after a successful write:
the SDK's passive transport-close callback could mark its handle closed before
the awaited close path started, detaching server cleanup and losing its error.
The initial regression received only the buffer failure instead of the expected
aggregate. On unexpected transport closure, CAVE now lets its awaited close
path perform teardown without also invoking the passive SDK callback.

The regression commits a claim, exceeds the input buffer, holds server cleanup
behind a gate for an event-loop turn, then throws a cleanup error. Serving stays
pending until the gate opens and rejects with both errors in order, retaining
the buffer failure as cause. Cleanup runs once, listeners are removed and the
complete committed history is unchanged.

All 67 MCP server and stdio tests passed on Node 24.21.0 and Node 26.8.1.
Workspace and website builds, nine documentation checks, changeset metadata,
scoped whitespace and packed smoke/API checks passed. This strengthens the
previous transport-closure fix; the full workspace checkpoint below remains
an earlier integration boundary.

### MCP buffer exhaustion rejects without waiting for EOF

An oversized, unterminated input caused the SDK transport to close while

one-second fallback and then failed with a missing rejection. Serving now
observes unexpected transport closure and propagates its latest transport
error; receiving a new message clears stale diagnostics. Teardown starts
before the SDK marks its handle closed so CAVE can await cleanup.

The regression exceeds the SDK's 10 MiB buffer by one byte while leaving stdin
open. It now rejects without fallback, preserves complete database history and
removes stream/abort listeners. A fresh discovery session succeeds against the
same store. Ordinary malformed-frame and protocol-error recovery tests still
pass because they do not close the transport.

### Provenance backfill belongs to migration, not ordinary reopen

Revalidated the remaining backfill concern from the preceding projection pass.
Provenance.backfill is called by the legacy version-1 migration, not each store
open. A current-schema reopen preserves explicit empty provenance. Sync's
present provenance table is authoritative, and inferred-dimension differences
allowed by conflict checks do not imply that existing target identities are
backfilled during ordinary sync. The initial race experiment therefore did not
perform the assumed update and was removed rather than treated as a defect.

Extended the existing legacy migration regression to assert that read-only open
rejects the unmigrated schema before the existing successful migration/backfill
checks. Existing sync tests also exercise explicit empty provenance across
reopen and text/database interchange. Clarified the query reference accordingly.

### Closed WASM stores report lifecycle errors clearly

Real-store replacement tests found that reading a closed SQL.js database reported
`out of memory`. The adapter now tracks successful closure and checks it before
execution, preparation, export and retained-statement calls. These operations
report an explicit closed-database error. Repeated close is harmless, while a
failed native close does not prematurely mark the wrapper closed and remains
retryable.

close and replacement using real WASM stores. An ordinary ingestion failure
preserves the working store's exact annotated history and usable query results
while closing the candidate. Old-store observer failure, with or without a
candidate observer failure, closes both stores, preserves fatal cleanup errors
and allows a fresh working store. The initial real-store tests failed on SQL.js's
misleading message before the explicit lifecycle guard was added.

### Shared bigint normalization for scenario arithmetic

Measured the separate scenario Euclidean reducer identified in the integrated
review. On consecutive Fibonacci fractions at index 100,000 (41,798 total
numerator/denominator digits), adding zero took about 1.45 seconds and unit
conversion about 1.49 seconds. Reusing `Exact.rational` through decimal strings
improved this case but regressed the 64,000-place common-denominator sum from
about 14 to 24 ms because of serialization and parsing. The final implementation
adds public `Exact.fromBigInts(numerator, denominator)` and routes both rational
parsing and scenario intermediates through its shared normalization. It validates
bigint arguments and nonzero denominators, retains decimal-string outputs and
canonical signs/zero, and adds no model syntax or numeric budget.

The isolated `scripts/scenario-reduction-bench.mjs` now measures Node 24
add-zero/conversion at 34.04/70.80 ms versus 1461.95/1492.44 ms before; Node 26
at 32.66/66.02 ms versus 1449.63/1483.08 ms. Exact output assertions pass for
all four Fibonacci indices. The previous common-denominator benchmark remains
about 14 ms at 64,000 places on both runtimes. These observations do not bound
product growth, standalone input sizes or general normalization time.

### Alias discovery preserves endpoints or reports representation failure

canonical emission. ALIAS is undirected: prefer the conventional less-established
subject, but reverse the emitted relation if only that direction preserves
entity payload identity. The structured `entity`/`canonical` fields retain their
original meaning, score, confidence and evidence. If neither direction is
representable, discovery throws a pair-specific error; it does not return a
numeric claim or silently quote an entity as a literal. This preserves the
current language boundary rather than inventing a new entity-object syntax.
The prior atomic write guard remains in place for retained suggestions.

positive-finite delta validator in metadata emission, matching construction,
parsing and storage. Placing the guard here also covers abbreviated existence
conditions, which do not call the full claim renderer.

### Sigma overrides retain extreme finite magnitudes

Canonical emission interpolated sigma levels with JavaScript's default numeric
string conversion. Valid small and large overrides therefore became tokens such
as `(1e-7σ)` and `(1e+21σ)`, which the decimal-only sigma parser diagnoses and
drops. Use the existing lossless `Value.formatNumber` after validating a positive
finite sigma level. This also rejects malformed structured overrides at the
emitter boundary without extending the language grammar.

Both new regressions failed before the fix. They exercise finite magnitudes from
`Number.MIN_VALUE` through `Number.MAX_VALUE`, standalone emission, grouped and
qualifier claims, annotated store export, strict reimport, metadata and invalid
structured values. The store intentionally omits explicit default level 2 during
export; the regression compares its effective level, retaining that behavior.
All 366 parser/canonical/store tests pass on Node 24 and 26. Root and website
builds, packaged-package/API smoke checks, 9 documentation checks, changeset
validation and scoped whitespace checks pass. The full Node 26 workspace run
passes 2,107 tests across 24 summaries; all 89 browser tests pass (2.0 minutes).
Evidence: `/tmp/cave-sigma-emission-*.log`.

Updated canonical and store READMEs after reviewing documentation projections.
The existing positive finite decimal specification and book syntax remain valid,
so no specification or book edit was needed. This pass fixes serialization; it
does not change the separately validated bounds on derived uncertainty arithmetic.

changing the close-promise rejection branch would not fix actual lost errors.

identity; multiple cleanup errors aggregate. A preceding stream error stays first

behavior; no unsolicited protocol output is introduced.

close error, and EOF incorrectly resolved after a reported cleanup failure. The

continued writes through the borrowed store. The EOF fixture disables the
stream's own automatic destruction to distinguish it from transport ownership.

(`/tmp/cave-mcp-transport-close-pause-final.log`). Cleanup that fails before

### Report real directory-sync failures after snapshot publication (2026-09-08)

is outside the unsupported-sync fallback, so its error cannot be mistaken for
a successful optional sync. The store README lists the exact policy and links
its POSIX error-category and Gnulib portability rationale.

### Implemented an aggregate solver numeric-expansion budget (2026-09-08)

Implemented the preceding proposal as public `Limits.maxNumericDigits`, default
100,000. Validation counts authored integer digits and pre-reduction decimal or
fraction digits across variable bounds, every numeric literal occurrence, and
soft-constraint weights. It rejects excessive expansion with ModelLimitError
before parsing the offending value or invoking a backend. Zero avoids exponent
expansion; explicit larger limits permit larger models. The 75,000-variable Z3
stress fixture now explicitly budgets its 150,000 bound digits as well as its
literals. Its first integration failure correctly exposed the newly independent
numeric limit rather than a need to weaken the default.

Numeric values and fraction fields are captured before budgeting and parsing.
Literal divisor checks reuse the parsed zero result. Canonical serialization and
linear analysis first validate, then copy and revalidate before their own exact
arithmetic. An initial blanket-copy approach broke existing early node-limit and
invalid-identifier contracts; the final approach preserves both and has passing
regressions for changing bounds, fraction getters, and literal divisor values.
The budget is a representation-size limit, not a total CPU or memory ceiling:
intermediate expression arithmetic and standalone Exact helpers remain outside it.

Final verification:

- Full Node 24.16.0 workspace suite: 1,878 tests across 24 summaries, no failures
  (`/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-workspace-node24-verified.log`).
- Node 26.5.0 solver suite: 98 tests
  (`/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-solver-final.log`); Z3 suite: 28 tests, including the
  raised-variable-limit fixture
  (`/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-solvers-node26-verified.log`).
- Root build and final website build passed
  (`/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-build-verified.log`,
  `/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-site-final-verified.log`).
- Node 24 packed smoke passed for all 12 public packages, including the new
  default and excessive-expansion rejection
  (`/tmp/cave-numeric-budget-packed-verified.log`). The reviewed API snapshot
  changes only the Limits field and its declaration fingerprint relative to
  this pass's starting snapshot; final smoke verified it without update mode.
- Minor solver changeset metadata and affected-file whitespace checks passed.

The solver and Z3 references and architecture now describe the budget and its
limits. Website documentation imports those references; no book source or
language semantics changed. This implements one measured enhancement and does
not complete the remaining system review or hosted release validation.

### SQLite parameter reuse and binary ownership (2026-09-08)

The previous browser RETURNING fix made progress. This pass examined parameter
reuse and failure recovery directly on both real SQLite engines. The probes
agreed: omitted positional bindings become NULL, excess parameters throw, empty
blobs retain BLOB type, and binary bytes are preserved. No new production defect
was reproduced at this boundary.

Added a shared contract regression that transitions a prepared read through
complete, partial and empty bindings, then recovers after an excess-parameter
failure. A reused insert verifies that failed binding writes no partial row,
that an empty blob differs from NULL, that all four test bytes survive statement
cleanup and later mutation of the caller's input buffer, and that an omitted
label does not inherit the preceding call's value. Both live adapter references
now document these verified behaviors.

### Browser SQLite RETURNING write counts (2026-09-08)

The previous numbered-highlight optimization pass made progress. This pass
reviewed the browser SQLite adapter against the native statement contract and
found that `run()` stepped only once before reading the change count. For
`INSERT ... RETURNING`, SQL.js yielded the first returned row before finalizing
that count: two rows were inserted but zero changes were reported. A direct
comparison showed native SQLite reporting two, and the shared adapter regression
failed on the browser with `0 !== 2`
(`/tmp/cave-wasm-returning-before.log`).

The browser adapter now drains and discards returned rows before reading
`changes` and `lastInsertRowid`. The shared regression checks multi-row inserts,
statement reuse, updates, deletes, zero-match writes and the persisted final
rows on both real engines. Existing statement cleanup remains in the finally
block. The store and website READMEs document this contract.

### Report filter whitespace and incomplete filters (2026-09-08)

The previous Unicode placeholder pass made progress. This pass found that
report blocks recognized only a literal space after `WHERE`, even though the
query tokenizer accepts tabs. A tab-separated context filter became fragment
prose and the renderer emitted three cited rows instead of the intended one.

(`/tmp/cave-report-filter-whitespace-before.log`).

filters. The README documents the boundary and packed smoke checks the

### Report Unicode placeholder boundaries (2026-09-08)

The previous scoped-projection cleanup pass made progress. This pass found that
report substitution treated only ASCII letters and digits as variable-name
continuations. A binding for `?x` therefore rewrote unknown placeholders such as
`?x東京`; even a longer bound Unicode name could replace the prefix of an unknown
name. The regression reproduced substitutions across accented and astral
letters, Arabic digits, combining marks and CJK text before the fix
(`/tmp/cave-report-unicode-placeholders-before.log`).

Placeholder matching now uses Unicode letter, mark and number boundaries while
retaining longest-bound-name precedence and single-pass substitution. The test
checks that bound `?x` and `?xé` substitute and all unknown names remain intact.
The report README documents the boundary, and the installed-package smoke
exercises the same case through `@cavelang/cli/view`.

### Unpublished scoped-projection cleanup (2026-09-08)

The previous performance-baseline validation pass made progress. This pass found
that a revision-read failure after building a sensitivity projection leaked its
SQLite database: the candidate had not entered the cache and no failure path
closed it. A real SQLite regression injected failure on the post-copy revision
read and confirmed that the unpublished database was still usable before the
fix (`/tmp/cave-scope-revision-cleanup-before.log`).

finally block closes candidates whose ownership was not transferred, including
revision mismatch/retry and read failure. The regression preserves an existing
cache entry, verifies the failed candidate is closed, restores revision reads,

entry normally. The owning viewer README documents this lifecycle.

trigger runs the corrected Unicode reply successfully. This verifies the
consumer behavior of the previous shellComplete fix; no additional runtime
change was needed. The automation README and CLI changeset explicitly state
this distinction between reply rejection and firing replay. All 72 automation
tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build and whitespace check
passed. Logs: `/tmp/cave-agent-encoding-settlement.log`,
`/tmp/cave-agent-encoding-settlement-node24.log`, and
`/tmp/cave-agent-encoding-settlement-build.log`. The previous agent-adapter turn
was progress, recorded below.

The shellComplete agent adapter now enables the process runner's strict UTF-8
stdout option. The regression first demonstrated that a subprocess reply
containing a valid-looking selection followed by an invalid byte returned

accents, and emoji round-trip unchanged. Reconstruction and automation prompt

24; all 71 automation tests and the CLI build also passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-shell-complete-utf8-{before,after,node24,automate,build}.log`.
The generic process runner retains its opt-in default, and no public signature

Reviewed consolidation constraints before attempting to merge the three matching
hook-file readers. Private-package imports are rewritten to public CLI subpaths;

resolution or changing consolidation. No runtime/API refactor was made on that
assumption. IMPLEMENTATION now maps action/doctor, automation, and MCP readers
to their owning regressions, records their shared contract and validation timing,
and explains the installed-resolution checks required for a future move. The
current runtime-dependency verifier and whitespace check passed, and a fresh
website build included the guide (`/tmp/cave-hook-ownership-site.log`). The prior
stream-failure turn was progress; its verified behavior is recorded below.

Automation declaration failure coverage now exercises three distinct stream
termination paths: a truncated multibyte UTF-8 sequence at EOF, premature close
without EOF, and an explicit transport error after a valid buffered prefix.
Each rejects without command stdout or changes to annotated history, removes
all reader data/end/error/close listeners, and allows a corrected declaration
on a fresh stream without resurrecting the discarded prefix. No runtime defect
was found in these paths; this closes a verification gap in the recently
changed reader. The README and CLI changeset describe the guarantees. All 71
automation tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build and whitespace
check passed. Logs: `/tmp/cave-declaration-stream-failures.log`,
`/tmp/cave-declaration-stream-failures-node24.log`, and
`/tmp/cave-declaration-stream-failures-build.log`. The preceding server-startup
cancellation turn was progress, as recorded below.

Direct HTTP viewer and MCP entry points now honor an already-aborted signal
before argument handling, database access, or service startup. Regressions first
showed MCP creating its database and the viewer binding an ephemeral HTTP port
and announcing it before shutting down. They now verify quiet returns, no MCP
database creation or protocol reads, and unchanged viewer history for existing
and absent store paths. All 83 viewer tests and 9 MCP stdio tests passed on Node
26 and Node 24, and the CLI build and whitespace check passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-server-pre-cancel-{before,view,mcp,view24,mcp24,build}.log`.
The owning READMEs and CLI patch changeset describe the direct-entry guarantees;
the dispatcher already provided this guard for routed CLI calls. The previous
connector-startup turn was progress, recorded below.

Direct `runConnect` callers now receive the same already-cancelled startup
boundary as dispatcher callers: a quiet return before argument handling,
source reads, or database access. Inspection found the ordinary source branch
opened its writable database before lower-level cancellation checks; the new
regression first returned a cancellation error instead of stopping at entry.
It now verifies no database creation or output on an aborted initial import,
a successful uncancelled import, and unchanged annotated history for aborted
prune, list, and dry-run calls. In-flight cancellation behavior remains as
previously documented. All 123 connector tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24;
the CLI build and diff whitespace check passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-connect-pre-cancel-{before,after,node24,build}.log`. The connector
README and CLI patch changeset document the package entry boundary. The prior
integration checkpoint was progress, with its current-artifact evidence below.

The current cancellation and hook-validation changes passed an integration
checkpoint: all 1,692 workspace tests in 24 summaries passed on Node 24, with

against the current worktree with the reviewed public API snapshot unchanged.
A fresh production website build incorporated the updated CLI, automation, and
MCP references; targeted browser checks passed for all bundled documentation
section links and responsive routes. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-cancellation-hooks-{integration,packed,site,browser}.log`.
These checks cover the accumulated declaration decoding, stream cancellation,
startup/dispatcher cancellation, quiet signal exits, and hook-file validation
changes together, without claiming hosted deployment or publication. The prior
MCP hook-reader turn was progress, recorded below. Action/doctor share one hook
reader; automation and MCP still have separate matching readers, a possible

MCP hook-file validation now matches the strict contract used by actions,
automation, and doctor: fatal UTF-8 decoding, nonblank JSON keys with string
commands, and no unpaired Unicode surrogates in either. The real-process
regression first showed that an invalid byte inside a command still started
the server and created its database. Four malformed configurations now exit
with code 2, no protocol stdout, and no database creation. A corrected Unicode
configuration round-trips through the reader and starts the real server normally.
All 8 MCP stdio tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24; the final corrected-startup
check also passed on Node 26, and the CLI build and whitespace check passed.
Logs: `/tmp/cave-mcp-hooks-{before,after,node24,recovery,build}.log`. The MCP
README and CLI patch changeset document the pre-startup boundary. No public

recorded below.

The shared CLI dispatcher now checks an already-aborted runtime signal before
argument normalization or command selection/loading. Its existing cancellation
catch returns quietly, while runCli still maps received OS signals to their
exit codes. The regression first found that a cancelled connect invocation
printed help. It now verifies ten command routes (ingest, eval, connect,
automate, serve, MCP, parse, reconstruct, suggest-alias, and highlight) produce
no output and never read stdin when cancelled before dispatch. An uncancelled
help invocation still succeeds. Four targeted dispatcher and real automation
signal tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build and diff check
passed. Logs: `/tmp/cave-dispatch-cancel-{before,after,node24,build}.log`.
The CLI README and patch changeset document the common entry boundary. This
complements command-local cancellation for callers that invoke package entry
points directly. The prior startup-cancellation turn was progress, recorded
below.

An already-aborted automation invocation now returns quietly before argument
handling or database access. The new regression first demonstrated that
`--retract` still appended a retraction despite an aborted signal. It now
verifies unchanged annotated history, empty output, and no new database for
cancelled once/declaration/list commands; an uncancelled retraction still works.
The startup check avoids TypeScript narrowing the live AbortSignal property
across later awaits, so cancellation arriving during work remains checked by the

final startup/pending-read cancellation checks and CLI build also passed.
Logs: `/tmp/cave-automate-pre-cancel-{before,after,node24,final,build}.log`.
The automation README and CLI patch changeset document startup cancellation.
The previous real-process signal turn was progress, with its evidence below.

Real CLI process checks now cover SIGINT and SIGTERM during automation declaration
stdin reads. A preload only observes the actual stream's resume event to establish
readiness, then the test leaves stdin open and sends the signal. Both tests first
exposed an unwanted `This operation was aborted` diagnostic despite correct exit
codes. Automation's outer error handler now treats an observed cancellation
quietly, matching watch-mode shutdown; process lifecycle handling still maps the
received signals to 130 and 143. The module cancellation regression now expects
the same quiet return and still verifies listener cleanup and stream reuse.
Both process tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24 with empty command stdout,
no command error diagnostic, and byte-identical annotated restricted history.
All 69 automation tests and the CLI build also passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-declaration-signals-{before,after,node24,automate,build}.log`.
The automation README and CLI changeset document signal behavior. These tests
exercise the source CLI entry and real OS signals; the build separately verifies
compilation. The previous cancellation-reader turn was progress, recorded below.

Automation declaration stdin now observes cancellation while waiting for more
input. The regression first timed out after aborting a still-open stream; the
reader previously awaited EOF without consulting the signal. The replacement
reader preserves streaming UTF-8 decoding, rejects on abort/error/premature
close, removes its data/end/error/close and abort listeners, and pauses rather
than destroys the caller's stream. A second cancellation check precedes the
actual declaration. The regression verifies unchanged annotated history after
cancelling a buffered valid prefix, listener cleanup, and a successful retry on
the same stream without resurrecting the discarded prefix. All 69 automation
tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-automate-cancel-input-{before,after,node24,build}.log`. The README and
CLI patch changeset describe cancellation and stream ownership. This does not
claim that cancellation can undo already committed settlement work. The prior
hook-configuration turn was progress, as recorded below.

Automation's separate hook-file reader now enforces the same contract as action
execution and doctor: fatal UTF-8 decoding, a JSON object of nonblank names to
string commands, and no unpaired UTF-16 surrogates in names or commands. The
regression first reproduced successful settlement with invalid UTF-8 in a hook
command. It then verified rejection of that input, escaped malformed command
and name strings, and a blank name, all before any stdout settlement report or
change to annotated history. Correcting the configuration consumes the still
pending event exactly once. The automation README and CLI patch changeset
record these pre-settlement checks. All 68 automation tests passed on Node 26
and Node 24, and the CLI build and diff whitespace check passed; logs:
`/tmp/cave-automate-hooks-{before,after,node24,build}.log`. The reader remains
private to automation, with no public API or package dependency changes. The
previous declaration-decoding turn was progress and is recorded below.

Automation declaration input no longer decodes each binary stdin chunk
independently. A fatal streaming UTF-8 decoder preserves multibyte characters
split across chunks and detects incomplete final sequences; declaration files
also use fatal decoding. String chunks remain text, preserving the existing
store-level rejection of malformed UTF-16 instead of repairing it through a
Buffer conversion. A new regression first reproduced successful acceptance of
an invalid byte after a valid prelude claim, then verified file/stdin rejection
with the existing annotated history unchanged. A corrected Unicode declaration
arriving one byte per chunk retains its accented/emoji entity and literal
replacement character. All 67 automation tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24;
the CLI build and diff whitespace check passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-automate-utf8-{before,after,node24,build}.log`. The automation README
and CLI patch changeset describe the boundary. Database opening still precedes
input reading; the guarantee here is no declaration/prelude append on decoding
failure, not absence of a newly created empty database. The separate automation
hook-config reader remains a next review target. The previous turn was progress:
its failure-path verification and full integration/packed evidence are below.

The playground download enhancement now has explicit startup-failure coverage:
a production browser test prevents SQLite from loading, rejects both high and
low unpaired surrogates without any download, then saves a corrected Unicode
draft while queries remain disabled. Saving triggers no SQLite retry. Restoring
the asset and rebuilding recovers the same edited source. Both this failure path
and the normal keyboard/download path passed against the production build; see
`/tmp/cave-download-failure.log`. This verifies the previous turn's documented
runtime-independent behavior without requiring a further runtime change.
The full current workspace suite then passed all 1,684 tests in 24 summaries on
Node 24 with no failures, cancellations, or skips, including the recent fixture,
instruction, and hook decoding changes (`/tmp/cave-download-integration.log`).
The current 12-package packed smoke also passed with the reviewed API snapshot
unchanged (`/tmp/cave-download-packed.log`). No publish or hosted deployment was
performed. The previous turn was progress: the local draft-saving enhancement,
mobile controls, documentation, and browser verification are recorded below.

The browser playground now offers Download claims to preserve work from its
ephemeral editor. It saves the exact current UTF-8 text, including unapplied or
syntactically unfinished drafts, to a sample-named `.cave` file without rebuilding
or appending. The control works independently of the worker and rejects unpaired
Unicode surrogates before Blob conversion. Temporary download URLs are released
after the browser starts the download. The footer wraps at narrow widths; the
page and website README distinguish editor downloads from database history.
A production browser regression verifies the actual downloaded Unicode bytes,
filename, unchanged editor/current-belief count, unapplied notice, and successful
query against the prior database at 320px. Keyboard activation retains button
focus, and the mobile screenshot was inspected. All 54 production browser tests,
37 website unit tests, and the fresh site build passed; the final keyboard and
screenshot refinement also passed independently. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-download-{site,browser,unit,keyboard}.log`. This implements a small
preservation enhancement; it does not add file uploads or persistent browser
storage. The previous evaluation-decoding turn was concrete progress, with its
regression, implementation, documentation and checks recorded below.

Evaluation fixture decoding now rejects malformed UTF-8 in the shared reader for
golden answers, query fixtures, reconstruction knowledge, and loop specifications.
The regression first reproduced silent acceptance of an invalid byte, then verified
file-specific rejection before any agent call for golden and query files. Corrected
fixtures containing valid replacement characters, accents, and emoji recover to a
perfect score. Read/decode failures continue to abort evaluation; semantic fixture
problems retain their existing per-case skip behavior. The evaluation README and
CLI patch changeset document the distinction. All 62 evaluation tests passed on
Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build passed. Logs:
`/tmp/cave-eval-utf8-{before,after,node24,build}.log`.

Hook recovery guidance now reflects the shared validator: doctor explains UTF-8,

before effects from failure of a hook that runs after commit. All eight targeted

configuration cases; the CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks
passed. No book example or public signature changed.

Hook-file review reproduced action execution accepting malformed UTF-8 and
identified separate execution/doctor validators with different name rules.
Both now share a private reader requiring valid UTF-8 JSON, nonblank names,
string commands and well-formed Unicode in names/commands. The regression covers
raw invalid bytes, JSON-escaped surrogate halves in both positions and blank
names; execution rejects before effects and doctor reports its existing redacted
configuration failure. Complete annotated history remains unchanged, and a
corrected configuration executes normally. All nine targeted action/doctor tests
passed on Node 26 and Node 24, including the existing diagnostic-redaction checks.
The CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The CLI reference
documents the common contract; no public signature changed.

Ingestion instruction-file review reproduced invalid UTF-8 reaching prompt
construction through replacement decoding. Instruction loading now shares the

path and purpose. A runtime regression verifies rejection before the agent call,

passed on Node 26 and Node 24; the CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace

The current installed-process checkpoint closes the final getter-capture gap:

The subsequent full Node 24 workspace run passed 1,681 tests across 24 summaries,
with zero failures, cancellations or skips, covering the recent connector/CLI/
text-replay byte decoding, raw-file hashing and strict process-output changes
together. The implementation guide records the installed process checks; shell
syntax, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed.

Process-output review found that the shared runner repaired invalid stdout before
shell-agent consumers could validate claims or structured judge output. Added
the opt-in `strictStdoutUtf8` process option and typed `stdout-encoding` failure;
both async and sync runners preserve ordinary replacement-decoding defaults and
existing resource-error precedence. The flag is captured once, including getters
and non-enumerable values, and cannot be disabled by a caller mutation after
async launch. Shell agents enable it; a real local shell-agent check rejected
invalid output without claims/digests and recovered on retry. Node 24 loop,
ingest and eval suites passed 46/59/61 tests before the final capture assertions;
the final 46 loop tests and CLI build passed on Node 26. The deliberate additive
public API change is recorded as a minor changeset and reflected in the reviewed
packed snapshot. All 12 packed packages passed both snapshot-refresh smoke and
ordinary snapshot verification before the final synchronous getter refinement.
Loop, ingest and eval references describe the contract and judge fallback.
Changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed.

LLM ingestion file hashing reproduced distinct bytes (`FF` then `FE`) collapsing
to the same decoded replacement text and incorrectly skipping a changed file.
Local selection and pre/post-agent drift checks now hash raw bytes; valid UTF-8
digests stay compatible, while old lossy non-UTF-8 digests naturally reselect.
Path-reading agents retain binary-file support. Embedded sources use strict UTF-8
decoding from the selected bytes, including fallback prompt construction, and
retain existing BOM behavior. Unit coverage checks byte-distinct selection,
invalid embedding rejection and valid U+FFFD/accent/emoji content. A runtime test
changes those bytes during an agent call and verifies rejection without stdout
claims or a digest. All 59 ingestion tests passed on Node 24; Node 26 passed
before the final runtime assertion. The final CLI build, changeset metadata and
whitespace checks passed. The ingestion reference records hashing, embedding and
compatibility behavior; helper functions remain private to the implementation.

Connector mapping and declared-CAVE review reproduced malformed bytes being
accepted by both explicit `--map` loading and declared source preparation. All
connector file readers now share a private strict UTF-8 helper with the existing
record-file and fetched-body decoding, preserving their BOM behavior. Regressions
cover CAVE sources and declared mapping files, plus an explicit mapping refresh
under pruning that must fail with no stdout and unchanged annotated history.
Corrected files prepare/run successfully; restoring the explicit mapping leaves
the prior history unchanged. All 122 connector tests passed on Node 26 and Node
24; the CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The connector
reference now lists these file boundaries. The helper is not a public export.

Text-store replay and annotated file sync independently accepted malformed UTF-8
before string validation; both new rejection assertions failed against the prior
readers. `openText` now decodes strictly before creating its in-memory store or
calling assembly, reporting a source-located `LocateError`. `syncFile` keeps
SQLite sources on the binary path and strictly decodes text before parsing or
merging, reporting a source-located error in real and dry-run modes. Tests check
unchanged source bytes and skipped assembly for failed read/scratch opens,
successful Unicode replay after correction, unchanged target history for invalid
annotated sync, and corrected preview/merge/idempotence. All 152 store and 52 sync
tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24; the CLI build, changeset metadata and
whitespace checks passed. Store and sync references describe these boundaries.

The CLI's shared CAVE text reader also silently repaired malformed UTF-8; the
real `parse --json` binary accepted an invalid byte with status 0. File and stdin
reads now use fatal UTF-8 decoding while retaining existing BOM behavior. The
binary regression exercises parse/add/import over both files and stdin, checks
status 1 with no stdout and a source-specific diagnostic, compares existing
annotated history, verifies failed add does not create a missing database, and
then adds/queries explicit U+FFFD, accented text and emoji successfully. The
targeted regression passed on Node 26; it and existing stdin/lint checks passed
on Node 24 (three tests). The CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks
passed. The CLI reference documents the decoding contract. Other independent
file readers are not implied to share this helper.

Structured-source byte decoding review found that local UTF-8 reads silently
replaced invalid bytes before string-level storage checks could see them. Local
CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL loading and fetched text now use fatal UTF-8 decoding with a
source-located diagnostic, retaining their existing BOM handling. Regressions
exercise stray continuation bytes, overlong encodings, encoded surrogate halves
and truncated multibyte sequences in all four formats over files and injected
HTTP responses. Explicit U+FFFD, accented text and emoji round-trip after failures.
A declared-source refresh under pruning and text-store assembly both reject bad
bytes without changing annotated history; restoring the source skips the same
two records and prunes none. All 120 connector tests passed on Node 24; Node 26
passed before the final declared-refresh assertion. The final CLI build,
changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The connector reference
documents strict decoding and recovery. No public signature changed.

The current packed checkpoint now includes the latest read-boundary fixes.
Installed store search rejects malformed Unicode; installed query and match
calls preserve the first transaction-boundary and structured-term getter values,
alongside the existing pagination capture and Unicode append/query checks. The
installed CLI HTTP server rejects malformed UTF-8 and percent escapes for GET
and HEAD with 400/no-store and correct body behavior, then serves a valid entity
request in the same process. All 12 public tarballs packed and installed, the
public API matched its unchanged reviewed snapshot, and the complete smoke
workflow passed. Shell syntax, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed.
The implementation guide describes these installed checks. This supersedes the
packaging evidence gap noted in the preceding integration entry below.

The combined read-boundary checkpoint includes direct-store Unicode validation,
search option capture, export option coverage, MCP stdio recovery, strict HTTP
query decoding, structured-pattern capture and shared query-option capture.
The full Node 24 workspace run passed 1,673 tests across 24 summaries with zero
failures, cancellations or skips. A fresh production website build followed by
all 53 browser tests also passed, covering the real worker/SQLite playground,
Unicode recovery, documentation links, keyboard navigation and failed-download

Numeric normalization retained malformed suffixes as atoms in the exercised
cases, so they remained subject to Unicode validation. The adjacent query-option
review found a separate inconsistency: an `asOf` getter initially returning an
earlier transaction then a later one selected the later value. The shared query
execution entry now captures all declared options before historical vocabulary
lookup, compilation and post-filtering. Regressions check earlier-transaction
results for textual and structured entry points, one accessor read, and a
changing row-limit getter retaining its original cap. All 111 query tests passed
on Node 26 and Node 24; all 46 rules tests passed on Node 24. The CLI build,
changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The query reference documents
the common option boundary; no public signature changed.

Structured query review reproduced a changing payload getter selecting `other`
instead of the initially requested `good` entity: numeric detection and SQL
compilation read different values. Public `match()` now captures declared AST
fields into ordinary data before those stages, including nested slots, payload,
contexts, tags and filters. The internal capture helper does not add an export
to the public API; textual queries use their freshly parsed data directly.
The regression covers literal and exact-numeric terms, checks the expected
entity and one getter read, and the existing malformed/non-enumerable Unicode
cases continue passing. All 110 query tests passed on Node 24; Node 26 passed
before the final numeric assertion. All 46 rules tests and the final CLI build
passed on Node 26. The query reference documents capture; changeset metadata and
whitespace checks passed.

HTTP decoding review reproduced status 200 for a search containing the invalid
UTF-8 sequence `%ED%A0%80`: URLSearchParams repairs those bytes to replacement
characters before store validation can inspect them. The server now validates
the encoded query with strict URI decoding before ordinary parameter parsing,
discarding the validation result so values and delimiters are not double-decoded.
The live-server regression rejects encoded surrogate halves, overlong UTF-8,
invalid bytes and malformed percent escapes for GET and HEAD, checks 400/no-store
and HEAD's empty body, then successfully searches explicit replacement characters,
accents and emoji with a separately encoded literal percent sign. Annotated
history stays unchanged and overview remains available. All 82 view tests passed
on Node 26 and Node 24; the CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks
passed. The view reference documents strict query encoding and recovery. No API
signature, command option or book example changed.

Export option review confirmed that history selection, sensitivity ceiling and
transaction annotation mode already read their option fields once. A shared
native/browser regression now uses changing getters to verify both public
historical values survive with two transaction annotations, the restricted
current value stays excluded, current-only public export remains empty, and
stored current belief remains the secret value. The semantic comparison parses
canonical output so legitimate grouped attribute formatting does not masquerade
as missing claims or annotations. All 151 store and 37 website unit tests passed
on Node 26; the CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The
store reference records this verified boundary. No runtime fix was needed.

Search option review reproduced inconsistent repeated reads: a limit getter
returning 1 then 10 yielded two rows, and a sensitivity getter returning public
then restricted returned both a secret and public row. Search now captures its
three declared options once before validation and SQL construction. Shared
native/browser regressions verify the original cap, rejection of an initially
negative cap even if subsequent reads would be valid, and the original public
sensitivity ceiling, with one read per getter. All 150 store and 36 website unit
tests passed on Node 24; Node 26 passed the same suites before the final
negative-limit assertion. The CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks
passed. The store reference records the option-capture contract; no public
signature changed.

MCP stdio verification sends both unpaired surrogate halves as JSON escapes
through one initialized live session. Literal/raw searches, neighbor lookup,
CAVE-Q and mixed valid/invalid additions all return `isError: true` without a
JSON-RPC protocol error. Corrected queries for explicit U+FFFD, accented text and
emoji succeed in that same session; querying the valid prefix of a rejected
addition confirms no partial claim was appended. All seven stdio tests passed
on Node 26 and Node 24, and the CLI build passed. The MCP reference documents
the checked failure/recovery behavior; changeset metadata and whitespace checks
passed. No transport implementation change was needed.

Direct store reads had the same lossy Unicode binding outside CAVE-Q: searching
or looking up `bad\ud800name` returned a stored `bad�name` record, and topic
traversal returned its child. Read parameters now reject lone surrogates before
SQLite binding; direct alias, current-belief, provenance-ID and edge-ID paths
receive the same guard. The shared native/browser adapter regression covers
both halves across search (including raw syntax and zero limit), entity/alias
and topic traversal, tags, contexts, provenance and belief-key/ID lookups. It
checks unchanged annotated history and successful explicit U+FFFD reads after
rejection. Node 26 store and website suites passed 149 and 35 tests; Node 24
store and query suites passed 149 and 109. The CLI build, changeset metadata and
whitespace checks passed. The store reference documents the direct-read contract
and preserves the exclusion for caller-issued SQL. No public signature changed.

The installed-artifact checkpoint now exercises the storage/query Unicode and
pagination option fixes through the public JavaScript exports. Both lone
surrogate halves must reject whole ingestion batches and query input while
preserving full annotated history. Explicit U+FFFD, accented text and emoji
remain queryable. A changing `all` getter must be read once and produce a cursor
that continues with equivalent plain options to return both historical values.
All 12 packages packed, installed, matched the unchanged public API snapshot and
passed the full smoke workflow, including the earlier fusion/source/sync checks.
The implementation guide records these installed invariants. The subsequent
full Node 24 workspace run passed 1,665 tests across 24 summaries, with zero
failures, cancellations or skips. Shell syntax, changeset metadata and whitespace
checks passed. This is local artifact and integration evidence, not publication.

Pagination review found that cursor fingerprinting read declared option values
directly while query execution received an object-rest copy. Inherited and
non-enumerable `all: true` values therefore identified a history query but ran a
current-belief query, dropping historical results and its continuation; changing
getters could also disagree across those reads. The reproduced regression failed
because the first page had no continuation. Pages now capture every declared
option once before fingerprinting, snapshot selection or execution. The test
traverses three historical values with inherited, non-enumerable and changing
accessor options, continuing with equivalent plain options and checking that
the getter was read once. All 109 query tests passed on Node 26 and Node 24; the
CLI build, changeset metadata and whitespace checks passed. The query reference
records the option-capture contract. No public type or cursor encoding changed.

Production browser verification now covers the Unicode query boundary through
the actual editor, module worker and SQLite WASM adapter. A new regression
constructs both lone surrogate halves inside the page (avoiding protocol text
replacement), verifies the original multiline source line in the error, checks
that the replacement-character record is not returned, and immediately queries
explicit U+FFFD, accented text and emoji successfully without rebuilding. The
belief count remains unchanged. The fresh website build and all 53 production
browser tests passed, including the preceding malformed-storage rebuild check.
All 108 final query tests also passed on Node 24, including the non-enumerable
structured-pattern regression. The website reference documents this recovery
contract; the specification and book need no change for this additional browser
coverage.

The matching Unicode read-boundary check reproduced a false match: an unpaired
surrogate in a query became U+FFFD during SQLite binding and matched a different
stored literal. Text parsing now rejects malformed Unicode with the original
one-based source line, including LF/CRLF filters. Structured patterns are checked
before compilation using the actual string-bearing fields, so non-enumerable
slot properties cannot evade validation. Regressions cover both surrogate halves,
text and structured entry points, contexts, unchanged history, and valid accented,
emoji, NUL and explicitly authored U+FFFD queries. All 108 query tests passed on
Node 26; the Node 24 query/website run also passed before the final non-enumerable
regression (108/34 tests). The CLI build passed. The query reference describes
the boundary; no public signature changed.

Storage Unicode review reproduced silent replacement of an unpaired UTF-16
surrogate with U+FFFD despite an empty problem list. Claim append preflight now
prepares and validates all stored claim columns, raw text, contexts, tags and
provenance before transaction IDs are allocated or observed. Tests cover both
surrogate halves across fields and metadata, whole-batch history preservation,
and successful accented/emoji/NUL round trips. The shared native/browser adapter
contract additionally verifies unchanged vocabulary and receive clock after a
bad explicit-ID replay. Store and website unit suites passed (148 and 34 tests),
and the full Node 24 integration passed all 1,663 tests across 24 summaries
with no failures, cancellations or skips.
The CLI and website builds passed. A production playground regression constructs
the malformed string inside the page, verifies the error and retained database,
then recovers with corrected input; it passed. The store reference documents
the append boundary, including lenient ingestion and the raw-SQL exclusion.

Action/hook parameter review reproduced an inconsistent execution: a getter
returned `api` during effect validation and `other` when the post-commit hook
read the caller object again. Non-enumerable own parameters were also omitted
by the hook's enumeration. Actions now capture each validated primitive value
once and pass that parameter snapshot to the hook. The real-process regression
checks both property-enumerability modes, one getter read, matching hook output
and stored effect, and absence of the alternate effect. All 43 action tests and
66 automation tests passed on Node 24.16.0; the CLI build passed too. The action
reference documents the shared parameter values. Hook timing remains strictly
after commit and public report shapes are unchanged.

Current distribution verification now imports fusion from the installed tarball
and checks equal subnormal means under unequal weights, a representable
contribution after root-weight underflow, and cancellation retaining a small
residual. The normal smoke passed for all 12 public packages, including the
unchanged public API snapshot and existing installed CLI workflows. A fresh
website build and all 52 production browser tests also passed, including the
expanded overview-alias navigation cases. The implementation guide records the
new installed numeric checks. These runs close the artifact/browser gaps after
the recent fusion and navigation fixes; hosted release evidence remains open.

Further fusion probing found an earlier loss point: dividing square-root
confidence by a very large spread could round a root weight to zero or a coarse
subnormal value before normalization. Separate 800-digit Decimal calculations
over the exact binary64 inputs established nonzero reference means of
4.94065645841e-312 and 1.9762625833649865e-19. Fusion now retains the factors and
uses a finite combined denominator for those small root weights; the original
ratio remains available if that denominator overflows. Both signs and input
orders pass against the independent references. A separate overflow-denominator
probe retained its expected 1e-310 mean. All 30 fusion tests passed on Node 24
and Node 26, and the CLI build passed. The owning reference documents the
factor-preserving boundary; public signatures remain unchanged.

Verification-workflow review replaced the local skill's unbounded HTTP startup
poll and job-number shutdown with a bounded loop, exact child PID, exit/signal
cleanup and a bounded failing curl request. The exact Markdown shell example
ran against a scratch store and returned the expected overview JSON; a missing
store failed with retained diagnostics in 0.25 seconds. The MCP example now
sends `notifications/initialized` and captures stderr rather than discarding
errors. Its exact documented initialize/list/query sequence passed against a
scratch store and returned the stored claim. The skill points rendered checks
to the maintained Playwright workflow and distinguishes them from HTTP checks.
This changes contributor verification guidance, not runtime behavior.

The follow-up fusion invariant sweep found roundoff moving an average outside
its input interval, including repeated identical means near the normal/subnormal
boundary. The posterior mean is now bounded by the smallest and largest
converted means carrying positive weight, as required by a convex weighted
average. A failing regression now checks 560 sign/scale/weight/count combinations,
each both alone and with an opposite extreme zero-confidence estimate, and
requires exact preservation of identical means. All 29 fusion tests passed on
Node 24.16.0; the CLI build also passed. The owning README documents the bound
and exclusion of zero-weight estimates. This does not change the posterior's
precision or spread calculation.

Fusion review reproduced premature underflow: averaging two identical
`Number.MIN_VALUE` means returned zero. Unequal weights could also erase their
identical mean. Fusion now scales all-subnormal means by a power of two before
weighting and uses a compensated weighted numerator before division when it is
finite, retaining normalized accumulation for overflow. Regressions cover both
signs, unequal weights, reversed order and subnormal residuals after cancellation
against ordinary-sized means. All 28 fusion tests and 107 query tests passed on
Node 24.16.0; rules/MCP consumer suites and the CLI build passed as well. The
fusion reference describes the numeric strategy. No public signature changed;
the latest packed checkpoint predates this numerical correction.

Documentation navigation now recognizes the logical overview page when the
current URL is `#/docs` or `#/docs/`. Previously, selecting its canonical
sidebar link changed the hash without changing the Docs component's slug, so
neither existing focus path ran. The expanded production regression reproduced
the failure and now passes for all three overview entry URLs at desktop and
mobile widths, including mouse, Enter and middle-click behavior. Canonical URL
navigation is preserved. A fresh site build and three affected navigation tests
passed; the website README records the aliases. The previous full browser
checkpoint predates this focused correction.

The latest normal packed smoke passed for all 12 public packages after adding
installed-CLI checks for the remaining source fixes. A DELETE over a header-only
source must return status 1 with its result-column diagnostic and no stdout,
preserving complete annotated history under prune. A packed sync with
`source:blue` and `target:green` labels must store queryable normalized endpoints.
Both checks passed, along with corrected-source recovery, the unchanged public
API snapshot and the existing installed workflows. The implementation guide
records these gates. This closes the packed-artifact gap noted in the preceding
integration checkpoint for the current source state; hosted CI and publication
remain separate evidence requirements.

The latest accumulated source state passed all 1,656 workspace tests across
24 summaries on Node 24.16.0, without failures, cancellations or skips. This
includes the sync-label correction, file-recovery regression, generated-client
consumer compilation, hook-output prefix check and source-SQL result-column
requirement. Incremental TypeScript verification reported every build output
current, and all 492 then-pending changesets passed metadata validation.
The existing 52-browser-test checkpoint remains the latest full UI run; the
packed checkpoint predates the subsequent sync-label and source-SQL fixes.
Hosted release verification remains separately open in the migration task.

SQLite source-boundary probing confirmed that read-only opening prevents a new
ATTACH target, but `VACUUM INTO` could still create a database copy and return
an empty record set. Prepared source statements now require result columns
before execution. Regressions verify no copy is created by either direct SQLite
loading or staged text-record SQL, and reject plain DELETE/UPDATE statements
while preserving valid zero-row SELECT projections. The declared-source test
also checks that a rejected DELETE under prune leaves complete annotated history
unchanged. All 119 connector tests passed on Node 24 before the added lifecycle
assertion and on Node 26 with it; the CLI build passed. The connector reference
documents the result-column requirement. This closes the observed side-effect
and false-empty-source case; it does not claim arbitrary SQL is sandboxed.

Action-hook review found a public type comment describing captured output as
trailing text, while the shared process runner retains stream prefixes up to
their byte limits. The type comment and action reference now describe stdout
followed by stderr with outer whitespace trimmed. The existing real-process
limit regression now emits distinct beginning/end markers and verifies the
exact retained 64-byte prefix, alongside its existing proof that the governed
write remains committed after the hook fails. All 42 action tests and the CLI
build passed. No runtime or output-format change was needed; the book and
specification do not repeat the incorrect trailing-output description.

Shape/client review extended the existing real TypeScript compilation fixture
with a consuming module. It verifies accepted scalar owners, literal `ms`
units and relation arrays, while expected compile errors enforce scalar/array
cardinality, wrong-unit rejection, read-only fields and collections, and unknown
property rejection. TypeScript also fails if any expected diagnostic disappears,
so permissive generated types cannot silently weaken these checks. All 98 shape
tests and the CLI build passed. The shape reference records this static consumer
coverage alongside runtime unit/cardinality checks; no generated API or runtime
behavior changed.

The synchronization file-entry regression now begins with a populated target
and explicit provenance, then alternates malformed SQLite-header files,

annotated history and leave no `cave_sync_src` attachment. Corrected previews
remain side-effect free; the final merge preserves the local claim, adds the
incoming claim, and repeats idempotently. All 52 sync tests passed. This adds
evidence for an existing recovery contract, with no runtime change. The owning
README records the file-entry boundary. The preceding label fix does not alter
the book or specification's existing basename/default-label examples.

Synchronization label review found that an attribute colon could make the
generated merge record fail parsing: `team:blue` was emitted as an unquoted
destination token. Label normalization now replaces colons with hyphens, as it
already does for literal delimiters and metadata markers. The failing regression
now passes for source, destination and combined labels across text/database
merges and dry runs; previews leave the target empty. File-derived labels have
an explicit colon regression too. All 51 sync tests passed on Node 24.16.0 and
Node 26.5.0, and the CLI build passed. The built CLI also merged a colon-bearing
source filename into `local:green` and stored the expected normalized endpoints.
The sync reference records this behavior. This source fix follows the latest
packed checkpoint and has these targeted runtime checks.

Packed distribution verification now exercises connector SQL-column rejection
through the installed CLI, covering populated and header-only sources with

The normal 12-package packed smoke passed, including the API contract without

Website navigation review reproduced a focus gap when activating the current

Unmodified repeated activations now scroll and focus the article heading using

Connector mapping review found repeated array-front insertion while moving a

The resulting source state passed all 1,654 workspace tests across 24 summaries
on Node 24.16.0, with no failures, cancellations or skips; the CLI and website

SQL source review reproduced silent loss with `SELECT id, 2 AS id`: the

The supported Node 24.16.0 runtime passed the native SQLite lossless-text check

The verification map now connects each requested outcome to its implementation

Real editor visual verification captured the isolated VS Code 1.126.0-insider

Real editor-host coverage now extends beyond initial activation: the smoke test

Real VS Code host verification is now available and locally exercised. An

Production integration checkpoint after the report/parser blank-prefix and

Declared-source ownership closure used repeated Array.shift calls to drain its
selection queue. It now uses an indexed queue seeded from distinct selected
names. A local empty-store lookup of 100,000 distinct nonexistent names took
793 ms before and 13 ms after; this isolates queue overhead rather than measuring
source discovery or I/O. A real-store regression covers source-record ownership,
cycles, shared descendants, duplicate selections, missing selections, and
unchanged transaction-annotated history. All 115 connector tests and the CLI
build passed. Connector README documents the traversal semantics; no public
signature, declaration meaning, or book output changed.

Parser comment-block review found the same repeated Array.shift cost when
trimming leading empty comment lines. Index scans now trim both edges while
preserving interior paragraphs and original expanded source. A local document
with 100,000 leading bare-semicolon lines parsed in 805 ms before and 17 ms after
the change, with identical evidence/trailing comment text. Regressions cover
10,000-line empty edges, empty-only comments, interior blank paragraphs, and
expanded-source preservation. All 82 parser tests and the CLI build passed.
Parser README records semantics and measurement limits; language behavior,
public signatures, and book outputs are unchanged.

The report benchmark now permanently exercises empty query blocks and live
blocks with both query/fragment blank prefixes at 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000
lines. Each case checks exact diagnostic location or equality with the compact
cited output outside its timing region. The complete benchmark passed 14 cases
and 70 renders. Local five-render medians at 100,000 lines were 211.5 ms for
empty blocks and 442.7 ms for the two-prefix live block. README documents the
new case schema, correctness checks, measurements, and informational scope.

Report blank-prefix review found repeated Array.shift calls in query-block and
fragment trimming. Replacing them with index scans reduced a local end-to-end
empty-block render with 100,000 generated blank lines from 1,021 ms to 238 ms,
with the same diagnostic line. A 10,000-line regression verifies empty-block
locations and identical cited output for padded versus compact fragments.
All 82 view tests passed; the final targeted regression and CLI build passed
after correcting an optional-index assertion in the test. The view README
records the implementation boundary and measurement limits. No grammar, public
signature, or executable book output changed.

Integration checkpoint after the query diagnostics/record decoder, multiline
playground, CLI recovery, and VSIX verifier changes passed all 1,648 workspace

VSIX duplicate-entry review reproduced a package with two manifest paths passing
when the final manifest was valid. Archive reading now rejects duplicate paths

Independent ZIP regressions cover duplicate manifests, JavaScript bundles, and
