archive. All 14 editor tests, typechecking/build, and the real VSIX packaging
workflow passed. The editor README documents unambiguous path requirements and
read-failure cleanup; no extension runtime or language behavior changed.

VSIX verifier review found that required executable/metadata files could be empty
and the manifest could point at an absent entry point while archive verification
still passed. The gate now requires every required file to be nonempty and the

exercise every empty required file and missing/incorrect/non-string entry points;

rendering or Marketplace publication.

Editor packaging checkpoint ran the current pnpm package workflow successfully:

Real CLI query recovery verification now covers a non-finite filter on authored
line 6 across LF/CRLF input, one multiline argument versus separate pattern/filter
arguments, and text/JSON output modes. Every rejected process exits 1 with empty

documents the error/output and source-line contract. No runtime wrapper change
was required, and existing book sessions remain valid.

Query-record decoding review reproduced boxed strings and other non-plain
bindings objects being accepted despite changing JSON shape or losing contents
when encoded. Bindings now require plain string maps, with null-prototype maps
accepted. A regression rejects boxed strings, dates, maps, and sets while
checking JSON round-trips for empty, ordinary, and null-prototype maps. All 107
query tests and the CLI build passed. The query README documents the direct
JavaScript input boundary; serialized valid records and public types are
unchanged, so no book example or API snapshot changes are needed.

The multiline playground now has a built-in example: Postmortem graph starts

Website README records the example. Source review also confirms the playground
passes the authored query text to the runtime without trimming leading lines.

Playground query review found the single-line input stripping pasted multiline
CAVE-Q, obstructing WHERE filters and comments. The editor is now a vertically
resizable five-row textarea with visible, screen-reader-linked keyboard guidance:
Enter runs without adding a newline, Shift+Enter inserts one, and IME composition

line, and recovers to a successful Wasm query without rebuilding the database.
The full 50-test browser suite passed; after increasing the default editor height,
a fresh build and nine targeted multiline, IME, and responsive-route checks
passed. Final mobile/desktop query-panel screenshots were visually inspected
with all four authored lines visible and no clipping. Website README documents

Numeric query-filter review reproduced Infinity, -Infinity, and exponent-overflow
confidence thresholds being accepted by Pattern.parse and passed toward SQL.
Confidence parsing now rejects every non-finite result with the existing

zero thresholds. All 106 query tests and the CLI build passed. The query README
states the finite-threshold contract and preserves the distinction between a
comparison threshold and the stored confidence range; public types and book

Query parser diagnostic review reproduced a malformed filter authored on line 6
being reported on line 2 because blank and comment lines were removed before

passed. The query README documents source-line counting; public types, grammar,
and existing executable book sessions are unchanged.

Packed-artifact checkpoint after the search, hook, scenario, and solver review

Website/book projection review found the homepage promising a citation behind

Integration checkpoint after the exact-arithmetic regressions and solver

Solver count-limit review reproduced oversized declaration arrays being read

All 83 solver tests, 28 Z3 backend tests, and solver typechecking passed.

Solver structural validation review reproduced sparse arrays being accepted in

All 81 solver tests, 28 Z3 backend tests, and solver typechecking passed. The

Solver provenance review reproduced a sparse evidence-ID array passing model

Exact solver arithmetic review added independent invariants for 2,080 signed

Integration checkpoint after the hook configuration/lookup fixes, fusion

CLI build pass. Store README records the query boundary; public signatures and
existing book sessions are unchanged.

Fusion review verified numeric input validation and added a physical-unit
invariance regression. Across all six permutations of three independent
estimates and each supported duration output unit, converted posterior mean,
spread and precision agree with a closed-form reference in seconds. Frozen
inputs include a leading zero-confidence estimate with an unrelated unit,
confirming it neither contributes weight nor chooses the output unit. All 27
fusion tests pass. Fusion README now accurately names the first positive-
confidence estimate as the output-unit source. No runtime, API, language or
book-example change was required.

Website review of the new report-outcome table found inline flags split across
lines, including --out and --as-of, in both mobile and desktop screenshots.
Documentation table code now stays on one line, while existing table overflow
and keyboard scrolling remain available. The new production browser regression
checks one text rectangle per flag at 390px and 1280px, no page overflow, and
keyboard scrolling when needed; it and the existing wide-table test pass.
Both resulting screenshots were visually inspected. Eight production
route/viewport checks also verified the current view, act, automate and scenario
references. The production build passes. The normal packed smoke after the
scenario and hook fixes passes across all 12 tarballs with the public API snapshot
unchanged. Website README records table-token behavior; book and language
semantics are unaffected.

Lazy hook lookup review reproduced getter execution during dry runs and an
uncaught lookup exception after action effects committed. Actions now skip
getters for dry runs/no-ops and reject nested configured hooks without invoking
getters. Lookup exceptions and invalid returned commands retain the successful
action-effect report while recording an unfired hook error. Direct automation
hooks report failed lookup steps and continue later steps; recorded events are
not silently retried. Getter exception details are omitted from diagnostics.
CLI text reporting now prioritizes hook errors even when no process fired.
All 42 action tests, 66 automation tests, 10 act-related CLI checks and the CLI
build pass. Both owning READMEs document lookup timing and failure outcomes;
public signatures and valid book examples remain unchanged.

Library hook-mapping review reproduced a null configuration throwing after
action effects committed, despite CLI file loaders already rejecting malformed
maps. Action and settlement entry points now validate mapping shape and own data
property types before store work, including unused and non-enumerable entries.
Tests verify unchanged annotated stores and corrected-config automation retry.
An existing post-commit getter test caught eager preflight property access; the
final validation uses descriptors so lazy getters retain their original lookup
timing. Their eventual return values are not validated by preflight, as both
READMEs now state. All 41 action and 65 automation tests and the CLI build pass.
Public signatures, language syntax and existing book examples are unchanged.

Hook configuration ownership review reproduced action and direct automation
hooks treating Object.prototype.constructor as a configured command in an empty
mapping. Both paths now use own-property lookup; the action nested-transaction
guard uses the same rule. Regressions cover constructor, toString and a custom
inherited command, confirm unconfigured outcomes and permitted nested actions,
then execute explicitly supplied commands under the same names. All 40 action
and 64 automation tests and the CLI build pass. Both owning READMEs document
configuration ownership; public signatures, language syntax and valid book
examples are unchanged.

Automation hook-budget review reproduced settlement consuming an event under
invalid hook configuration instead of rejecting before work. settle now validates
timeout and output-byte budgets before transactions or derivation, and passes
normalized integer milliseconds to direct hooks. Tests cover direct and action
hooks, preservation of the complete annotated store under invalid budgets with a
pending rule derivation, corrected-budget retry of the original event, and a new
event under the explicit zero-timeout setting. All 63 automation tests and the CLI
build pass. Automate README distinguishes preflight rejection from actual hook
execution failure. No public signature, language or book-example change was
needed; the separate automation boundary identified in the action review below
is now covered.

Action hook-budget review reproduced invalid configuration being detected only
after effects committed. act now validates timeout and captured-output budgets
before the transaction, returns a failed report for invalid settings, and
normalizes decimal seconds to whole milliseconds before invoking the process
runner. The regression checks unchanged annotated history for invalid timeout
and byte limits, a real hook with 1.001 seconds, and zero's existing no-timeout
behavior. All 39 action tests and the CLI build pass. Act README distinguishes
configuration rejection from actual post-commit hook failure; API signatures and
book examples are unchanged. The separate direct-hook runner in automation was
reviewed through settlement in the subsequent hook-budget entry above.

Scenario evaluator-handoff review found that documented immutable input records
were only readonly in TypeScript: JavaScript could mutate values or evidence
after the digest was computed. Bound records now deeply freeze their owned object
graph before return and evaluator handoff. Snapshot output copies only contract
fields, preventing arbitrary caller metadata from being published or frozen.
Regression coverage traverses the returned graph, rejects nested value/evidence
mutations, verifies digest/explanation integrity, checks asynchronous handoff and
preserves caller-owned snapshot metadata. All 61 scenario tests and the CLI build
pass. The full integration checkpoint passed 1,626 tests across 24 summaries,
with no failures, skips or cancellations. Scenario README documents runtime
immutability and JSON-copy behavior; a minor changeset records the stronger
runtime contract. Public signatures and existing book examples are unchanged.

Scenario numeric-definition review reproduced optional bindings accepting null
target units when no candidates existed. Numeric target units now require a
non-empty string when supplied, before database access; omission retains the
authored unit as before. The regression covers integer and number bindings with
null, numeric, Boolean, object, array and empty-string target units against an
empty store, verifying invalid-definition and the binding identifier. All 60
scenario tests and the CLI build pass. Scenario README documents the validation
and omission semantics; public signatures and valid book examples are unchanged.

Scenario input validation review reproduced unclassified TypeErrors for malformed
definition containers. Binding now checks definition/snapshot/binding/expected/
policy object shapes, the bindings array, and string query/overlay inputs before
database access, returning ScenarioInputError with invalid-definition. The
regression includes nulls, arrays in object positions, sparse bindings, primitive
entries and non-string text, using a closed store to prove the validation does
not depend on database reads. All 59 scenario tests and the CLI build pass.
Scenario README records the JavaScript/JSON input boundary. Public signatures,
valid scenario semantics and existing book/website examples are unchanged.

Packed-artifact checkpoint after the watch and report fixes passed the normal
smoke with the existing public API snapshot unchanged. The smoke now additionally
calls the installed report executable with invalid --at and --as-of options on
a static template, checking exit status 1, option diagnostics, empty stdout and
byte-for-byte preservation of an existing report. The complete updated smoke
passes against all 12 public tarballs installed without workspace symlinks,
including declaration contract checks and the existing solver, backup/recovery,
ingestion, MCP, automation, sync, HTTP and highlighter exercises. IMPLEMENTATION
records the added packed report contract. No public API or book-session change
was needed.

Shared time-boundary review added generated checks across a complete 400-year
Gregorian cycle plus years 0000, 0001, 0004, 0099, 0100, 1900 and 9999. The
checks independently derive leap years and month lengths, verify month intervals
partition each year, reject excess month days, and check ISO week-year lengths
against the Jan-1 weekday rule. Transaction tests verify year 9999 ends at year
10000, a fractional final-second boundary crosses that rollover, and the maximum
UUIDv7 remains an inclusive exact boundary, including uppercase input. All 19
time and transaction-boundary tests pass; no runtime defect surfaced. Core README
now states the four-digit calendar-year range and low-year/exclusive-end behavior.
No API, language or book-example change was needed.

Report temporal-option review reproduced a static template overwriting an
existing output and returning success with --at not-a-time. CLI report now
validates valid-time and transaction-time options with the shared Time and
QuerySql parsers before reading inputs or opening the store. Regressions cover
both options, static and query templates, unchanged output, validation before
missing input/store access, and accepted periods, timestamps and UUIDv7 bounds.
The library keeps per-query diagnostics unchanged. All eight atomic-output tests,
21 report-related CLI checks and the CLI build pass. CLI and view references
distinguish option rejection from published template diagnostics; website docs
inherit these references. Existing book time-option examples remain valid and
need no output or language-semantics change.

Report publication review confirmed that complete diagnostic Markdown is
intentionally published even when template problems produce exit status 1,
whereas write, flush or rename failure preserves the previous output. The CLI
reference already described this distinction; the owning report reference now
includes a command example and an outcome table mapping exit status, file
contents and stderr, plus a link to permissions/symlink details. All seven
atomic-output tests pass, including partial-write faults across export,
generate and report, flush/rename failures, link behavior and diagnostic report
publication. No runtime or API change was needed. Website docs import this
reference; language semantics and existing book sessions are unchanged.

HTTP viewer shutdown review verified the real CLI with a TCP client that sends
only partial request headers. A separate client still receives the page and
search results, then SIGTERM disconnects the unfinished client and exits with
143 after cleanup. A temporary mutation removing closeAllConnections reproduced
the blocked shutdown and failed the regression's five-second guard; restoring
the existing implementation passes. The CLI build passes. View README now
distinguishes CLI cancellation, which may interrupt responses in transit, from
graceful library handle closure, which retains caller ownership of the store.
This is regression coverage and a documentation clarification, with no runtime,
API, language or book-session change.

Website navigation checkpoint after the connector documentation updates rebuilt
the production site and passed all 47 browser tests. The rendered-document crawl
checks section-link targets across every bundled page; separate interactions
cover direct fragment loads, reload and Back, repeated section clicks, native
middle-click, malformed fragments, filter recovery and active-entry visibility.
The suite also checks responsive routes, keyboard scrolling, lazy-download
recovery, local-viewer searches, and the playground's production worker/WASM
assets. Visual inspection of the 320px documentation overview confirmed readable
content and navigation with a visible heading focus indicator. No new defect was
found in this pass; existing website contracts and book content need no edit.
These browser checks complement the 1,620-test workspace checkpoint below and
do not establish completion of the remaining whole-system review scope.

Direct watcher shutdown review reproduced late file callbacks scheduling work
after the command had returned and closed its store. Direct watches now ignore
callbacks after abort, stop queued follow-up passes, and omit the watching message
when startup was cancelled. The existing lifecycle regression now checks that
shutdown cancels a pending debounce callback and late source/map callbacks cannot
replace it. Connect README clarifies the actual cleanup order: subscriptions
close, the active pass settles, then the store closes. No API or language change
requires book or website copy updates. The integrated checkpoint after the recent
watch fixes passed all 1,620 tests across 24 summaries with no failures, skips or
cancellations; the CLI build and whitespace check also pass.

Declared watcher refresh failure review reproduced a scheduled callback rejecting
when registration of a newly discovered source failed. The rejection left the
running flag set, preventing later saves from starting another pass. Refresh
errors now have their own diagnostic boundary, preserving existing subscriptions
and allowing the next save to retry. The redundant refresh after the initial pass
was removed so initial discovery uses that same recovery boundary. Initial-set
registration failures still exit through startup cleanup. The regression covers
discovery during startup and after a later parent edit, successful registration
on retry, persisted child edits and retractions, and shutdown cleanup. All 114
connector tests and the CLI build pass. Connect README records this distinction;
public APIs, language semantics, website copy and book examples need no changes.

Declared watcher lifecycle review reproduced obsolete subscriptions remaining
open after a followed source moved its child declaration. Refresh now computes
the current target set, registers replacements, and closes targets no longer
needed. Closed subscriptions ignore late callbacks. The regression moves a
child source, verifies its shared mapping remains watched, then removes the
declaration and verifies only the parent subscription remains. All 113 connector
tests pass. Connect README documents this lifecycle; public types, language
semantics and book examples are unaffected.

Connector watch startup review reproduced a leaked first watcher when the
second registration failed. Both direct target registration and declared watcher
refresh happened before their cleanup try/finally. They now register inside the
existing cleanup scope, retaining each successfully created handle immediately.
The regression injects a second-registration failure in both modes, verifies the
first handle closes, preserves the diagnostic and checks the full store export
is unchanged because no initial pass ran. All 112 connector tests and the CLI
build pass. Connect README records this startup ownership boundary; syntax and
book examples are unaffected.

Structured-source cancellation now covers direct and declared loads. The direct
regression first reproduced returned URL records committing after abort; the
companion declared regression reproduced the same gap through preparation and
discovery. Source.Options.signal combines caller abort with timeout and preserves
the reason; Declared.prepare accepts an optional fourth signal argument and
DiscoverOptions carries it through snapshot discovery. Callers check cancellation
before applying or publishing prepared data. Ordinary declared passes preserve
sources committed earlier, while dry/query discovery discards its private snapshot
and cancelled results. Watch shutdown suppresses queued work and closes watchers.
Tests cover JSON and .cave URLs across run/dry/query/watch, unchanged populated
stores under --force --prune, stopped nested discovery, native pending-body abort
for direct/declared loads, snapshot disposal, pre-aborted allocation avoidance,
and pending debounce cleanup. All 111 connector tests pass. The integrated
checkpoint passed 1,617 tests across 24 summaries with no failures/skips; the
final dry-output guard and watch assertions also pass the targeted suite and final
normal packed smoke. API review is limited to optional signal parameters and
their declaration hashes. README and IMPLEMENTATION document ownership and
cancellation guarantees. The completed cancellation task and TODO entry are
removed; the overall system review and hosted release verification remain active.

Preview asset review reproduced another server-termination path: an asset
removed before statSync could throw outside request handling, and stream errors
had no listener. The server now catches metadata failures, opens the stream
before sending 200 headers, maps missing assets to 404 and other pre-stream
failures to 500, and terminates only the affected response for later read errors.
Response closure destroys the file stream. Subprocess fault injection covers
metadata removal, denied stream opening and partial-response read failure,
checking subsequent requests still succeed. All 33 website unit tests, the site
build and the real worker/WASM browser smoke pass. Website README records this
preview-infrastructure behavior; deployed hosting is outside this change.

Malformed-request review confirmed the local viewer already handles URL parsing
failures, but found uncaught URL/percent decoding in the separate production
website test server. A real subprocess request for /cave/% reproduced connection
reset and server termination. The preview server now answers 400 for malformed
URLs/encoded paths and survives subsequent requests. It reports its actual bound
port so the regression can use PORT=0 instead of reserving a fixed port. All 32
website unit tests, the website build and the targeted real worker/WASM browser
smoke pass. Website README records the test-server contract. This fixes local/CI
preview infrastructure; it does not claim to change deployed hosting behavior.

The combined ingestion/evaluation checkpoint passes 1,611 tests across all 24
workspace summaries, with zero failures/skips. This includes embedded snapshots,
path-drift rejection, setup/plan cleanup, early timeout validation, partial-output
failure distinctions, the judge syntax index and executable book sessions.
A fresh website build and all 47 website/local-view browser tests pass. The new
evaluation benchmark section and expanded ingestion retry/timeout section were
also opened directly at 390 px, checked for page overflow, and visually inspected;
section navigation and rendered content are intact. The preceding packed smoke
already covers the same runtime changes and passes. This integrated evidence
supplements subsystem regressions; the remaining system scope and hosted release
verification stay active.

The judge-parser scaling task is implemented. The original malformed nested
fixture recovered the right answer but repeatedly parsed overlapping invalid
spans, taking 13.1/41.8/146.4/538.1 ms at about 2/4/8/16 KB. A reverse JSON syntax
index now shares value and comma-separated suffix boundaries in linear work,
then permits native decoding only for valid candidate spans. Existing bracket
recovery and last-array selection remain unchanged; consumed valid arrays keep
total decoding work linear. The index uses memory proportional to input length.
A 20,000-case differential recovery probe matched the previous parser. New tests
compare nested and damaged arrays with native JSON syntax, handle 20,000-level
valid/malformed nesting without recursion, and count decoded bytes to reject
repeated overlapping attempts. All 61 evaluation tests, the CLI build and packed
smoke pass without an API snapshot change. Isolated benchmark medians are now
0.65/0.36/1.09/1.67 ms; the README preserves both measurements and warm-up/memory
limits. The completed task and TODO entry are removed. This implements the
measured enhancement without truncation, attempt limits or relaxed scoring.

Evaluation review found an interaction with source-drift rejection: it inferred
scoreable partial stdout from any rejected batch with writes and problems. A
path-reading MCP agent could write correct claims, alter its source, and still
receive a successful score despite the rejected ingestion batch. The regression
reproduced that success before the fix. Ingestion now marks accepted partial
stdout explicitly with optional BatchReport.partial; evaluation uses that flag
and preserves source diagnostics in failed-run notes. Existing valid-lines-plus-
parse-errors scoring still passes. All 57 ingestion and 59 evaluation tests and
the CLI build pass. The packed smoke passes after reviewing the API snapshot:
only optional partial, the preceding Files.select embed option, and associated
declaration hashes changed. Ingest/eval READMEs record the failure distinction;
book scoring examples and query semantics remain unchanged.

Timeout review found that ingestion accepted positive finite CLI durations
outside the process runner's whole-millisecond timer range, rejecting them only
after setup. Direct ingestion options lacked matching validation. A shared
seconds conversion now validates CLI options before store opening and API options
before staging/source reads, with the supported 1..2147483647 millisecond range.
It also tolerates only floating-point conversion noise: a direct probe confirmed
1.001 * 1000 became 1000.9999999999999 and the old process call rejected it.
The new real shell regression succeeds at 1.001 seconds. Tests reject zero,
negative, non-finite, submillisecond and over-limit ingestion values and accept
valid boundary/decimal inputs; the lower-level shell helper retains exact-zero
no-timeout compatibility. All 57 ingestion and 58 evaluation tests and the CLI
build pass. The README and option comment document the range and distinguish
shell deadlines from function-agent cancellation. Initial test invocation of a
negative CLI value used ambiguous separate arguments; the corrected test uses
--timeout=-1, matching Node argument syntax. No book examples change.

Reviewing command-side ingestion planning found that --plan allocated a
persistent MCP configuration before knowing whether it had any batches or could
build the first prompt. An empty plan reproduced the unused-directory leak.
Configuration creation now occurs lazily after the first prompt is ready.
The regression covers empty selection, missing instruction input, and a valid
two-batch plan that retains one shared configuration for its external driver,
without creating the target database. All 55 ingestion tests and the CLI build
pass. The README records lazy allocation and external-driver cleanup ownership;
valid emitted plan fields and book examples remain unchanged.

Ingestion setup review reproduced an owned temporary-directory leak when
writeMcpConfig failed writing its configuration. The run also allocated that
configuration before creating the prompt directory and entering cleanup, leaving
an additional setup gap. The helper now cleans only directories it allocated on
failure. Runs put configuration and prompts in one owned directory and create
the configuration inside its cleanup scope. Fault-injection coverage fails the
configuration write through the standalone helper and run, verifies owned paths
are removed, and preserves a caller-supplied directory. The regression failed
before the fix; all 54 ingestion tests and the CLI build now pass. Ingest README
records ownership after failure and successful standalone use. This internal
cleanup correction does not change CLI syntax, prompts or book examples.

The companion path-based ingestion review reproduced stale digest acceptance
when an agent changed or removed its input during execution. Non-embedded local
batches now check their selected digests before and after an agent call. Observed
changes/read failures reject the batch before stdout insertion or digest recording;
pre-call failures skip that paid call. Strict staging is discarded on failure,
while lenient mode retains earlier accepted work and direct agent writes and
continues later batches. Regressions cover replacement/removal across both
policies and stdout/MCP modes, and an earlier batch changing a later input checks
call avoidance, source statuses and continuation. All 53 ingestion tests and the
CLI build pass. Ingest README and IMPLEMENTATION document observed-drift checks,
retry eligibility, write ownership and their distinction from embedded snapshots.
The checks do not claim to prove an external agent's reads or detect edits that
are reverted between observations. Book extraction/atomicity guidance remains
accurate; no syntax or example-output change is introduced.

Local embedded ingestion had a selection/prompt race: selection hashed each
file, but a later batch reread it from disk. Edits during earlier agent calls
could therefore produce claims from replacement text under the original digest.
A two-batch regression failed before the fix. Embedded selection now retains the
exact text used for hashing and prompt construction consumes that snapshot;
non-embedded selection retains its existing path-based behavior. Strict and
lenient regressions replace the second file during the first batch, check the
second prompt still contains the original text, verify its recorded digest,
and confirm only the changed file is selected on the next run. All 51 ingestion
tests pass and the CLI build passes. Ingest README, selection API comments and
IMPLEMENTATION preserve this boundary, including lazy store context across
batches. The book's embedding and incremental-ingestion descriptions remain
accurate; no syntax, CLI output or extraction rules change in this correction.

An integrated checkpoint after schema/index validation, historical backup
recovery, older-source sync validation and playground context changes passes
all 1,601 tests across 24 workspace summaries, with zero failures or skips.
The initial packed smoke also passed. Its installed-CLI snapshot coverage was
then expanded to a version-1 fixture: independent SHA-256 verification, schema-v1
reporting, byte-identical restore, read-only export's migration refusal, empty-add
migration, unchanged full annotated history, and retained backup checksum/version.
The first expanded run exposed an incorrect test assumption that export migrates;
the check now explicitly asserts its read-only boundary before using add. The
final expanded smoke passes all 12 packed public artifacts and the reviewed API
snapshot without updating that snapshot. IMPLEMENTATION preserves the installed
recovery contract and a dedicated changeset records the added release coverage.
This checkpoint supplements the preceding 47-test browser run; it does not close
the remaining whole-system review or hosted release verification.

Sync's schema upgrade review found that structural validation applied only to
sources equal to the current version. Moving currentVersion to 2 unintentionally
removed that protection from version-1 sources: a missing provenance table was
accepted as legacy input and explicit dimensions could be replaced by inference.
A regression failed before the fix. Every supported versioned source now passes
Schema.validate for its recorded version; unversioned legacy behavior remains
covered separately. The regression checks real/dry rejection, unchanged target,
released attachment, repair/retry with exact provenance and unchanged source
version. All 51 sync tests and the CLI build pass. Sync README and the normative
schema rules now distinguish supported older schemas from unversioned legacy
sources. The book's existing identity and compatibility descriptions remain
accurate; no command output or book source change is needed for this correction.

The playground now keeps the submitted query visible alongside its valid-time
context in both results and query errors. Previously only successful results
identified the anchor, so changing query text during execution made the result
appear to answer the edited input. A delayed-worker browser regression failed
before the change and now verifies that editing both fields cannot relabel the
submitted operation, the next query uses the edits, and errors retain their
original query/date while controls recover. The website README records this
behavior. The production website build and all 47 combined website/local-view
browser tests pass. A 390 px screenshot of the delayed error result was inspected
for wrapping and layout. This changes only the playground presentation; query
semantics and book command output remain unchanged.

Reviewing recovery after the schema upgrade exposed a compatibility regression:
verifyBackup required the current schema exactly, so valid version-1 snapshots
could no longer be verified or restored. A regression failed with the exact
format rejection before the fix. Verification now accepts recorded schema
versions 1 through the current version and validates their version-specific
structure without migration. Restore still verifies both copies and publishes
identical bytes; a subsequent writable open upgrades only the restored copy.
Tests check SHA-256, byte equality, retained backup immutability, read-only
migration refusal, and unchanged provenance/qualifier export after writable
migration. Version 0, future schemas and malformed version-1 structures remain
rejected without replacing the destination. A CLI regression verifies schema-v1
reporting and exact restore with the reported digest. All 145 store and 132 CLI
tests pass, including executable book sessions; CLI and website builds pass.
Store/CLI READMEs, the specification, implementation guide and book now explain
the recovery boundary. The PDF was rebuilt with Typst 0.15.0 and page 30 rendered
and inspected. The historical-snapshot changeset records the added compatibility.

A follow-up schema-boundary review found that a same-named transaction index
with NOCASE collation passed validation. EXPLAIN showed it lost the `(tx<?)`
range search, despite still appearing as the selected covering index. A native
regression failed before the fix. Validation now inspects index key metadata
and requires binary collation, while accepting equivalent case spelling and
descending order. Shared native/WASM tests reject mismatched collation, partial,
wrong-table, expression and composite definitions through both current-schema
checks and migration, preserving exports and version 1 after failure and
allowing repair/retry. Query-plan assertions now require the bounded range,
not just the index name. An attached-source sync regression verifies rejection
leaves the target unchanged, detaches the source, and permits repaired retry.
All 143 store, 31 website/WASM and 50 sync tests pass. Store README and the
normative schema specification record the collation requirement; the public
schema version and API are unchanged. The book's migration description remains
accurate and needs no source or PDF change for this validation correction.

Schema version 2 now installs `idx_cave_tx ON cave_claim(tx)` through an
atomic migration, preserving the historical version-1 migration and validation
contract. Validation checks the new index's table, column and full coverage.
Native and WASM regressions verify interrupted migration rollback, rejected
incompatible indexes, retry, unchanged annotated claims/provenance/lineage,
and indexed global/bounded head-query plans. Closed-file backup recovery and
read-only/no-migrate rejection pass; an additional sync regression confirms a
version-1 source merges into version 2 without upgrading the source.
All 142 native store and 30 WASM tests pass. The workspace checkpoint passed
1,593 tests across 24 summaries; the subsequently added source-compatibility
test brings the targeted sync suite to 49 passing tests, with its build passing.
The final packed smoke test and website build pass. The packed API snapshot
changes only the schema version constant and its declaration hash. Store,
specification, implementation and book documentation now describe version 2;
the PDF was rebuilt with the pinned compiler and affected pages inspected.
An isolated production-schema benchmark on Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 macOS
arm64 measured median 0.079 ms for 100 head reads and 10.83 ms for 100 single-row
appends on five fresh 10,000-row fixtures; counts and integrity checks pass.
The store README retains the original index trial, storage overhead, production
measurements and workload limits. The completed index task and TODO entry are
removed. This closes that enhancement, not the broader system review.

Profiling a quiet 1,000-rule run attributed 253 ms of 338 ms to 1,000 repeated
`SELECT MAX(tx)` reads. The engine captured this boundary before its skip test,
although skipped rules never used it. Moving the read immediately after that
test preserves a fresh pre-evaluation boundary for every firing rule and avoids
those scans for quiet rules. A regression failed before the move and now checks
zero quiet head reads, unchanged export, and a real boundary read plus corrected
derived value after a premise changes. Isolated benchmark medians improved from
11.4/102.6/333.2 ms to 8.3/39.0/79.5 ms at 100/500/1,000 rules, all with zero
writes; the 1,000-rule case is about 4.2 times faster. All 146 rule/action/
automation tests, CLI and website builds, changeset metadata and diff checks
pass. The rules README retains the before/after table and profile rationale.
This does not introduce a transaction-head cache or alter the book's incremental
derivation contract, so no book rebuild is needed.

The new many-rule quiet-run benchmark validates complete initial derivation,
then five quiet runs at 100, 500 and 1,000 rules with unchanged full annotated
exports and zero writes. An isolated Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 macOS arm64 run
measured medians of 11.4, 102.6 and 333.2 ms. Its separate 1,000-policy-hash
phase measured 0.95 ms, so an additional policy-hash cache would target little
of the measured quiet-run cost. No production optimization was made on that
evidence. The root bench:rule-watermarks command and rules README preserve the
fixture, correctness checks, measurements and rejected optimization rationale.
Further profiling should locate the remaining rule-discovery/database cost;
the isolated hash measurement does not establish that bottleneck by itself.

The combined browser suite now passes all 47 tests against a fresh website
build (1.1 minutes). This includes the three live local-viewer tests for narrow
layouts, repeated searches after appends and preserved pending-search drafts,
alongside the 44 production-site tests. CI and Pages install the full workspace;
the local fixtures import workspace TypeScript entry points and do not require
a private-package dist build. The two workflow step names now describe both
the website and local viewer. This is a local browser result and configuration
review, not a claim that a hosted CI or Pages run has executed these changes.
Changeset metadata and diff checks pass. The broader system and hosted release
review remains open.

Automation's firing watermark intentionally differs from a rule's evaluation
fingerprint. An integration regression now settles direct event triggers and
derived facts together, enables aliases, appends a new alias-matched event, and
then restores exact matching. Derived facts expand and retract with the policy,
but trigger rows already behind the firing watermark do not replay. The new
event invokes its completion callback exactly once, and restoring defaults adds
no calls. This verifies that the rule-policy fix does not rewind automation's
event log, including older rows newly matched by aliases. All 62 automation
tests, the CLI build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. The automation
README records this distinction; existing normative event semantics and book
examples remain accurate without generated changes.

Rule watermarks did not include evaluation settings: a settled rule could skip
when alias matching was enabled or its confidence floor lowered, and could keep
unsupported conclusions when defaults were restored. Both option-change
regressions failed before the fix. The persisted derive-vocabulary companion now
uses a versioned fingerprint of registry content plus effective aliases/minConf.
Changes re-evaluate support automatically; old registry-only fingerprints cause
one conservative re-evaluation. The existing mark and complete-run/dry-run
transaction semantics remain intact. Tests cover enabling aliases, dry-run
rollback, reopening and disabling aliases, lowering and restoring the confidence
floor, and quiet repeats. All 45 rule tests and 99 action/automation tests pass;
the full workspace run passes 1588 tests across 24 package summaries with no
failures, skips or cancellations. CLI and website builds, changeset metadata
and diff checks pass. Rules README, normative specification and implementation
guide describe the behavior. The book was rebuilt with pinned Typst 0.15.0;
pages 59–60 were rendered and visually inspected with clean layout. This fixes
evaluation-policy invalidation without adding a new bookkeeping claim series.

The scenario binder also reads SQLite data_version and total_changes, but uses
them only to detect inconsistent materialization within one binding; it retains
no projection cache. Applying the viewer's cache bypass there is unnecessary.
A new regression binds staged values inside an outer transaction, binds again
after a nested savepoint rollback, then again after the outer rollback. Fresh
records exactly match the restored values, evidence and digest at each boundary,
while already returned records retain the staged data they captured. All 58
scenario tests, the scenario build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass.
The scenario README documents this distinction and clarifies that the package
closes its own transaction scope, not an outer transaction owned by its caller.
This pass adds coverage and corrects the lifecycle description; it does not
change binding or solver semantics.

Sensitivity projection caching used SQLite data_version and total_changes as
its revision. A view built after an uncommitted append remained cached after
rollback because total_changes does not rewind; the new row-rollback regression
reproduced that stale result. Scoped reads now use disposable projections during
transactions, including nested savepoints, and when adapter transaction-state
inspection is unavailable. They close after the synchronous callback even if
it throws. Committed native reads retain the existing cache and reuse checks.
Additional regressions cover an edge-only savepoint rollback restoring verb
declaration eligibility, and the no-inspection cleanup path. All 80 view tests,
the CLI build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. View README and the
implementation guide describe why transactional reads bypass the cache and why
temporary projections are excluded from cache statistics. No public query or
language semantics change; this fixes the view's reflection of actual store
state. The earlier full integration checkpoint precedes this cache fix.

The local viewer's search renderer assigned the submitted query to the input
when its response arrived, overwriting a new draft typed during the request.
Search navigation now fills the input before starting the request, and result
rendering leaves it untouched. A browser regression holds the search response,
types a new draft, releases the response, and verifies that the draft and focus
survive while the results and heading still describe the submitted search.
It failed before the change. All three local-view browser tests, all 77 view
tests, the CLI build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. View and website
READMEs record the timing contract and coverage. The change does not affect
query evaluation, URL identity or the existing stale-navigation guard.

Repeated searches in the local viewer previously left stale results after a
store append: assigning the current fragment does not emit hashchange. The
search handler now calls the ordinary guarded route loader when its destination
already equals the current fragment. A live browser regression first finds one
claim, appends another matching claim, submits the same search and verifies two
results with the URL and input focus retained; it failed before the fix and now
passes. Unit coverage also confirms that composition and blank input do not
trigger refreshes. Both local-view browser tests, all 77 view tests, the CLI
build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. View and website READMEs record
the interaction and coverage. The HTTP API and search semantics are unchanged;
the fix refreshes the existing query through the same read-only route.

The local HTTP viewer overflowed at 320 px because its search input's automatic
minimum width pushed the aliases control past the viewport. The input now has
an explicit zero minimum width, and page text can wrap long unbroken content.
A new browser regression starts a real ephemeral view server and checks both
the dashboard and entity page at 320 and 390 px with long entity and topic names,
a long quoted value and a long store label. It failed before the fix and now
passes with no page-wide overflow and visible search/alias controls. The mobile
entity screenshot was inspected: names, values, topic chips and the footer wrap
within the page, and history links remain visible. All 77 view tests and the CLI
build pass, as do changeset metadata and diff checks. View and website READMEs
describe the layout and browser fixture coverage. This is one additional browser
test beyond the prior 44-test full-site checkpoint; the full browser suite was
not rerun for this local-view-only CSS change.

The local HTTP viewer's loading and error text previously changed without
accessible status semantics. Its main view now exposes aria-busy, a separate
persistent status region announces loading and completion outside that busy
subtree, and current request or fragment errors render as alerts. The existing
navigation regression now verifies status alongside content, including an old
response completing while the latest request is still pending; it failed before
the change and passes now. A Chromium check against a live ephemeral server
held the overview request, observed loading and completion through the status
role, aborted an entity request, checked its alert and cleared busy state, and
confirmed later HTTP requests still succeed. This verifies browser semantics,
not speech output from a particular screen reader. All 77 view tests, view and
CLI builds, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. The view README records the
behavior; book language and command examples are unchanged. Existing malformed
HTTP URL and interrupted-response coverage was reviewed and remains sufficient
for those specific server boundaries.

The integration checkpoint after atomic text-output handling and sync failure
coverage passes all 1582 workspace tests across 24 package summaries, with no
failures, skips or cancellations. This includes CLI command behavior, the
recorded book sessions, both Git-driver regressions and the new output/sync
failure tests. The workspace build passes. Packing and installing all 12 public
packages into an isolated project also passes the complete smoke script,
including the installed CLI's export/import and annotated branching workflows,
API contract, optional solver assets, MCP, HTTP serving and highlighting.
All 398 pending changesets at the start of the checkpoint validate; its own
additional evidence changeset validates separately. This pass did not rerun
browser tests: the latest full browser result remains the earlier 44-test
checkpoint, while the website build passed after the output-documentation
changes. These checks strengthen integration evidence without closing the
remaining system review or hosted release verification.

Report and typed-client output shared the export path's partial-write risk:
fault injection left existing files containing only `# S` and `// ` respectively.
All three text-output commands now use the shared atomic-output helper, with
the same staging, flush, replacement, permissions and link behavior. Their
partial-write regressions pass. A separate report regression verifies that
template problems still publish complete diagnostic Markdown and return the
same nonzero status and diagnostics as stdout rendering; filesystem failure
handling does not suppress useful report output. The 97-test CLI/output group
and subsequent 16-test output/documentation group pass, along with the CLI
build, website build, changeset metadata and diff checks. CLI help and README
describe the shared behavior. Book command sessions and generated output remain
unchanged, so the book needs no rebuild for this implementation change.

Text export previously wrote directly over an existing destination. A partial
write fault reproduced truncation to the first three bytes of the new export.
`export --out` now writes and flushes a temporary file beside the destination
before renaming it into place. The helper preserves existing permission bits,
follows valid symlinks, refuses dangling links and non-regular files, and leaves
hard-link aliases pointing at the old file. It cleans up staging files on write,
flush and rename failures. Four export regressions exercise those boundaries;
the 97-test CLI/export/Git-driver group passes, as do the subsequent 13-test
export/documentation check, CLI build, website build, changeset metadata and
diff checks. CLI help and README document the replacement contract, directory
permission requirement, and distinction from shell redirection and power-loss
durability; the sync README records the stronger final-output protection in
its merge driver. Existing book export sessions retain their commands and
output, so this change does not alter the generated book. The broader review
of other artifact-output commands remains separate from this export fix.

Sync's late failure boundary now has four regressions covering database and
annotated-text sources, each with normal and dry-run execution. A SQLite trigger
rejects only the merge-record insert, after imported rows, lineage, explicit
provenance and reverse vocabulary have been staged. The target's annotated
export, provenance count and registry identity remain unchanged; database sync
leaves no source attachment or temporary merge table. Removing the trigger lets
the same target merge all four claims and their edge, retain exact explicit
provenance, activate the inverse spelling and then repeat without new claims.
The implementation already satisfies this boundary; this pass adds durable
regressions and documents the transaction contract in the sync README. All 48
sync tests and the sync build (including test typechecking) pass, as do changeset
metadata and diff checks. The book's existing atomic merge description remains
accurate and requires no generated artifact change. Normal transaction rollback
does not rewind the shared UUID generator, as the store README already states;
this review does not reinterpret that deliberate behavior as a defect.

The Git union driver now also has a local repository integration regression.
It creates two divergent branches from an annotated base, installs the exact
README configuration and attributes, and lets Git invoke the real CLI driver.
Valid inputs produce a two-parent merge commit with no conflict stages and
exactly the union of both branches' claim identities. Invalid incoming text
returns failure, preserves our file, and retains all three unresolved index
stages. Repository paths, the knowledge filename and TMPDIR contain spaces;
both paths remove temporary databases. Both driver tests, the CLI build
(including test typechecking), changeset metadata and diff checks pass. These fixtures
create commits only in disposable local repositories with no remotes and
isolated Git configuration; they do not exercise hosting or modify the working
repository's Git configuration. The sync README records the coverage.

The documented Git union driver failed through the real CLI when temporary or
input paths contained spaces, and left its temporary database behind after an
input sync failed. Both the sync README and normative branching instructions
now quote the complete Git configuration value and shell paths, and install an
exit cleanup trap. The standalone manual-union example also stops on failure
and cleans up. A regression reads both live configuration snippets through
Git's own parser, invokes their commands with the real CLI, verifies the exact
annotated union, and checks that invalid incoming text leaves our input
unchanged, returns failure, and removes temporary files. This is configuration
and command execution coverage, not a hosted Git merge trial. The regression
failed before the fix; all 54 sync, CLI documentation and driver tests now pass,
as do the website build, changeset metadata and diff checks. The book describes
the union workflow without this shell implementation and needs no source or
PDF change. Shared scrolling components were also inspected in this pass;
their current observers cover the relevant rendered content widths, with no
additional production change warranted from that inspection.

The homepage's overflowing code now uses the same named keyboard scroll region
as documentation examples. Its previous plain pre element failed the new
production browser regression. The shared focus outline applies to both
locations, and homepage lines expose their intrinsic width so the resize
observer can detect font or highlighting changes. The regression checks arrow-key
scrolling at 390 px, a visible focus outline, no page-wide overflow, and removal
of the region label and tab stop when the example fits at 1440 px. All 44
production browser tests pass against a fresh website build, including the
decorative-line-number regression from the previous pass. The mobile screenshot
was inspected: the outline remains inside the card and the example scrolls
within it. Website README, changeset metadata and diff checks are current. This
website-only change does not alter language behavior or require a book rebuild.

The homepage code example's decorative line numbers were exposed as source
text in the browser accessibility snapshot. CaveCode now marks only the number
elements aria-hidden, retaining their visual display. A production browser
regression failed before the change and now verifies all nine number elements
remain in the visual example, the first remains visible, and the accessibility
snapshot omits numbering while retaining verbs, entity names and the version
literal. Website build, the focused browser regression, changeset metadata and
diff checks pass. The website README records the behavior. The prior 42-test
browser checkpoint remains separate from this focused check of the new change.

The current integration checkpoint after the action-gate optimization and
follow-up contract coverage passes 1569 workspace tests across 24 package
summaries, including the recorded book sessions, with no failures, skips or
cancellations. All 42 production browser tests also pass (1.1 minutes), including
runtime recovery, metadata-safe result display, documentation links and
keyboard access. The workspace build passes. All 390 pending changesets present
at the start of this checkpoint validate against the current fixed-group and
ownership rules, and git diff --check passes. This refreshes integration
evidence after the recent runtime changes; it does not stand in for hosted
release verification or close the remaining system-review scope.

The pinned Changesets action runVersion source was exercised against a
copied CAVE workspace using the installed CLI version command and real
synchronizer. A temporary local Git repository supplied the versioning context;
branch preparation, pushing and PR creation were captured by local doubles,
with network fetches guarded during execution. The action generated the
expected release branch/title and a 3,325-character summary containing public
core, private act/automate, and extension entries at fixture version 0.35.1.
Alignment changelog text appeared and the unchanged website was excluded.
The temporary repository had no remote and all source/dependency/fixture files
were removed. This verifies the previously fragile private-package changelog
path through upstream code. Grammar regeneration, lockfile refresh, bundled
entrypoint execution and hosted GitHub behavior remain outside this trial;
no real checkout version, remote branch or PR was changed. Dependency
maintenance and the release task record those evidence boundaries.

The publication-output bridge was exercised through runPublish from the exact
Changesets action 2.1.1 commit, rather than only a locally mirrored parser.
The temporary workspace installed source dependencies with lifecycle scripts
disabled and invoked CAVE's release-output helper. Full and partial modes
returned the expected package/version arrays and exit 0; empty recovery returned
published=false/exit 0; a failing custom script returned published=false/exit 1
and the expected missing-output warning. Guarded GitHub methods and execution
fetches were never called, and tag pushing/release creation were disabled. The
scratch source, dependencies, workspaces and output files were removed. Dependency
maintenance and the release task now distinguish this verified source interface
from the still-unverified bundled entrypoint and hosted workflow. No package,
tag or external repository mutation was performed.

The release backlog now distinguishes local implementation from hosted
verification. TODO.md points to verification of the migrated workflow, and the
release task retains only remaining action/PR/publication evidence requirements.
Lasting CLI/action compatibility notes and pinned upstream references moved to
DEPENDENCY-MAINTENANCE.md instead of remaining embedded in a mostly completed
migration checklist. The task no longer presents the old audited commit as the
current implementation. Website build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass;
no hosted workflow or publication result is inferred from those local checks.

Action metadata idempotence was checked against normative section 25.2's
explicit key/value/confidence comparison. A new regression changes only an
action effect's tag, verifies an unchanged execution retains the original row
and lineage without writes, then changes the value and verifies the new version
carries the updated tag while old lineage survives. All 38 action tests pass.
The action README now explains this deliberate metadata boundary and that an
effect report's line describes the instantiated template, even when the stored
row was retained. No runtime semantics were changed; the specification and book
already state the governing idempotence criteria.

The live-documentation follow-up aligned ARCHITECTURE.md, the shape README
and normative section 25.3 with deferred action shape snapshots. Changed
effects retain a complete before/after comparison; entirely unchanged actions
retain declaration/argument/premise validation without shape evaluation. A
new regression verifies the malformed-declaration boundary: a prior effect can
return unchanged without writes, but a new effect still fails constraint
validation and leaves both claims and lineage unchanged. All 37 action tests
pass. The book's conditional description (reject executions introducing new
violations) remains accurate and required no source or PDF change.

The no-op action follow-up verifies that prior effects do not grant permission
to execute again after a premise loses its inverse mapping. A new regression
first executes the action, then qualifies the REVERSE declaration through the
same connection or a peer writer. Both normal and dry-run repeats reject the
now-unsatisfied premise and append nothing; the previous effect row and its
lineage remain intact. All 36 action tests pass. The action README records this
boundary. The explicit registry replay at action entry was retained: the store
API also accepts caller-owned pre-canonicalized registry snapshots, so changing
that refresh deserves a separate contract review rather than assuming every
cache is authoritative. This pass adds coverage for the optimization's semantic
boundary and does not claim a further runtime speedup.

Idempotent actions no longer take two full shape snapshots. The baseline is
now deferred until immediately before the first changed effect; entirely
unchanged executions retain declaration, parameter and premise checks but do
not enter shape evaluation. A regression first observed two snapshots for an
unchanged execution; it now verifies zero for normal and dry-run no-ops, two
for actual writes, and full gate rejection/rollback when an unchanged prefix
is followed by a changed effect that introduces a violation. Action, shape and
automation tests pass (35/98/61), and the workspace build passes. The action
README records the lazy baseline contract. The automation benchmark now accepts
--repeat and checks idempotent executions explicitly. An isolated --shapes
--repeat run passed all assertions at 100/500/1,000 events; 1,000 repeated
actions took 513.1 ms with zero writes while the initial gated settle took
11.61 seconds. This improves no-op execution; writes still receive full
before/after shape evaluation. The automate README records that distinction.

The shape-gate performance review added a repeatable fact-selection diagnostic
at pnpm bench:shape-query. It compares the existing correlated current-row
lookup with grouped selection restricted to the same stable verb/attribute
fields. Fixtures include unrelated rows and final retractions; ordered
projections and expected row counts agree before timing. Isolated median
20-read samples (Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3, macOS arm64) were 37.3 versus
49.4 ms at 1,000 entities / one version, 129.7 versus 113.0 ms at 1,000 / ten,
and 107.0 versus 73.4 ms at 100 / one hundred. The grouped alternative improves
these deep histories but regresses shallow history, so production SQL remains
unchanged. The shape README records the command, measurements and rejected
blanket replacement. This narrows the performance investigation; it does not
claim that repeated full gate evaluation has been eliminated.

The vocabulary-watermark follow-up ran the existing automation benchmark in
isolation, first without shapes and then with populated shape gates, at 100,
500 and 1,000 events. All exact entity, action, owner, final-shape and quiet-write
assertions pass. At 1,000 events the no-shape run measured 787.7 ms active /
11.4 ms quiet; the shaped run measured 12292.8 ms active / 12.8 ms quiet. Every
active run settled in two passes and every quiet cycle fired no action and
appended no row. The one-rule fixture adds one initial vocabulary bookkeeping
row. The automate README now records these results and distinguishes the
older large-run table from the newer implementation. These are individual
local observations, not a claim of a new scaling order; repeated populated
shape gates remain the primary measured optimization opportunity.

Rule invalidation now tracks the active vocabulary as well as claim
transactions. Each fired rule records a derive-vocabulary fingerprint: SHA-256
of the sorted registry contents, cached by immutable registry identity. This
avoids replay-order and local-edge-rowid dependence and does not wake rules
for ordinary lineage whose vocabulary is unchanged. Missing, retracted or
stale fingerprints conservatively re-evaluate once; equivalent reopened
registries remain quiet. Both marks advance only after complete derivation.
A vocabulary change during evaluation discards the current support calculation
and re-suspends current derivations on the next bounded pass. This also covers
conclusions established earlier in that invocation.

The metadata-only inverse-mapping regression failed before implementation;
reopen, dry-run rollback, committed retraction and quiet-rerun assertions now
pass. A second regression exposed stale support within one invocation and now
passes after the support restart. Legacy watermark recovery is covered too.
A separate pass-limit probe verifies that vocabulary restarts persist neither
mark on truncation and resume to a quiet fixpoint. All 1,565 workspace tests
pass across 24 package summaries with no failures, skips or cancellations.
Workspace build, website build and packed-artifact smoke pass. Rules README,
normative section 24.4 and the book now explain the companion mark. The PDF
was rebuilt with Typst 0.15.0, and pages 59–60 were rendered and visually
inspected for the changed paragraph and following chapter transition. The
fixed metadata-only invalidation bug file and its index entry were removed.

The metadata-only lineage review found a live/reloaded vocabulary mismatch:
appendEdges could attach a WHEN/VIA/BECAUSE edge to an existing declaration,
but the live registry retained it until explicit reload or reopen. Appending
such edges now checks their child declaration and rebuilds vocabulary within
the transaction; ordinary premise edges avoid declaration replay. A shared
adapter regression failed before the fix and now checks all three qualifier
roles, visibility inside a transaction, rollback of edges and vocabulary, and
agreement with explicit reload. Native store tests pass 140, website/WASM tests
29, and rules/actions/automation tests 40/34/61; workspace and website builds
pass. The store README documents the behavior.

A follow-up public-API probe confirmed a separate outstanding rule defect:
a settled inverse-premise rule skips after an edge excludes its REVERSE
mapping, retaining an unsupported conclusion. A full derivation retracts it.
The self-contained reproducer and required edge-watermark work are indexed in
bugs/rule-edge-only-invalidation.md. This pass fixes registry consistency; it
does not claim incremental rule invalidation is complete.

The playground result review confirmed that quoted CAVE binding values already
retain their delimiters, including a value containing the result separator
and text resembling another binding. Control characters, however, were emitted
invisibly: the embedded-NUL storage regression displayed the raw NUL. Worker
formatting now shows bindings containing control characters as escaped quoted
strings, including explicit escapes for C1 controls and Unicode line/paragraph
separators. Ordinary binding text is unchanged. The updated NUL browser case
failed before the display change and now verifies the complete escaped value;
a separate browser case retains the ordinary quoted separator value. All 42
production browser tests pass in one minute, and the website build, changeset
metadata and diff checks pass. The website README explains the display rule;
storage and query values are unchanged. Startup-construction and worker-crash
recovery were also inspected and remain covered by existing browser cases.

Documentation code examples now expose an explicit named keyboard scroll
target when they overflow, matching the existing reference-table treatment.
A browser regression first failed because the installation example had no
explicit Tab target. ScrollableCode measures both its container and intrinsic
code width, adds a focusable “Scrollable code example” region only on overflow,
and removes its extra stop and label when it fits. The inset focus outline
stays visible inside the clipped code frame. The new mobile-to-desktop browser
case checks arrow-key movement, page containment and removal of overflow
attributes after resizing. All 41 production browser tests pass in one minute;
the website build, changeset metadata and diff checks pass. The captured mobile
code-example image was inspected and its focus outline is visible. The website
README records the behavior. This change covers documentation examples; it
does not establish the accessibility of every website surface.

The synchronizer's filesystem-error regression found that the VS Code
manifest advanced before its alignment changelog succeeded. A retry then saw
an already-current version and skipped the missing entry. Extension alignment
now writes its changelog first, matching package alignment. A deterministic
filesystem obstruction reproduces the failure and checks that both private
package and extension versions remain old on their changelog failure; removing
the obstruction permits recovery with the correct Major Changes heading,
preserved historical text, and no duplicate entry on a further run. Three
focused versioning tests pass. The complete workspace suite after this fix and
the Changesets migration passes 1560 tests across 24 package summaries, with
zero failures, cancellations or skips. Website build, changeset metadata and
diff checks pass. IMPLEMENTATION.md records that successful earlier writes may
remain and that recovery invokes the synchronizer directly after Changesets
has consumed its inputs. This ordering does not make multi-file writes atomic.
No real release versions or external publication state were changed.

The local release toolchain now pairs exact Changesets CLI 3.0.1 with action
2.1.1's reviewed commit, renamed script inputs, default token input, and both
action-level release/tag creation disabled. The config schema follows v4 and
the temporary major-update ignores are removed. An isolated CLI trial and a
new installed-tool workspace test confirm fixed-group versioning, private
package opt-in, ignored website stability, root/extension/grammar
synchronization, and exit 1 on an empty second version run. CAVE intentionally
retains that empty-run failure; the action routes only pending changesets to
versioning. The workspace fixture initially exposed missing changelog entries
for private workspaces advanced only by the synchronizer (first failure:
automate). The synchronizer now supplies alignment entries for these packages
using the same path as the extension, preserving existing release entries.
Both focused versioning tests pass. The MCP run passed 106 of 107 tests; its
only failure was the workflow convention requiring a major-only action comment.
After correcting that comment, all 19 workflow/package-reference tests pass.
Frozen installation, workspace build, website build, Changesets status,
changeset metadata and diff checks pass. No release versions in the real
checkout were advanced. Hosted-action output, the version PR and actual npm /
Marketplace publication remain unverified and separately tracked; no external
publication or repository write occurred.

The release script now bridges verified pnpm publication to Changesets action
v2 output events. A new helper appends git-tag JSON lines only after successful
registry verification and tag handling; fully published recovery creates an
empty file, and absent CHANGESETS_OUTPUT remains a no-op. A fixture failed
before implementation because publication produced no output file. The final
106 release/MCP tests pass, including full/partial publication, tag recovery,
publication failure, verification failure and tag-push failure. Failed paths
emit no events or remote tags; successful paths retain one lockstep tag. All
registry and publish operations in these tests are local doubles, with local
bare Git remotes. No actual npm publication, remote repository write or action
upgrade occurred. Implementation docs and the migration task record this
completed bridge and the remaining coupled CLI/action migration. A core patch
changeset records the change.


Backlog reconciliation confirmed the whole-system audit and Changesets migration
remain active. Pinned action v2.1.1 source exposed a concrete migration gap:
CAVE publishes through pnpm, so forwarding CHANGESETS_OUTPUT cannot generate
the git-tag JSON-line events the action uses to report published packages.
The migration task now records the exact action commit, all required renamed
inputs, explicit disabling of action-owned tag pushes, the event schema and
required success/recovery/failure coverage for a custom output bridge. Source
review confirms the existing release script already owns validated tagging.
No CLI/action major, release workflow behavior or external state changed in
this pass. A core patch changeset records the review; the original completion
criteria, including real release verification, remain open.


Playground client lifecycle coverage is consolidated around a shared worker
double and bounded asynchronous tests. Explicit close, worker error, unreadable
message and fatal reply paths now each settle concurrent open/append/query
requests, terminate once, ignore late replies/errors and reject future work.
Ordinary request errors preserve another pending request and a later query.
Existing failed-send coverage is retained: 100 throwing sends leave only an
earlier legitimate request pending, then both earlier and later work resolve
on the same healthy worker without retained entries. All 28 website unit/runtime
tests pass. No client production change was needed; the website build passes
and the README explains the expanded lifecycle coverage. A core patch changeset
records this test consolidation. The prior production browser result remains
40 passing tests; it was not rerun for these unit-test/documentation changes.
No specification, command example or book-source change was required.


The SQL.js patch now has clean-install evidence independent of the current
node_modules tree. An isolated copy of the workspace manifests, pnpm lockfile,
workspace settings and tracked patch installed website production dependencies
with frozen resolution, ignored lifecycle scripts and a fresh package store.
All 111 dependencies were downloaded with zero reuse. Both installed optimized
bundles (sql-wasm.js and sql-wasm-browser.js) then initialized against the
installed WASM binary and preserved exact bound values and SQL hex bytes for
NUL-containing ASCII/Unicode, a leading BOM and empty text. The scratch tree
was removed after successful completion. The dependency-maintenance guide now
records this verification procedure and its scope; a core patch changeset
records the checkpoint. The log is /tmp/cave-sqljs-clean-install.log. This is
patch reproducibility evidence, not a new full-workspace or browser test run.
No public behavior, examples, specification or book source changed.


The WASM adapter now preserves SQL output names that overlap JavaScript
prototype properties. A shared adapter regression passed natively but failed
on WASM because SQL.js getAsObject discarded an aliased __proto__ column.
The adapter now reads column names and positional values into a null-prototype
object, matching native result shape; repeated output names retain the last
value. Column names are acquired after stepping and reused within an all()
result set. The shared test covers get/all, __proto__, constructor, toString,
duplicate names and JSON serialization. All 139 native store tests, 28 WASM
runtime tests and 40 production browser tests pass; the website build,
changeset and whitespace checks pass. An older allocation-lifecycle test now
expects the native-style object prototype while retaining its cleanup and
retry checks. Store and website READMEs document the result-name contract and
a core/store patch changeset records the fix. No schema, query syntax or book
source changed. Logs use /tmp/cave-wasm-column-names-* and
/tmp/cave-native-column-names.log.


The browser SQL.js binding had a separate embedded-NUL defect on both input
and output: binding a NUL-containing value stored only its prefix, while
reading complete TEXT produced from blob bytes also truncated it. Both
regressions failed before the fix. A tracked pnpm patch for SQL.js 1.14.2 now
passes explicit UTF-8 byte lengths when binding and decodes complete TEXT
bytes, preserving a leading BOM. Both optimized Node and browser bundles are
patched, with blobs/numbers/nulls retaining their original types. The website
pins the exact version and the lockfile records the patch hash. All 27 WASM
runtime tests pass, including ASCII/Unicode and leading/internal/trailing NULs;
all 40 production browser tests pass in 58.5 seconds, including rebuild/query
of a NUL-containing claim name. The website build and frozen install pass.
Website and dependency-maintenance docs explain the patch, its limited bundle
scope and upgrade/removal requirements; a core patch changeset records it.
No store schema or claim identity change was made. The book source/examples
remain valid and need no PDF update. Logs use /tmp/cave-wasm-text-*.


The native SQLite NUL-decoding defect is resolved at the runtime support
boundary. Upstream PR #61954 supplies explicit text byte lengths and shipped
in Node 24.16.0 and 26.1.0; direct probes pass on both and fail on 22.18.0,
24.0.0 and 26.0.0. All 350 selected store/rules/action/automation/view tests
pass on each new minimum. Package engines, doctor, CI and live runtime docs
now require ^24.16.0 || ^26.1.0. The native adapter checks text round-tripping
before opening caller data and caches success. A real Node 22.18.0 check
verifies two rejected attempts create no database file. Native adapter tests
cover ASCII and Unicode text with leading, internal and trailing NULs through
get/all. This replaces the unresolved compatibility status below; the bug file
and BUGS.md entry are removed. Node 22 support is deliberately withdrawn, so a
CLI/store minor changeset records the runtime requirement change. The store
README preserves upstream references, rationale and the standalone reproducer.
Book source contains no old minimum-version promise and needs no PDF update.
Final validation passed all 1,553 workspace tests across 24 summaries with
zero failures, cancellations or skips, plus the website build and packed
artifact smoke checks without an API snapshot refresh. Logs are
`/tmp/cave-lossless-runtime-integration.log`,
`/tmp/cave-lossless-runtime-site.log` and
`/tmp/cave-lossless-runtime-packed.log`. The focused minimum-runtime logs are
`/tmp/cave-lossless-node24-min-tests.log` and
`/tmp/cave-lossless-node26-min-tests.log`; these remain local macOS arm64
checks. Updated CI matrix jobs have not run remotely in this dirty worktree.


Cross-runtime lifecycle checks uncovered an unresolved native SQLite TEXT
compatibility defect. Node 22.18.0 passed 211 of 212 selected rules/action/
automation/view tests; the separator-name action test failed because its
stored NUL-containing declaration was truncated. A direct SQLite probe on
22.18.0 and 24.0.0 confirmed complete stored bytes but truncated returned TEXT.
Node 24.18.0 passed all 212 selected tests; local 26.5.0 passes the standalone
round-trip reproducer. The bug is indexed in BUGS.md, detailed in
bugs/native-sqlite-nul-decoding.md and called out in the store README.
The checked-in scripts/check-sqlite-text.mjs isolates it without CAVE parsing.
A store patch changeset records the finding; website build and changeset/
whitespace checks pass. No runtime minimum has been changed or failing test
skipped. Resolving the compatibility contract is the next concrete task;
this checkpoint does not claim supported-runtime completion.
