Settled rules now wake when vocabulary declaration rows arrive after their
watermark. A regression established a quiet rule over `MANAGED-BY`, then added
`MANAGES REVERSE MANAGED-BY` while its matching `alice MANAGES api` fact remained
older than the watermark. The ordinary query matched but derivation skipped
before the fix. A conservative probe for new `IS verb`, `REVERSE` and
`RENAMED-TO` rows now re-evaluates mappings over old facts; the next quiet run
skips again. All 40 rule and 61 automation tests and workspace/website builds
pass. A real source-entry CLI run against a temporary on-disk database also
derived this inverse fact and an equivalent numeric-value premise, retracted
the numeric conclusion after replacement, and skipped both rules when quiet.
The temporary database was removed. The rules README and specification §24.4
document why registry refresh alone cannot invalidate a watermark; a CLI/rules
patch changeset records the fix. Changeset and whitespace checks pass.
Existing book overview and examples remain accurate without a source/PDF edit.
This check covers newly appended vocabulary rows; it does not establish a
general invalidation mechanism for metadata-only database mutations.


Incremental rule wake-up detection now accounts for mutable values and tags.
The prior SQL probe compared exact attribute text and required current tag
membership; it missed a new `900M` claim for a `0.9B` numeric premise and
could leave conclusions active after a matching attribute, metric or tag was
replaced. Regressions reproduced missed firing and missed retraction before
the fix. The probe now keeps stable identity restrictions, admits metric rows
regardless of their replacement value, and leaves value/tag conditions to
the full query evaluator. Tests verify normalized numeric additions and
retractions, changed attribute/metric values, removed bare tags and changed
valued tags, then confirm quiet runs return to skipping. All 39 rule tests,
61 automation tests, workspace and website builds, changeset validation and
whitespace checks pass. The rules README and specification §24.4 now explain
the conservative probe and its support implications; a CLI/rules patch
changeset records the fix. The book's existing shape-probe/retraction overview
does not enumerate the removed filters and remains valid; no book source or
PDF was changed. Broader probe matching may cause extra evaluations when
unrelated metadata changes, preserving correctness over missed invalidation.


The website now provides a focus-visible “Skip to content” button before its
repeated navigation. Keyboard activation moves focus to the main heading (or
the loading main region if no heading exists), preserves the route/history,
and bypasses the documentation sidebar. A new browser test exercises
documentation, home, playground and unknown routes at 390 and 1,280 pixels.
Its stronger positioning assertion initially caught headings hidden behind
the sticky header; shared heading scroll clearance fixes that. The final
production browser suite passes all 39 tests in 55.4 seconds, including focused
heading position below the header and unchanged URLs. The website build,
changeset validation and whitespace checks pass. The mobile focus screenshot
was visually inspected: the control is legible and visible above navigation.
The website README documents the control and a core patch changeset records
it. This affects website navigation only; specification, command examples and
book source require no change.


A fresh whole-workspace integration run on the current worktree passed all
1,549 tests across 24 package summaries, with zero failures, cancellations or
skips. It includes the epoch/vocabulary composition, scenario candidate-read
optimization, shared shape SQL, action history lineage and expanded report-date
changes added since the previous full checkpoint. The current packed-artifact
smoke run also passed, including installed NodeNext/Bundler API contracts,
runtime imports, optional solver assets, CLI workflows, HTTP serving and grammar
highlighting. The packed API snapshot required no refresh. These are local
Node 26.5.0 macOS arm64 results, not remote CI or proof for other supported
platforms/runtimes. Logs are `/tmp/cave-current-system-integration.log` and
`/tmp/cave-current-system-packed.log`. A core patch changeset records this
integration checkpoint; no public behavior, specification, example or book
source changed in this validation pass.


Report citation dates no longer truncate expanded ISO years. UUIDv7 permits
unsigned 48-bit millisecond timestamps, including dates beyond year 9999;
taking the first ten ISO characters rendered year 10000 as `+010000-01`,
dropping its day. The renderer now retains the date before the ISO time
separator. A regression failed on that truncated output before the fix and
now checks the last millisecond of year 9999, the start of year 10000 and
the maximum UUID timestamp (`+010889-08-02`). All 77 view tests, workspace and
website builds, changeset validation and whitespace checks pass. The view
README documents complete UTC citation dates and a CLI/view patch changeset
records the fix. Stored timestamps, date-query syntax, public API shapes and
ordinary-year output are unchanged; existing examples and book source need
no update.


Action lifecycle coverage now follows an effect through its first write, a
premise revision, a no-op, a dry-run update, a committed update and database
reopen. Both historical effect versions retain their own BECAUSE premise and
VIA declaration IDs and action run provenance. The no-op preserves the original
row and edges; the dry run leaves claim and edge tables unchanged. All 34 action
tests, workspace and website builds, changeset validation and whitespace checks
pass. Source review confirms action reads already share the outer write
reservation with effects; no transaction implementation change was needed.
The action README now explains historical lineage and no-op ownership. A
CLI/act patch changeset records this coverage. The behavior agrees with existing
specification and examples, so no book source or PDF update was required.


The shape package's remaining general latest-claim SQL literal now uses
`QuerySql.current()`. An exact string comparison verified that the replacement
produces the same SQL; all 98 shape and 33 action tests and the workspace build
pass. The shape README documents the shared ownership and the dependencies a
future incremental gate must preserve: forward/inverse slots, inherited
targets, declarations and metadata, vocabulary mappings, and current-version
changes. Complete before/after evaluation remains in place. This refactor
does not claim a runtime improvement or implement a narrowed gate. A CLI/shape
patch changeset records it. Documentation review found no semantic, example,
specification or book-source changes needed.

The current large shaped automation benchmark passed at 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000
events in an isolated run. Active times were 11,636.1, 45,928.1 and 186,204.2 ms;
quiet times were 12.6, 24.0 and 53.2 ms. Each workload settled in two passes,
derived one ready claim and fired one action per event, verified every handled
entity/owner and all final shape checks, and appended zero quiet-cycle rows.
Final store sizes were 4,006, 8,006 and 16,006 rows. The Node 26.5.0 /
SQLite 3.53.3 macOS arm64 measurements extend the earlier selective-indexing
follow-up beyond 1,000 events. They are roughly 20% below the older projection
baseline but retain approximately quadratic active scaling. Source review
confirms full shape evaluation before and after every action. The automation
README records the new table and its limits; a CLI/automate patch changeset
records the review. The completed larger-workload measurement item is removed
from the remaining review wording; lifecycle/provenance work remains open.

Winner-mode scenario binding no longer queries unresolved base candidates that
it immediately discards. Coexisting mode retains both candidate queries so it
can identify evidence excluded by winner resolution. A regression counted two
candidate SQL reads before the change and now verifies one in winner mode,
two in coexisting mode, the expected Boolean value and supporting row identity.
All 57 scenario tests, workspace/website builds and packed-artifact smoke checks
pass, including existing contested input and snapshot-change checks. The scenario README documents the distinction
and now explicitly carries the shared pre-epoch transaction-boundary rule from
the earlier SQL fix. A scenario patch changeset records this optimization.
Public input/output shapes, definition digests and evaluator ownership are
unchanged; no new latency claim is inferred from the query-count reduction.

The shared native/WASM adapter contract now verifies epoch clipping together
with historical qualifier visibility. A CUSTOM verb declaration recorded at
millisecond zero is absent before the epoch, present in the second crossing the
epoch and at its exact transaction, then excluded once its later WHEN parent
(at millisecond 1,000) enters the view. Both exact-parent and whole-day boundaries
exclude it. All 137 native store tests, 25 website runtime/WASM tests and the
workspace build pass. Source review confirms query and scenario transaction-time
validation use the shared QuerySql helpers, while valid-time anchors use Time.
No additional production change was needed. The existing epoch and qualifier
specification paragraphs and package references cover this composition; no
further user-facing documentation or book source edit was required. A store
patch changeset records the verification.

Valid transaction-time dates before 1970 previously reached Uuidv7.at with a
negative timestamp and threw instead of producing an empty historical interval.
The shared SQL boundary helper now clips both ends at the UUID epoch. Regressions
cover year 0000, 1969, all six tx comparison operators, the ISO week crossing
1970, and a one-second interval starting 500 ms before the epoch. Epoch claims
remain visible in the overlapping portion, while valid-time at:1960 still selects
claims about that earlier period independently. All 136 store tests, 104 query
tests, the full 1,544-test workspace suite, workspace/website builds and packed
smoke checks pass. Real CLI queries against an epoch-stamped database return
zero matches for --as-of 1969 and one for the crossing timestamp. Store/query
READMEs and the as-of specification clarify the boundary; a store/query patch
changeset records the fix. Existing book examples remain accurate and no book
source changed. Public declaration shapes and the packed API snapshot are
unchanged.

The recent kernel, pagination and cleanup changes were rechecked locally on
macOS arm64 with Node 22.18.0, the supported Node 24.0.0 minimum, and CI-pinned
Node 24.18.0. Each exact binary was version-checked through pnpm dlx, and each
then passed the same 457 tests: all core, store, query, fusion, view and website
runtime/client files. Runs were sequential with test-concurrency=1. This covers
the new UUID failure handling, native/WASM cleanup subscriptions, projection
failure paths, interrupted HTTP delivery and raw-position pagination through
those runtimes. It is source-test evidence for those packages on macOS, not
Linux/Windows execution or a claim that every workspace test was repeated on
every runtime. The existing full Node 26 workspace and packed checks remain
separate evidence. A core patch changeset records this compatibility review;
no production code, public behavior, book source or website copy changed.

Projection lifecycle coverage now injects throwing cleanup callbacks into both
public and internal cached stores. Source closure reports both errors while
closing both SQLite projections and the source, running a later source cleanup
callback, clearing the cache and avoiding repeated callback execution. Explicit
cache eviction reports the same errors but leaves its source usable; a newly
built replacement projection then closes with the source. All 76 view tests and
the workspace build pass. No production change was needed. The view README
records the callback-error behavior and a CLI/view patch changeset records the
verification. These tests concern throwing cleanup callbacks, not a guarantee
that an underlying database close can never fail. Language and book semantics
are unchanged.

Visual QA of the expanded query benchmark table at a 390-pixel viewport found
that inherited overflow-wrap:anywhere split headings such as Claims and numeric
values across lines even though the article reported no horizontal overflow.
Markdown tables now preserve normal word boundaries and retain their existing
horizontal overflow container. A ResizeObserver-backed table renderer supplies
a named keyboard focus target only while the table overflows, observes intrinsic
section widths as well as the outer box, and disconnects on unmount. The focus
outline uses the site's existing theme token. A production-browser regression
verifies ArrowRight scrolling, no document-wide overflow, and removal of the
extra tab stop and label after resizing to desktop. Visual inspection confirms
whole numeric values and readable column headings in the mobile result. The
website build and all 38 production browser tests pass. The website README
records the responsive keyboard behavior; a core patch changeset records the
improvement. Markdown table data and book source are unchanged.

Cleanup-hook subscriptions now have independent registration identity. The first
implementation used callback identity in a Set, so registering the same function
three times and unsubscribing one left zero callbacks; the new shared-adapter
regression expects the remaining two. A per-registration wrapper preserves both
remaining callbacks, makes repeated unsubscribe harmless and retains exactly-once
close behavior. All 135 native store tests, 24 website runtime/WASM tests,
74 view tests and the workspace build pass. The store README clarifies the
subscription contract, and the packed consumer fixture exercises the same case
through installed imports. The normal packed smoke test, both consumer type
resolutions and the website build pass. A store patch changeset records this correction to
the newly introduced lifecycle API; its declaration shape is unchanged.

A real HTTP disconnect regression interrupts a two-MiB overview response after
its first received chunk and verifies that the response is incomplete. A
subsequent entity request succeeds. Closing the HTTP handle does not invoke the
source cleanup hook, and a later direct ingest still works; the owner's explicit
store.close runs that hook once. All 74 view tests and the workspace build pass.
The view README records disconnect recovery and distinguishes it from cancelling
synchronous SQL already running. No production HTTP change was needed. A CLI/view
patch changeset records the evidence. This test covers delivery interruption and
ownership, not every network failure or a long-running query cancellation policy.

Source-store closure now deterministically releases cached sensitivity projections.
A regression previously observed two cached SQLite stores still open after the
source closed. Store.onClose registers synchronous dependent cleanup and returns
an unsubscribe function. Store.close attempts all callbacks before closing the
database, reports one error directly or several through AggregateError, prevents
reentrant/repeated cleanup, and permits a database-close retry without repeating
callbacks. View cache disposal unregisters its hook, forgets the cache and attempts
every projection close even when another fails. HTTP handles retain caller
ownership of their source store. Shared native/WASM lifecycle tests cover
unsubscribe, callback failures, reentrant close and database-close retry; view
tests verify both projections are closed and removed. All 134 store tests,
73 view tests, 23 website runtime tests, the full 1,537-test workspace suite and
workspace/website builds pass. The packed declaration review changes only the
store.d.ts fingerprint for the new method. The normal packed smoke check passes,
including NodeNext/Bundler compilation and execution of hook registration,
unsubscription and exactly-once cleanup from the installed store package.
Store/view READMEs and the
implementation guide document ownership and synchronous-only cleanup. A store
and CLI minor changeset, with the private view patch, records the enhancement.
No versions were edited manually. This resource fix does not close the separate
HTTP disconnect review or change language/CLI command semantics.

Profiling a 100-page, 10,000-row valid-time traversal attributed 2,609 ms of
2,901 ms total to candidate SQL (200 reads), compared with 75 ms for its 200
revision checks. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN showed repeated latest-row grouping and a
temporary ordering B-tree. The new current-query benchmark compares that shared
SQL with a correlated indexed MAX(tx) alternative, checking equal row identities
outside timing. On the same Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 macOS arm64 runtime,
three-sample medians for 100 SQL requests were 844.81 versus 517.86 ms with
10,000 distinct current keys, but 381.47 versus 518.86 ms with 100 current keys
and 100 revisions per key. The blanket replacement is rejected: its benefit on
distinct claims does not justify the regression on revision-heavy history.
Production SQL remains unchanged. The standalone comparison emits plans, samples
and runtime versions; the query README preserves the measurements and decision,
and a query patch changeset records this review. Future optimization must cover
both distributions and historical/latest-row semantics.

The pagination benchmark now follows every continuation in three complete
traversals per fixture, alongside its five first-page measurements. It checks
all expected bindings in order, stable snapshot identity, expected page counts
and termination outside the timing interval. All six traversal fixtures pass:
1,000/10,000 claims each produce 10/100 pages; dense valid-time and exact-number
queries return every claim, while the selective fixture returns 10/100 matches.
On Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 macOS arm64, 10,000-row medians are 2,887.18 ms,
2,889.77 ms and 2,739.98 ms respectively, versus 47.53, 44.75 and 30.75 ms at
1,000 rows. The query README records the full table and explains the superlinear
observed growth. Timings include retaining page results, not assertions, and do
not model transport or concurrent writes. This establishes complete traversal
for the measured fixtures without claiming general full-scan scalability. A
query patch changeset records the benchmark extension; the website build and
changeset validation pass, and no runtime API changed.

Selective pagination now reads a candidate batch up to its existing scan budget,
tracking original row positions in an internal weak map through valid-time and
exact-number post-filters. A full page advances only through its last returned
match; later fetched rows remain available to the next cursor. The index is
allocated only when filtered pagination requests it, with no public record or
cursor-format change. A regression that previously counted 101 SQL windows now
requires at most the candidate batch and lookahead, and walks matches at raw
positions 99, 100 and 200 across one-result pages without gaps or duplication.
Existing mixed 17-result pages, numeric approximation, empty scan-budget pages
and historical-revision regressions still pass. All 103 query tests, the full
1,532-test workspace suite, workspace and website builds, and existing performance
gates pass. Packed validation initially detected the intentional internal window
parameter change. Reviewing the generated snapshot confirmed that only the
bounded.d.ts and compile.d.ts fingerprints changed; exported declarations and
page/record schemas are unchanged. Those two fingerprints are refreshed, and
the normal packed-artifact smoke check now passes, including both consumer type
resolutions and installed CLI scenarios. Isolated five-sample selective medians dropped from
113.75 to 2.87 ms at 1,000 rows and 1,068.77 to 22.95 ms at 10,000 rows on the
same Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 macOS arm64 setup. The all-passing 100-result
fixtures remain about 4–5 ms and 24 ms respectively. The query README documents
the implementation and measurement limits; a query patch changeset records the
improvement. The specific small-page cost item is removed from remaining scope;
the later traversal benchmark above extends the evidence, while the wider
temporal/query review remains distinct work.

The pagination benchmark now includes a selective one-result valid-time page:
99 expired claims precede each eligible claim, so the page consumes its 100-row
scan budget to return one result. Five-sample medians on the existing macOS arm64,
Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 setup were 113.75 ms at 1,000 claims and 1,068.77 ms
at 10,000. A page-local historical-vocabulary cache was implemented and measured,
then removed: the 10,000-row median remained 1,070.44 ms, providing no meaningful
benefit for its added state. The caching experiment left production behavior unchanged.
Its evidence identified repeated SQL work as the dominant cost and motivated
the subsequent raw-row position implementation recorded above. The query README records the
fixture, measured limitation and rejected optimization, and a query patch
changeset records the benchmark extension. Workspace and website builds pass.
The benchmark runs correctness checks outside timing and does not establish
latency budgets or full-traversal cost. No public API or book content changed.

The initial filtered-pagination optimization batched SQL reads up to the
remaining match capacity and raw scan budget; the newer row-position pass above
removes the match-capacity restriction while retaining the scan budget. Previously every candidate required its own SQL window,
including candidates that all passed; a regression counted 101 windows for a
100-match exact-number page. The new path needs the batch and one lookahead,
consumes every fetched row, and preserves raw offsets without dropping the next
page's first match. Regression coverage also walks mixed valid-time rows across
17-match pages and retains the existing empty-page scan-budget checks. All 102
query tests, the full 1,531-test workspace suite, workspace and website builds,
packed-artifact smoke checks and existing performance gates pass. The reproducible pagination benchmark
measures five first-page reads with 100 passing candidates: on macOS arm64,
Node 26.5.0 and SQLite 3.53.3, 10,000-row valid-time medians changed from
1,079.97 to 24.39 ms and exact-number medians from 1,093.66 to 25.06 ms.
One-thousand-row medians changed from about 116 ms to 4–5 ms. These isolated
measurements exclude ingestion and do not represent cold CLI startup, selective
post-filters, page size one, or full traversal. The query README documents the
batching invariant, measurements and limits; pnpm bench:pagination reproduces
the fixture. A query patch changeset records the enhancement. No public API,
query semantics, CLI options or book source changed.

Pagination token validation now has broader malformed-input regression coverage:
invalid percent/UTF-8 encodings, incomplete JSON, non-object JSON values,
missing fields, negative/fractional/unsafe offsets, malformed revision arrays,
and noncanonical transaction IDs all produce the documented invalid-cursor
restart error. Rejection preserves the two stored claims and the original valid
continuation still returns the remaining match without another page. All 101
query tests and the workspace build pass; no production paging change was
needed. The query README records that malformed requests neither mutate stored
history nor invalidate a valid continuation. A query patch changeset records
the verification. Existing snapshot-arrival and lineage checks remain in place;
this bounded validation review does not establish completion of the wider query
cost and temporal audit. No CLI or book behavior changed.

Primary website navigation now exposes the active Docs or Playground area with
aria-current="location", matching its existing visual highlight. Documentation
sidebar links retain the more specific current-page marker. A real production
Chromium check verified home, overview, store documentation, a missing document,
playground and a missing top-level route; browser Back restored the Playground
marker. Home and unknown top-level routes mark neither area current. The website
build and all 37 production browser tests pass. The website README records the
behavior and a core patch changeset records this accessibility improvement. No package API, language specification,
CLI or book content changed.

The shared SQLite adapter contract now injects a randomness failure on the
second UUID of an ingest batch containing a verb declaration and a relation.
Both native SQLite and the real WASM adapter roll back the already inserted
first row, restore the vocabulary registry, preserve the pre-existing claim,
and accept a successful retry with increasing IDs. All 132 store tests and
21 website runtime/client tests pass, as do the workspace and website builds.
No production transaction change was needed. The store README distinguishes
prevalidated replay rejection from allocation failures: a successfully minted
ID in a rolled-back transaction may leave a sequence gap, since the generator
is process-wide and cannot safely be rewound for one store. This extends the
UUID failure fix with actual database evidence; it does not claim that every
adapter failure path has been exhausted. A store patch changeset records the
checks. The existing specification's atomicity and ordering rules remain
unchanged; no CLI or book source update was needed.

UUID generation previously mutated its process-wide timestamp and sequence before
validation and randomness completed. A regression demonstrated that a rejected
NaN clock erased the ordering floor: the following call minted at timestamp zero
below an observed future ID. Infinity could instead leave later calls failing.
Uuidv7.next now validates the clock and rolled timestamp, computes candidate
state locally, and commits it only after the ID is constructed successfully.
The regression covers nonfinite, negative, fractional and overflowing clocks,
plus a throwing random source, and verifies the exact next timestamp/sequence.
All 93 core tests, the full 1,528-test workspace suite, and the workspace and
website builds pass. The packed-artifact smoke test also passes, including
consumer type checks and installed CLI scenarios. The core README records the
failure contract, and a core patch changeset records the fix.
The storage receive-rule specification remains unchanged: this repairs its
existing monotonicity guarantee. No book source or CLI surface changed.

The editor resource review verifies four additional failure paths: parser
construction frees the previously allocated query, token-builder construction
and finalization failures free the per-document tree, and parser disposal
failure still frees the query while repeated disposal and later provider calls
remain inert. These are host/resource-double fault-injection checks of the
existing cleanup implementation; no production resource-handling change was
needed. All 12 editor tests, typechecking and the extension build pass. The
installed web-tree-sitter Language type has no disposal method; its parser,
query and tree handles have the explicit cleanup obligations checked here.
The editor README records token-building and disposal failure behavior, and a
tree-sitter patch changeset records the verification. Documentation review found
no language, CLI, book or package API changes requiring updates.

The extension's documented F5 development workflow now has checked-in launch and
task configurations under editors/vscode/.vscode. The README previously named F5
without providing either configuration. Run CAVE extension starts an extension
host for that workspace after the linked pnpm build task; the README now says
to open editors/vscode itself and restart debugging after source edits. JSON and
task-linkage checks pass, and executing the configured task produces the bundle,
source map, grammar, query and runtime assets. Packaging validates the 12-file
VSIX; independent ZIP inspection confirms the development configurations are
excluded and the source map is present. The website documentation build passes.
A tree-sitter patch changeset records the workflow. An interactive F5 session
was not launched, so debugger behavior remains distinct from these configuration,
build and archive checks.

The VS Code semantic-token provider now checks cancellation before reading the
document or parsing it. The regression first failed because an already-cancelled
request called getText; it now returns empty tokens without parser/tree activity,
and the subsequent active request parses and frees its tree normally. All eight
extension tests/typechecks pass, including real WASM Unicode/CRLF/incomplete-edit
range checks. The Marketplace toolchain builds and validates the 12-file VSIX,
and the website documentation build passes. The extension README and a tree-sitter
patch changeset record the entry cancellation check and its synchronous-parse
limit. No interactive extension-host session or publication was performed.

VS Code CAVE files now contribute two-space indentation defaults with hard tabs
and indentation autodetection disabled. The parser rejects tab indentation;
these language-specific defaults align new editing with that boundary while
allowing explicit CAVE settings to override them and leaving existing contents
untouched. All seven extension tests/typechecks pass, and the Marketplace
toolchain packages and validates the 12-file VSIX. Independent ZIP inspection
confirms insertSpaces=true, tabSize=2, detectIndentation=false and the preserved
semantic-highlighting default in its manifest. The website documentation build
passes. The extension README links the official editor settings reference, and
the website README clarifies that Tab retains normal focus navigation in the
browser editor. A tree-sitter package patch changeset carries the extension
change. No interactive VS Code extension-host session or Marketplace publication
was performed in this check.

Repeated live report queries now reuse the last successful identical query text
within one render's immutable scoped view and fixed options. Only one result is
retained; a different query replaces it and a new report starts fresh. Query
errors still produce per-occurrence line diagnostics. Regressions verify updated
store data between renders, independent historical options and both failure
locations. The report benchmark now includes repeated live splices with exact
expected values and one shared citation. Five sequential calls per case, run
without competing builds/tests, improved medians from 64.81 to 14.89 ms for 1,000
occurrences and from 610.48 to 164.36 ms for 10,000. These are repeated-query
measurements, not a claim about distinct queries. All 72 view tests, both focused
CLI report tests, repository/website builds and packed smoke checks pass against
the existing API snapshot. The view README and a CLI/view patch changeset record
the bounded reuse and measured benefit.

Report parsing now has a reproducible pnpm bench:report command. It renders
1,000 and 10,000 indented examples, HTML comments and multiline quoted code spans,
with one live splice per template, five sequential calls per case and no
competing build/test workload. Every call verifies preserved example text, a
successful live splice, one citation and no problems outside the measured time.
On macOS arm64/Node 26.5.0/SQLite 3.53.3, the 10,000-example medians were 47.87,
50.25 and 344.83 ms respectively; the view README records all sizes and medians
and replaces the older render measurements with current-parser evidence. The
benchmark emits runtime metadata and raw timing samples and sets no speculative
latency threshold. Both direct and package-script execution pass. All ten
existing performance budgets also pass independently, and repository/website
builds pass. A CLI/view patch changeset records the benchmark and documentation.

Production-browser checks distinguish empty input from invalid indentation in
the playground. A space-only query reports CAVE-Q: empty query and retains the
database. Tabs in claim indentation fail both append and rebuild while retaining
the previous belief count. Space/newline-only append adds zero claims/edges;
rebuilding that source yields zero beliefs and a valid query returns no matches.
A subsequent rebuild with api IS service yields one belief and the expected
query binding. The initial probe's assumption that tabs count as ignorable blank
input was corrected against the strict parser and observed browser error; no
runtime behavior was changed. The website README and a core patch changeset
record the verified input distinctions. The temporary browser and server closed
after the checks.

Website route-error recovery now focuses its own heading through the shared
route-focus component. Both simulated Docs and Playground download failures
first failed the heading-focus assertion; the updated browser checks verify
heading focus, Tab to Reload page, Enter to retry and destination-heading focus
after successful recovery. The existing home-navigation escape remains covered.
All 37 production-browser tests pass (52.0 seconds), and the website build passes.
The website README and a core patch changeset record the recovery behavior.

Website home, playground and missing-page routes now move focus to the main
heading and reset scroll when destination content is ready. A small component
inside Suspense waits for lazy playground content; its route key remounts it on
navigation without refocusing during ordinary page updates. Documentation keeps
its existing article/section focus behavior. The browser regression first failed
on home heading focus; it now covers keyboard activation, returning home, Back,
missing-page focus and tabindex=-1. All 37 production-browser tests pass (51.7
seconds), and the website build passes. The website README and a core patch
changeset record the accessibility improvement.

The accumulated fusion/release integration checkpoint passes all 1,521 tests
across 24 package summaries, with zero failures, cancellations or skips,
including executable book examples. The current production website passes all
37 browser tests (53.6 seconds). Incremental verification passes both before and
after the full suite. A CLI patch changeset records this local checkpoint.

Read-only GitHub inspection also verified successful main CI run
34019970004 for 4a5c4c7a3f1c9f7a43cbc283e40db0fd08eb0360, this audit branch's
base commit. Its suite, browser, smoke, VSIX and aggregate jobs succeeded, as did
Node 22.18.0/Linux, Node 24.18.0/macOS, Node 24.18.0/Windows and Node 26.4.0/Linux
runtime jobs. The changeset job was skipped on that main push as expected.
The [remote run](https://github.com/mirek/cave/actions/runs/34019970004) establishes
coverage of the base commit only: it does not validate the uncommitted audit
changes on those runners or close the outstanding repository-setting and
release-migration criteria.

The changeset exemption no longer trusts a branch-name prefix. Every PR runs
the changeset job, whose shell step waives the new-file requirement only for
the exact changeset-release/main head from the same repository targeting main.
The aggregate requires success on every PR and accepts a skipped changeset job
only on pushes. Seven executed shell scenarios cover the recognized version PR,
forks, prefix/suffix lookalikes, a case variant, another base and an ordinary
branch. Forks and lookalikes continue to the Git/metadata validation path.
All 105 MCP tests, repository build, CI YAML checks and website documentation
build pass. Implementation/changeset documentation and a CLI patch changeset
record the narrower exemption. This recognizes the reserved same-repository
branch; it does not attest that its contents are an authoritative version commit,
which remains the release preflight's separate responsibility.

Release preflight now reads NUL-delimited committed changeset paths and raw file
contents. The regressions first counted only two of five committed unusual
filenames and accepted frontmatter preceded by a blank line that CI rejected.
All five paths now reach metadata validation and the pending-publication guard,
and shared parsing sees the original text. A further fixture verifies that an
otherwise authoritative version commit cannot publish when every pending name
requires Git quoting. The complete MCP run passed 103 tests before that final
fixture was added; the final nine-test version-PR group, including the new
publication guard regression, passes too. The final repository build passes.
Changeset documentation and a CLI patch changeset record the input-preservation
contract. All Git remotes and publish validation in these tests were isolated
fixtures; no real publication or remote repository settings were changed.

PR CI and release preflight now share changeset metadata validation through
scripts/changeset-metadata.mjs. The CI fixture first showed malformed contents
being accepted by the former awk/sed check. The new working-tree checker rejects
missing frontmatter, empty summaries, invalid severities, duplicate/unknown
packages, private-only releases and missing or insufficient bundled CLI bumps.
Tests preserve valid documentation-only empty frontmatter and matched CLI/private
severity, along with the unusual Git ref/path cases. Release fixtures use the
same shared helper and retain committed-state and version/tag checks. All 101
MCP tests, repository build, CI YAML parsing and website documentation build
pass. Running the new checker over all 329 current pending changesets passes.
Implementation and changeset documentation plus a CLI patch changeset record
the shared contract. Working-tree metadata validity does not establish release
readiness or close the separate external release criteria.

Changeset CI now treats Git refs and paths as data. The fixture first reproduced
a Git-quoted Unicode changeset path being opened as a nonexistent literal name.
The job now uses an environment variable for the base ref, NUL-delimited Git
output and a quoted Bash array for added filenames, with an explicit failure on
Git comparison errors. Real temporary Git repositories cover spaces, quotes,
glob characters, newlines and Unicode filenames; a ref containing shell syntax
does not execute a marker command. Private-only changesets still fail validation
under an unusual filename, and a missing base ref fails. All 101 MCP tests pass,
including the actual aggregate shell gate, as do the repository build, CI YAML
parsing and website documentation build. Implementation docs and a CLI patch
changeset record the behavior. These local checks do not prove execution on the
remote CI runners or change the outstanding required-status-check setting.

The aggregate CI test job now includes the changeset job. A regression first
demonstrated that the actual aggregate shell script accepted a failed changeset
check; it now rejects failures, cancellation, missing results and unexpected
skips. The subsequent exact-version-PR exemption runs a successful changeset job
for the recognized version PR; skipped jobs are now accepted only on pushes.
Tests check dependency
wiring and condition agreement and execute ten outcome/requirement combinations.
All 100 MCP tests pass, along with the repository build, CI YAML parsing and
website documentation build. Implementation documentation and a CLI patch
changeset record the gate behavior.

Read-only GitHub API inspection on 2026-09-07 found active main ruleset 22335398
protecting the default branch against deletion/force pushes and requiring a
squash pull request, but containing no required-status-check rule. Thus the
local aggregate improvement does not establish enforced green CI before merge;
that repository-setting gap remains open in the release/platform review. No
remote settings were changed. The separate Changesets v3 migration also retains
its real version-PR, npm, Marketplace and single-tag completion criteria.

Fusion total weight now uses compensated accumulation as well as the mean.
The regression first showed a unit-precision estimate followed by 10,000
estimates of precision 1e-16 retaining only the unit precision. The corrected
denominator retains their combined weight for both tested input orders; the
posterior precision, sigma and constant mean match their expected values within
1e-15. All 26 fusion tests and four focused MCP fusion tests pass, including
the prior cancellation, tiny-weight and finite-boundary cases. The repository
build, website documentation build and packed smoke checks also pass against the
existing API snapshot. The fusion README and a fusion patch changeset record
the improvement.

Posterior mean accumulation now compensates for rounding during cancellation.
The regression first returned 0.5 for equal-weight means 1e16, 1 and -1e16,
whose mean is 1/3. All six tested input permutations now retain the small
contribution and return 1/3. Additional checks exercise repeated positive and
negative Number.MAX_VALUE estimates; their posteriors remain finite and within
the tested relative tolerance. Existing tiny-weight and overflow cases pass.
All 25 fusion tests and four MCP fusion tests pass, along with the repository
build, website documentation build and packed smoke checks against the existing
API snapshot. The fusion README and a fusion patch changeset record the change.

Hypothesis normalization and gap checks now use compensated probability sums.
The regression first showed a dominant probability of 1 followed by 10,000
probabilities of 1e-16 producing a gap of zero, losing their combined mass.
Neumaier summation retains the contribution for both tested input orders and
provides the corrected denominator to normalization. The same regression checks
new output records, unchanged frozen inputs, preserved hypothesis fields and
equal normalization of the smallest positive representable probabilities.
All 24 fusion tests pass, including malformed/sparse input checks; the repository
build, website documentation build and packed smoke checks also pass against the
existing API snapshot. The fusion README and a fusion patch changeset record the
improvement and the remaining JavaScript floating-point precision limit.

Fusion optional fields now distinguish omitted confidence from malformed null.
The regression first reproduced null being silently treated as confidence 1;
validation now rejects it with RangeError, including through structural claim
extraction. Supplied non-string estimate units throw TypeError before weighting,
even at zero confidence. Missing/undefined confidence still defaults to 1,
missing/undefined units remain dimensionless, and arbitrary string units retain
their existing exact-match behavior. All 23 fusion tests and four focused MCP
fusion tests pass, as do the repository build, website documentation build and
packed smoke checks against the existing API snapshot. The fusion README and a
fusion patch changeset document the runtime boundary correction.

The accumulated report Markdown changes pass the complete repository suite:
1,511 tests across 24 package summaries, with zero failures, cancellations or
skips. Incremental build verification also passes. Dependency maintenance now
excludes mdast-util-* and micromark* from routine Dependabot groups, applying the
existing separate-parser-review policy to the newly shipped report dependencies.
The YAML parses successfully, and glob checks against the CLI manifest cover
all three direct report parser dependencies. The production advisory command
pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=low exits successfully with no known
vulnerabilities reported. The maintenance policy and a CLI patch changeset
record the exclusions. This local audit result is a registry snapshot, not a
guarantee about future advisories or completion of the remaining system scope.

Report query blocks now come from parsed top-level Markdown code nodes. The
regression first showed an invalid backtick info string being executed; it also
covers short-indented list fences, blockquotes and footnotes remaining literal
while subsequent prose splices run. Parsed block end positions replace the
independent line scanner, and the redundant HTML mask is removed. Closing-fence
validation accepts only spaces/tabs after the delimiter; nonbreaking and em
spaces preserve the unclosed-block diagnostic and authored fragment. Existing
empty, malformed and unclosed query-block tests still pass. All 71 view tests,
both focused CLI report tests, repository build, website documentation build and
packed smoke checks pass against the existing API snapshot. The view README and
a CLI/view patch changeset record the behavior.

Report inline splices now use parsed Markdown code spans instead of a separate
per-line backtick scanner. The new regression first reproduced execution through
escaped delimiters; coverage also checks multiline code examples and reference
definition titles stay literal. Valid multiline splices now normalize line
endings to query spaces, preserve surrounding text and adjacent splices, and
report problems at the opening delimiter's source line. Blockquote continuations
and LF, CRLF and CR inputs are covered. All 70 view tests and both focused CLI
report tests pass, along with the repository build, website documentation build
and packed smoke checks using the existing API snapshot. The view README,
implementation dependency description and a CLI/view patch changeset record the
change; the existing normative Markdown code-span contract remains unchanged.

Report HTML boundaries keep raw HTML examples literal. A regression first
showed inline and fenced queries expanding inside an HTML comment. The initial
fix masked parsed HTML positions for scanning; the subsequent parsed-span and
query-fence integration removed that mask and selects executable constructs
directly from the Markdown tree, retaining original output text. Coverage includes comments, pre,
script, style and div blocks, processing instructions, CDATA, blockquotes,
inline attributes (including unmatched backticks), multiline inline comments,
adjacent live prose, blank-line block termination and CRLF templates. HTML-only
examples add no citations or problems; inline element text remains live Markdown.
All 69 view tests, the repository build, website documentation build and packed
smoke checks pass, including the existing API snapshot and installed CLI report
workflow. View/implementation documentation and a CLI/view patch changeset record
the change. This is literal-region handling, not HTML sanitization, and does not
establish coverage of every Markdown construct.

Website destinations now set descriptive browser titles instead of retaining
the home-page title everywhere. Documentation uses the navigation label with
CAVE Docs; home, playground and missing destinations have their own titles.
Direct browser checks against the production build passed for seven destinations,
reloads, article fragments, native navigation, Back and Forward. All 37 existing
production-browser tests pass (50.8 seconds), and the website build passes.
The website README and a core patch changeset record the behavior. No book or
language/API documentation changes are needed for this browser-only improvement.

A fresh clean-build checkpoint verifies the accumulated changes without relying
on retained dist outputs. The clean targets were checked against tracked paths
before cleanup; pnpm clean and the full repository build pass. Incremental
verification passes both immediately after building and after all other checks.
All 1,508 tests across 24 package summaries pass with zero failures,
cancellations or skips, including executable book sessions. The rebuilt website
passes all 37 production-browser tests (51.3 seconds). Packed smoke checks pass
both module-resolution typechecks, the existing API snapshot and installed CLI
workflows, regenerating packaged legal/grammar assets as required. A CLI patch
changeset records this checkpoint. These are local macOS results and do not
establish completion of the remaining platform, external-state or system-review
scope above.

Incremental-build verification now anchors tsc to the repository rather than
the caller's directory, uses the fixed cmd.exe launcher for Windows pnpm shims,
and reports process-start/signal failures explicitly. A direct invocation from
an unrelated temporary directory failed before the fix and now verifies the
repository successfully. Two focused tests cover platform command construction,
root selection, pending projects, compiler failure, failed spawn and signals;
all 99 MCP package tests pass. Repository build, ordinary build:verify and the
website build pass. Windows command construction was tested through an injected
runner on macOS, not a Windows execution in this session. The implementation
reference and CLI patch changeset record the portability fix; clean-build and
platform CI coverage remain distinct checks.

Fusion collection validation now visits every claim, estimate, condition and
hypothesis array slot. forEach/flatMap previously skipped holes, silently
omitting evidence or returning sparse normalized hypotheses. Failing-before
regressions cover missing conditions after a zero factor, missing estimates,
missing claims and sparse hypothesis sets. for-of validation rejects them;
fuseClaims collects estimates in that same traversal. Dense and empty inputs
retain their documented behavior. All 22 fusion tests, 37 rules consumer tests,
four MCP fusion checks, repository/website builds and packed smoke checks pass
with the existing API snapshot. The fusion reference and patch changeset
document the required dense arrays.

Estimate extraction now shares the finite-mean, positive-finite-sigma and
confidence-range check used by fuse. Structurally constructed claims previously
bypassed Claim.of validation and could produce an invalid Estimate from
estimateOf. A failing regression covers non-finite means and out-of-range or
non-finite confidence, including zero-confidence invalid means. A valid
zero-confidence claim still extracts normally and fuse then skips its weight.
All 20 fusion tests, four MCP fusion checks, repository/website builds and
packed smoke checks pass with the existing API snapshot. The fusion reference
and patch changeset record the consistent boundary; no public type or claim
format changes were needed.

Uncertainty review confirmed differing value/delta duration units are valid
authored input and belong to fusion's conversion boundary, not record rejection.
It exposed estimateOf returning zero or infinity when an otherwise valid sigma
underflowed or overflowed during conversion. A failing regression preceded the
fix: converted sigma now passes the shared positive-finite validation before
an estimate is returned. Coverage retains valid extreme and subnormal spreads.
All 19 fusion tests, four MCP fusion consumer tests, repository/website builds
and packed smoke checks pass with the existing API snapshot. The fusion
reference clarifies conversion errors and distinguishes estimate extraction
from fusion's zero-confidence filtering. A fusion patch changeset records the
fix; claim parsing and record formats are unchanged.

The publisher now rejects unsupported arguments before changing directory or
running preflight. Previously it ignored every argument, so --dry-run could
proceed under ordinary publication semantics. An isolated copy with a
marker-writing preflight stub demonstrated the failure without registry access;
the fixed regression checks --dry-run, --help, a positional argument and a
validator-style mode all exit 2 without reaching the stub. All 31 release tests,
Bash syntax validation, repository build and website build pass. Existing
publication and recovery guards remain unchanged. The Changesets/implementation
references and CLI patch changeset document the publisher script's no-argument
contract and absence of its own dry-run mode.

Release-validator argument parsing now requires exactly one supported mode.
Previously it selected the first --mode argument and silently ignored extra
flags, positional arguments and competing later modes. A failing regression
uses an empty non-repository directory and verifies eight malformed invocation
shapes report usage before any Git error. The full 30-test release-validator
suite passes, including publish, branch/tag, version-PR and recovery guards;
the repository build passes too. The Changesets reference and CLI patch
changeset document the stricter invocation contract. No release mode, branch
restriction or publication permission was relaxed.

Release metadata review found three pending audit changesets named bundled MCP
or sync work without an explicit CLI entry at the required severity. Those
uncommitted entries now include CLI coverage. A new validator rule derives
bundled private modules from committed CLI internal export targets and rejects
missing or weaker CLI entries even when another public package is present.
A failing-before regression covers missing, weaker, matching and higher CLI
severity; all 29 release-validator tests and the repository build pass. The
Changesets working-tree preview and a separate ownership check now accept all
310 pending changesets. The release preflight itself correctly refused this
audit branch; its main/reachability/committed-input guards remain unchanged, and
this local preview is not proof of release readiness. Changeset and
implementation references plus a CLI patch changeset document the rule.

CLI consolidation now checks literal runtime imports in the published dist/src
and dist/internal trees against CLI production, optional and peer dependencies.
This prevents a private workspace's development dependency from silently being
omitted in the public package. Diagnostics name the importing file and missing
package root. Syntax-tree traversal covers static imports/re-exports, dynamic
string/template imports, require and require.resolve; comments, strings,
unrelated object methods and excluded compiled tests do not create false
dependencies. An initial preprocessing-scanner trial falsely treated
client.require as a load and was replaced before completion. Three fixture
tests cover rejection and allowed boundaries; the actual consolidated build
passes. All 1,499 repository tests across 24 summaries pass with zero failures,
cancellations or skips; packed smoke and website build pass. The CLI and
implementation references document scope and the remaining role of installed
checks, and a CLI patch changeset records the enhancement.

Report code-block parsing now recognizes handwritten GFM footnote containers.
The preceding CommonMark-only boundary pass mistakenly left a continued
footnote paragraph's inline splice inert. A failing regression established the
problem; the paired mdast/micromark footnote extensions now distinguish that
paragraph from an indented code example nested inside the same footnote. Both
space and tab indentation are covered, and rendered GFM checks confirm the
handwritten footnote survives with unchanged nested code and one expanded
paragraph splice. All 68 view tests, 119 CLI tests, repository/website builds
and packed smoke checks pass with the existing API snapshot. The extensions
are explicit view development and CLI production dependencies. The view and
implementation references and a CLI/view patch changeset record the fix;
earlier performance measurements are explicitly identified as predating these
extensions.

The new report parser passes all ten existing fixed performance gates, run
without concurrent build/test workloads. Those gates do not cover parsing or
CLI startup, so separate checks measured both. Nine alternating fresh-process
source-entry help runs yielded 165.7 ms median normally and 148.5 ms with a throwing parser
stub substituted by a module-resolution hook; output/exit remained identical.
The hook's own overhead prevents treating the difference as an exact isolated
import timer. Five repeated report calls on one store yielded 5.7 ms median
for 1,000 indented examples and 50.2 ms for 10,000, each followed by one live
splice; every run verified intact examples, one citation and no problems.
The view reference records runtime, method and limitations. Eager parser
loading is retained; no broader startup or parsing budget is claimed. A
CLI/view patch changeset accompanies the measured decision.

Indented report code examples now remain inert. A failing regression preceded
the fix; `mdast-util-from-markdown` supplies code-block line boundaries, while
the renderer retains original template text and existing cave-q fence handling.
Coverage includes tabs, blank lines, list/blockquote containers and transitions
back to live prose; indented paragraph and list continuations remain live.
Seven rendered GFM cases confirm unchanged code elements and live continuations.
All 67 view tests, 119 CLI tests (including book sessions), repository/website
builds and packed smoke checks pass against the existing API snapshot. The
parser is an explicit production dependency of the CLI and a development
dependency of its private view workspace. The view and implementation references
and a CLI/view patch changeset record the design. The fixed bug file and index
entry are removed.

Report code-span review found CommonMark removed one leading and trailing space
from fully bound default bullets using stored raw claim text. A failing
regression now covers one and two surrounding spaces; code-span generation
adds the padding CommonMark consumes, preserving the authored whitespace.
All 65 view tests and repository/website builds pass, and a GFM render confirms
the exact two-space boundaries inside the resulting code element. The view
reference and CLI/view patch changeset document the fix. This pass also
reproduced splices executing inside indented Markdown code examples. That
separate parser defect was subsequently fixed with parsed code-block boundaries
and paragraph/list coverage, as recorded above.

Report source citations previously decoded embedded newlines directly into
Markdown labels, splitting a footnote into multiple physical lines. A failing
regression demonstrated a three-line footnote. Labels now display C0/DEL and
Unicode line-separator controls as visible escapes while stored identities and
encoded HTTP(S) destinations remain unchanged. Coverage exercises local code
spans and HTTP links; a GFM rendering check verifies one footnote, literal
newline escapes, and the original encoded URL. All 64 view tests, report CLI
checks, the full CLI package suite, repository/website builds and packed smoke
tests pass. An initial broad direct-node test filter also selected the known
doctor environment check, which found system pnpm 9.12.3; it passes under the
repository-managed CLI test script. The view reference and CLI/view patch
changeset document citation escaping. Source syntax, public signatures and
book examples are unchanged.

The follow-up declaration audit found no other system-generated verb detection
using sync's former historical-row predicate. Connector source declarations
intentionally choose the newest surviving positive claim per attribute across
source series, unlike action/automation declaration winner selection. Existing
discovery coverage exercises fallback to a root declaration after a followed
source retracts its own series. An additional direct check verified that
retracting both path series removes discovery; a file-backed assembly check
verified that removing the last path does not retire already imported data.
The connector reference and source comments now state these boundaries rather
than implying any single path retraction globally removes the source. All 107
connector tests and repository/website builds pass. A CLI/connect patch
changeset records the clarification; runtime and normative semantics are
unchanged.

Sync merge-event declaration detection used a historical-row existence check,
which mistook conditional `SYNCED-INTO IS verb` claims for active vocabulary.
A failing regression demonstrated the missing top-level declaration. Detection
now uses the store registry. The regression covers WHEN/VIA/BECAUSE through
both annotated-text and database merges, checks dry-run rollback of rows and
vocabulary, and verifies repeat merges append nothing. All 44 sync tests and
seven matching CLI command tests pass; repository/website builds and the
packed-artifact smoke checks pass with the existing API snapshot. The sync
reference documents the condition boundary and rollback behavior; its entrypoint
description now distinguishes matching IDs from conflicting identity reuse.
A CLI/sync patch changeset accompanies the fix. Existing specification and
book semantics remain unchanged.

The accumulated external-record validation changes pass a fresh integration
checkpoint: repository build, all 1,490 tests across 24 package summaries
(zero failures, cancellations or skips), and installed-package smoke tests.
The book's runnable CLI sessions pass in that full suite. Packed imports pass
both NodeNext and Bundler checks against the existing reviewed API snapshot;
the installed CLI exercises backup/restore, reports, ingestion, MCP, derivation,
resolution, reconstruction, sync, automation, HTTP serving and highlighting.
The website production build also passes. Query documentation now states that
display formatting retains the finite unrounded value when rounding would
overflow; existing core regressions cover this fallback. No additional decoder
runtime change was justified by this pass. A query patch changeset records the
documentation and verification checkpoint.

Playground results now capture and display the submitted valid-time setting,
including empty results and unfiltered queries. A browser regression delays
worker submission, edits the date, then confirms the completed result retains
its original anchor and interpolated value. Existing coverage also checks the
label on out-of-coverage empty results. All 37 browser tests, 20 runtime/client
tests and the production build pass. The website reference and a core patch
changeset document the behavior.

Valid-time playground recovery coverage now verifies dated transitive queries
report the shared engine restriction and recover after clearing the anchor.
The worker-crash regression uses a non-default 2027 anchor and confirms rebuild
preserves edited claims and returns 400 people rather than the sample's 2026
midpoint. Both affected browser tests and the production build pass; no runtime
fix was needed. The website reference and a core patch changeset document the
restriction and retained query settings. The complete suite remains 36 tests.

Playground valid-time support adds an optional labelled anchor field, passes it
through the worker/client protocol to shared query options, and provides a
Changing headcount sample anchored at 2026. Browser coverage checks interpolated
endpoints/midpoint, out-of-coverage dates, unanchored trajectory text, invalid-date
recovery, Enter submission and resetting the anchor on sample changes. An initial
layout failure exposed the fixed query-row height; content-sized grid rows now
keep Run query clear of the result header. The mobile screenshot was inspected.
All 36 browser tests, 20 runtime/client tests and the production build pass.
The website reference and a core patch changeset document the feature.

SQLite WebAssembly record verification exercises the actual injected SQL.js
adapter with scalar/approximate uncertainty, trajectory, date, atom, literal
and oversized-number claims. Every claim/query record round-trips through the
shared decoders, computed 549.995 retains rounded `550 req/s` text, and a
corrupted nested scalar projection is rejected. No adapter change was needed.
All 20 website runtime/client tests and the production build pass. The website
reference and a store patch changeset record the cross-adapter verification.

Uncertainty-domain review reproduced zero/negative and nonscalar decoded deltas
passing despite authored CAVE requiring a positive finite scalar. Decoding now
applies that requirement after raw-value consistency checks. Object/JSON tests
reject zero, negative, atom, trajectory, oversized and literal deltas; small
positive and approximate unit-bearing deltas remain valid. All 131 store and
101 query tests plus workspace/website builds pass. The store reference and a
minor changeset document agreement with the authored uncertainty rule.

Nested query-evidence verification confirms the stronger claim value decoder
applies to both direct claims and support arrays. Separate stored scalar-with-
uncertainty and trajectory fixtures reject corrupted projections in object and
JSON envelopes, while valid supporting records round-trip. No additional
runtime change was needed. All 101 query tests and workspace/website builds
pass; the query reference and a patch changeset document nested consistency.

Interpolation record review confirmed a deliberate distinction from stored
value projections: `at.num` keeps computed precision while `at.text` and value
bindings use formatted display precision. A real trajectory regression preserves
549.995 beside `550 req/s` through encoding/decoding. Exact equality between
parsed display text and the numeric field would reject this valid result, so
that check was not added. All 100 query tests and workspace/website builds pass.
The query reference and a patch changeset document this precision boundary.

Value-projection consistency now reparses decoded attribute, metric and delta
values with the same core parser/literal constructors used for stored values.
Kind, approximation, scalar, endpoints and units must match raw spelling.
Regressions reject altered projections in object/JSON input across scalars,
approximation, trajectories, atoms and literals; a 400-digit authored value
still round-trips without a finite numeric projection. All 130 store, 99 query
and 56 scenario tests plus workspace/website builds pass. The store reference
and a minor changeset record the stronger contract, resolving the numeric
mismatch exposed in the preceding reference review.

Record-reference review replaces the ambiguous claim of transaction-identity
verification with the actual local checks: UUIDv7 syntax and recomputed key/
canonical text. A field table consolidates decoder requirements. A direct
runtime probe confirms remaining semantic gaps: changing a numeric projection
from 42 to 99 without changing raw text, or supplying independent provenance
dimensions, survived structural decoding at that point. Numeric projection
consistency was subsequently addressed by the value-projection pass. The website build and bundled-doc link
browser check pass; a store patch changeset records the corrected reference.

Shape-index integration verification passed all 1,485 workspace tests across
24 summaries, with no failures, cancellations or skips. Executable book examples
passed in 41.3 seconds. Packed smoke passed without an API snapshot refresh,
all 35 production browser tests passed in 49.3 seconds, and the fixed performance
benchmark passed after other workloads finished. This checks the narrower fact
projection and selective observed indexes across shipped consumers, alongside
recent claim-record validation. It does not close larger shape-gate scaling or
the remaining review scope above.

Selective shape indexing now derives required attribute names and primary
relation directions from active expectations, avoiding unused taxonomy relation
indexes while retaining the taxonomy target graph. A mixed regression covers
attributes, forward/inverse checks sharing a primary, explicit IS/EXTENDS
expectations and retraction of only the forward edge. The sequential shaped
benchmark measured 11.61 s at 1,000 events versus the prior 12.39 s projection-
only result, with exact outputs and zero quiet writes. All 98 shape, 33 action
and 61 automation tests plus workspace/website builds pass. The references and
a CLI/shape patch changeset document the optimization and measurement limits;
full-evaluation scaling remains open.

Populated-shape CPU profiling attributed 9.24 of 18.52 sampled seconds to the
fact snapshot reader, including native SQLite work attributed to its caller.
The positive-fact query already filters confidence and negation; removing those
two redundant projected columns and duplicate index checks reduced a sequential
1,000-event shaped benchmark from the prior 14.21 s baseline to 12.39 s, with
all correctness/quiet-cycle assertions passing. Latest-history predicates and
complete declaration rows are preserved. All 97 shape, 33 action and 61 automation
tests, plus workspace/website builds, pass. The shape and automation references
document the narrower projection and measurement limits; the older 4,000-event
table is explicitly identified as predating this change. A CLI/shape patch
changeset records the optimization. Full-evaluation scaling remains open.

Populated-shape allocation trial deferred sorting/copying observed units until
violations were reported. Sequential benchmark runs measured 14.21 s before
and 14.19 s after at 1,000 shaped events, with all correctness and quiet-cycle
checks passing. This did not establish a material workload improvement, so the
runtime trial was reverted. A retained regression verifies sorted distinct unit
diagnostics, successful correction and immutability of earlier diagnostic
arrays. All 97 shape tests and workspace/website builds pass. The automation
reference records the rejected optimization; repeated populated evaluations
remain the higher-value scaling target. A CLI/shape patch changeset records
the verification and finding.

Large automation review adds `bench:automation --large`, optionally combined
with `--shapes`, for 1,000/2,000/4,000 events. Both modes ran separately and
verified exact ready/handled sets, action counts, zero quiet writes and, with
shapes, every owner and final constraint. Active times were 0.79/2.38/8.55 s
without shapes and 14.45/57.00/231.31 s with shapes; quiet cycles stayed below
50 ms. Populated shape gates show approximately quadratic growth in this
fixture, so affected-constraint checking remains an optimization opportunity
requiring preserved rejection/rollback behavior. The live reference consolidates
current commands and measurements, replacing intermediate optimization history.
Duplicate/unknown flags fail before fixtures, and the website build passes.
A CLI/automation patch changeset records the benchmark enhancement.

Optional claim metadata review reproduced invalid sigma levels and malformed
uncertainty values surviving canonical identity checks. Decoding now validates
delta value fields, positive finite numeric sigma levels and string comments.
Regressions exercise matching emitted spellings in object/JSON input and a real
measured claim with units, uncertainty, sigma and comment. All 129 store tests,
99 query tests and workspace/website builds pass. The store reference and a
minor changeset record the validated optional metadata contract.

Claim payload review reproduced unknown payload kinds and malformed attribute/
metric value fields passing with recomputed semantic identity. Payloads now
require supported discriminants, string attribute names, supported value kinds,
string raw text, Boolean approximation and typed optional units/finite numeric
fields. Object/JSON regressions cover coerced names, invalid kinds/types and
nonfinite values; real stored claims round-trip all six value kinds and bare
existence. All 128 store tests, 99 query tests and workspace/website builds pass.
The store reference and a minor changeset document structural validation;
optional numeric projections remain optional.

Claim term review reproduced unsupported/missing kinds and nonstring text
passing decoding when semantic identity was recomputed. Subject and relation
object terms now require entity/text/code kinds and string text. Object/JSON
regressions cover both positions with matching keys and emitted text; all three
valid term kinds round-trip. All 126 store tests, 99 query tests and workspace/
website builds pass. The store reference and a minor changeset record this
validation boundary without changing valid serialized records.

Integration verification of record-decoding checks, asynchronous evaluator
coverage, overlay filters and documentation navigation passed all 1,479 workspace
tests across 24 summaries, with no failures, cancellations or skips. Executable
book examples passed in 41.1 seconds. Packed smoke passed with the existing
public API snapshot, and all 35 production browser tests passed in 52.0 seconds.
This verifies the accumulated changes across current consumers without closing
the remaining review scope above.

Claim tag review reproduced malformed fields passing canonical identity checks
through string coercion, including numeric keys/values, missing keys and null
values. Tags now require objects with string keys and optional string values
before canonical comparison. Object/JSON regressions use matching coerced
canonical spellings to demonstrate that identity alone is insufficient; valid
flat and scoped tags remain decodable. All 125 store tests, 99 query tests and
workspace/website builds pass. The store reference and a minor changeset record
the tag decoding contract.

Claim-record review reproduced sparse provenance arrays bypassing the shared
string-array validator. The validator now visits every slot, covering contexts
and all four provenance dimensions. Tests reject holes, undefined, null and
numeric entries, compare object/JSON provenance decoding, and preserve empty
and valid dimensions. All 124 store tests, 99 query tests and workspace/website
builds pass. The store reference and a minor changeset record dense string
arrays as the decoding contract; serialized valid records remain unchanged.

Query support-array review reproduced sparse object arrays bypassing nested
claim decoding because array mapping skipped holes. Decoding now visits every
slot and rejects absent evidence, consistently with JSON's null representation
of those holes. Regressions use a real claim record and cover isolated/mixed
holes, undefined/null entries, empty support and valid support. All 99 query
tests and workspace/website builds pass. The query reference documents dense
support arrays and a minor changeset records the validation tightening.

Query-record review reproduced the decoder accepting malformed interpolation
metadata. Supplied `at` metadata now requires an object with a finite numeric
value, string text and a string unit when present. Object and JSON regressions
reject null, arrays, missing fields, nonfinite/nonnumeric values and invalid
text/units; a real 250-people interpolation round-trips with its claim record.
All 98 query tests and workspace/website builds pass. The query reference and
a minor changeset record the runtime validation tightening; public types and
valid serialized records are unchanged.

Mobile documentation filter review reproduced clearing a narrowed list leaving
the active page offscreen again without a route change. A results-change effect
now adjusts only the navigation's horizontal scroll when the active page is
present, preserving filter focus and vertical position. The new browser
regression failed before the change and passes afterward; all ten documentation
browser checks and the production build pass. The website reference and a core
patch changeset document the behavior. The browser suite now contains 35 tests;
this pass ran the ten affected documentation checks.

Documentation navigation review reproduced direct routes leaving the active
page offscreen in the scrolling list. Page/fragment navigation now reveals the
active entry before setting article position and focus. A browser regression
checks horizontal mobile and vertical desktop navigation, article heading
focus and document scroll position, allowing CSS-pixel rounding. The production
build and all 34 browser tests pass, including existing section-link/history
and keyboard-filter behavior. The website reference and a core patch changeset
document the improvement.

Scenario documentation now includes a complete mixed-unit reduction example
with imports, store creation/cleanup, target-unit selection, a directed exact
conversion and an asserted 1,500 ms result. The exact TypeScript block extracted
from the README executed successfully against workspace packages. The opening
overlay example now names its required existing store and claim. The rebuilt
website and bundled-documentation link browser check pass; no runtime source
or public API change was needed. A scenario patch changeset records the example.

Pending evaluator review found the previous timeout-labelled regression threw
synchronously. New coverage blocks an asynchronous evaluator on a controlled
promise, verifies that overlay history is absent while it remains pending,
writes through a fresh store transaction, then verifies those writes survive
both evaluator resolution and rejection. No runtime change was needed. The
reference now explicitly assigns deadlines/cancellation to the evaluator and
documents that `run` forwards its outcome without holding an overlay transaction.
All 56 scenario tests and workspace/website builds pass; a patch changeset
records this stronger verification and clarified contract.

Overlay filter review adds stored/hypothetical parity coverage for confidence,
scoped tags, contexts, numeric units, combined filters and empty matches. Values
and authored confidence agree, overlay evidence contains only stable scenario
IDs, and success or failed unit conversion leaves the hypothetical store with
zero current or historical claim rows. No runtime correction was needed for
these cases. All 55 scenario tests and workspace/website builds pass. The
scenario reference records the shared-filter and rollback boundary, with a
patch changeset for the added verification and documentation.

Integration verification of scenario selection validation, numeric selected-slot
handling and reduction-unit consistency passed all 1,472 workspace tests across
24 package summaries, with no failures, cancellations or skips. Executable book
sessions passed in 41.7 seconds. Packed smoke passed with the existing public API
snapshot, including installed NodeNext/Bundler type checks and CLI workflows.
All 33 production browser tests passed in 48.7 seconds against the rebuilt site,
covering bundled documentation links, mobile navigation and playground recovery.
These checks verify the recent changes across consumers; the remaining system
review scope above is unchanged.

Scenario reduction review reproduced mixed-unit sums and comparisons accepting
raw magnitudes without a common unit. Numeric sum/min/max now reject differing
units after conversion with `incompatible-unit`, including unitless/unit-bearing
mixtures. Regressions cover both candidate orders and both numeric kinds,
explicit seconds-to-milliseconds conversion, common inferred units and unitless
inputs; `all` still retains individual units. All 54 scenario tests and
workspace/website builds pass. The live reference explains when conversions
