are required, and a patch changeset records the behavior correction.

Scenario numeric selection review reproduced a subject selection returning the
row's numeric attribute instead: `system HAS size: 8` selected as `system`
silently became integer 8. Numeric conversion now uses the selected binding,
and row uncertainty is attached only when selecting the attribute value slot.
Regressions cover invalid nonnumeric subjects, numeric subjects with unrelated
attribute uncertainty in both stored and overlay claims, and valid-time
interpolation that changes the value slot without replacing the subject.
All 51 scenario tests and workspace/website builds pass. The scenario reference
and a patch changeset document the corrected contract. Inspection also confirmed
that literal decoding should not unescape backslashes: CAVE's tokenizer defines
no literal escape sequences, so the existing delimiter removal is appropriate.

Scenario selection review reproduced an optional input silently accepting an
unbound `select` on an empty snapshot and accessing a closed database before
reporting the definition error. Supplied selections now require a string naming
a variable in the parsed query before reads. Regressions cover misspellings,
leading question marks, empty and non-string selections for text and Boolean
inputs; subject, verb, object and attribute value selections and omitted Boolean
existence selections remain valid. All 49 scenario tests, the workspace build
and the website build pass. The scenario reference documents the contract and
a minor changeset records the validation tightening.

Dense limited-discovery verification adds `bench:alias-limit`: 512 separator
variants produce 130,816 matching pairs. Full output and the best-20 run have
identical prefix digests. With identical Node settings, local time/peak resident
memory were 281 ms/251 MiB full and 212 ms/129 MiB limited; a separate limited
run also passed with V8 old-space capped at 128 MiB. The reference consolidates
the current algorithm, separate candidate/output costs, reproducible commands
and measurements instead of retaining intermediate optimization history.
Integration of bounded result retention and scenario time/enum/Boolean/unit
validation passed all 1,464 workspace tests across 24 summaries, with no
failures, cancellations or skips, including executable book sessions. Packed
smoke passed without an API snapshot refresh; website build and bundled-link
browser verification passed, as did all ten unchanged performance thresholds.

Scenario conversion review found that duplicate directed unit pairs selected
the first factor, making numeric inputs depend on declaration order. Conversion
definitions now require an array of valid entries, non-empty string endpoints,
unique directed pairs and positive exact rational factors. Regressions reject
conflicting pairs in both orders and malformed lists, holes, endpoints, factors
and identical duplicates before reads. Existing exact value/uncertainty
conversion also verifies that a reciprocal pair remains valid. All 46 scenario
tests and workspace/website builds pass. The scenario reference explains this
boundary and a minor changeset records the validation tightening; public types
and valid conversion results are unchanged.

Scenario Boolean review reproduced identical true/false mappings silently
returning true. Definitions now require supplied mappings to be strings and
their effective values to differ after applying defaults. Regressions reject
explicit overlap, one-sided collisions with default true/false, null/numeric
mappings and overlapping empty strings before reads, and verify real yes/no
binding plus a valid distinct empty-string mapping. All 44 scenario tests and
workspace/website builds pass. The scenario reference documents the mapping
contract, and a minor changeset records the validation tightening. Public
signatures and valid Boolean binding results remain unchanged.

Scenario enum review reproduced the string domain `"product"` accepting
`"prod"` through substring matching instead of exact enum membership. Domains
now require a non-empty dense array of unique strings before database access.
Regressions reject missing/null/string/set domains, holes, non-string entries
and duplicates on a closed store, and exercise the real substring case, exact
case sensitivity and a deliberately allowed empty string. All 42 scenario
tests and workspace/website builds pass. The scenario reference explains the
domain contract; a minor changeset records the intentional validation
tightening. Public signatures and valid enum behavior remain unchanged.

Scenario time review reproduced an empty binding set accepting impossible
valid-time dates; invalid transaction boundaries also reached the database
before validation. Both optional anchors now validate their string type and
shared parser result before any database read. Regressions cover malformed and
non-string anchors on a closed store, empty scenarios, valid period/timestamp
anchors, UUID rejection for valid time, and year/month start semantics against
dated facts. All 40 scenario tests and workspace/website builds pass. The
scenario reference now distinguishes inclusive transaction-time periods from
valid-time start instants. A minor changeset records the validation tightening;
valid examples and public signatures are unchanged.

Limited alias discovery previously collected every suggestion before slicing.
A bounded max-heap now retains only the requested best results while scoring;
unlimited calls keep their ordinary array and stable sort. Encounter ordinals
preserve ties when both score and locale comparison are equal. Regressions
compare limited output with the exact unlimited prefix across more than 2,016
dense matches, several limits through the maximum safe integer, and canonical
Unicode-equivalent names whose score/name comparisons all tie. All 96 shape
tests, five focused CLI suggestion tests, workspace and website builds, the
alias benchmark's output checks and ten unchanged performance thresholds pass.
The shape reference explains bounded retained output and the unchanged need
to compare all candidate pairs; public signatures and ranking are unchanged.

Larger alias verification adds a reproducible `--large` benchmark mode at
1,000/2,000/4,000 unrelated names. Running it alone with V8 old-space limited
to 128 MiB passed complete-output invariance at every size, with the same four
suggestions and digest in 404/1,633/6,774 ms. The shape reference distinguishes
that V8 limit from total/native memory and records the still-quadratic time.
Integration of group-based pair deduplication, governance-field validation and
playground lifecycle changes passed all 1,453 workspace tests across 24 package
summaries, with no failures, cancellations or skips, including executable book
sessions. Packed smoke passed without an API snapshot refresh, all 33 browser
tests passed, and all ten unchanged performance thresholds passed. Remaining
system review scope above stays open.

Alias candidate deduplication retained a string key for every compared pair.
Each pair now belongs to its first shared candidate group, using per-name
group memberships instead of the all-pairs `seen` set. An overlap regression
combines first-character, suffix, tokens, two rare values and reordered names,
requiring exactly one suggestion per pair and unchanged limited ranking.
The 250/500/1,000-name benchmark retained its exact output digest and measured
44/103/448 ms versus 43/140/676 ms before the change. All 94 shape tests, five
focused CLI suggestion tests, workspace and website builds, and ten unchanged
performance thresholds pass. The shape reference explains the storage bound
and the remaining quadratic comparison/output cases. Public signatures and
candidate-selection semantics remain unchanged.

Scenario governance recording accepted missing required payloads and audit
metadata. Entry points now require recommendation value, decision selection
and action parameters, allow explicit JSON null, require non-empty decider,
action-name and effect-kind strings, and enforce the declared action/effect
status choices. Eight field-boundary subtests require TypeError and unchanged
full store exports on invalid records; accepted null payloads and every valid
status round-trip through recorded artifacts. All 37 scenario tests and
workspace/website builds pass. The scenario reference lists the runtime
requirements and preserves optional metadata and transactional predecessor
checks. A minor changeset records the validation tightening; existing reads
and public TypeScript signatures are unchanged.

Late playground worker errors still invoked failure callbacks after intentional
closure or an earlier fatal reply. Regressions reproduced both spurious shutdown
errors and three callbacks for one fatal failure. Error and unreadable-message
handlers now ignore closed runtimes, preserving the original failure exactly
once. All 19 website unit/runtime tests, three focused production browser
recovery checks, and workspace/website builds pass. The website reference
documents quiet intentional closure and single-notification fatal failure;
pending-request rejection and replacement-worker recovery remain covered.

Pending playground recovery verification now injects a fatal request reply
after editing claims during the wait. Busy state clears, query/append remain
disabled until rebuild, the replacement worker preserves the edited source,
and its next query returns that source's entity. All three focused worker
recovery browser checks pass. A client regression also closes simultaneous
open/append/query requests, requires all three to reject, verifies empty pending
bookkeeping after late replies and rejects new requests on the closed runtime.
All 18 website unit/runtime tests and the workspace build pass. No production
fix was required; the website reference records these lifecycle guarantees.

Playground operation review found that query and append controls remained
available with no progress message while worker requests were pending. The
page now announces the operation, exposes the active button's busy state and
temporarily disables query, append, rebuild and dataset selection. A synchronous
ref guard also blocks repeated Enter presses before React commits a render.
Editors remain usable, and completion clears pending state on both success and
failure. A browser regression withholds worker requests to verify exactly one
submission, progress text and control recovery, including an injected error.
All 33 production browser tests, 17 website unit/runtime tests and the production
build pass. The website reference documents this behavior and existing worker
crash/rebuild checks remain green.

Integration after scenario identifier and evaluation-record validation, alias
name caching and bounded edit distance, and flexible documentation filtering
passed the workspace build and all 1,441 tests across 24 package summaries
with no failures, cancellations or skips. The executable book sessions passed
against the real CLI. Packed smoke required no API snapshot refresh, the fresh
website passed all 32 browser tests, and all ten performance thresholds stayed
unchanged and passed. The alias benchmark also passed its complete-output
invariance checks. This checkpoint preserves the remaining review scope above.

Website documentation filtering missed `solver z3` and reordered page-label
words because it required one exact substring. Filtering now requires every
normalized query word to appear across the label and slug, regardless of order,
and normalizes case, separators and Unicode compatibility forms. The browser
regression failed before the change and now verifies `solver z3`, `z3 solver`,
underscore and full-width forms, reordered labels, result announcements and
keyboard activation with destination-heading focus at a mobile width. All 32
production browser tests, 17 website unit/runtime tests and the production
build pass. The website reference documents matching behavior; clear-filter
focus, current-page indication and route state remain covered.

Alias edit-distance review replaced full pairwise matrices with a bounded
diagonal search using the existing 0.75 similarity threshold. Length and
row-minimum rejection stop pairs that cannot qualify; qualifying distances
and scores remain exact. A full-matrix reference agrees across exhaustive
short binary strings, Unicode examples and every tested distance limit.
The deterministic 250/500/1,000-name benchmark measured 49/146/671 ms after
this change versus 69/245/1,095 ms with name caching alone, preserving the
complete four-suggestion output and digest at every size. All 93 shape tests,
five focused CLI suggestion tests, workspace and website builds, and ten
unchanged performance thresholds pass. The shape reference records the
algorithm, reproduction and remaining quadratic candidate-pair count; matching
semantics and public signatures are unchanged.

Alias discovery performance review measured repeated normalization, digit
stripping and tokenization inside pair comparisons. A per-call name-feature
map now serves grouping and scoring without retaining data across calls.
The new `bench:aliases` workload keeps fixed spelling, version and rare-value
evidence while adding 250/500/1,000 unrelated names in a common candidate group.
It requires the complete suggestions to equal the reference without noise.
Local before/after times were 115/414/1,780 ms and 69/245/1,095 ms; all three
sizes retained the same four suggestions and output digest. All 92 shape tests,
five focused CLI suggestion tests, workspace and website builds, and ten
unchanged performance thresholds pass; the new package benchmark command also
passes. The shape reference documents measurements, reproduction and the
remaining quadratic pair count. Public signatures and matching semantics are
unchanged.

External evaluation recording accepted missing/non-string evaluator identity,
omitted output and modified scenario inputs retaining their old digest. All
three cases reproduced durable writes before the fix. Recording now requires
non-empty string name/version, explicit output (including valid null), and the
same input content-digest verification used by solver explanation construction.
Regressions require zero appended rows on rejection and exact readback of valid
evaluations. All 28 scenario tests, workspace and website builds, and packed
smoke pass without an API snapshot refresh. The scenario reference describes
these checks and correction under a new result ID; a minor changeset records
the validation tightening. Existing artifact reads and public types are unchanged.

Scenario identifier review reproduced numeric `1` and string `"1"` bypassing
duplicate-ID detection and addressing the same bound-value slot. Regular
expression coercion also accepted missing or boxed identifiers and boxed model
digests. Validation now requires strings before regex checks and validates each
binding before adding its ID to the duplicate set. Regressions reject numeric,
Boolean, null, missing, array, boxed, symbol and custom-coercion IDs before any
database access, and preserve valid string names including `"1"`, `"undefined"`
and `"constructor"`. All 25 scenario tests and workspace/website builds pass.
The scenario reference and a minor changeset document the tightened runtime
boundary; public types and valid book examples are unchanged.

Integration after client relation snapshots, alias-judge evidence and reply
parsing, and scenario recording schema checks passed all 1,435 workspace tests
across 24 package summaries with no failures, cancellations or skips. The real
CLI's executable book sessions passed. Packed smoke required no API snapshot
refresh, and the rebuilt website passed its bundled-documentation link check.
This evidence covers these changes together without closing the remaining
system review scope.

Scenario recording review reproduced an action artifact passed to
`Record.result` being persisted without its decision predecessor. Recording
entry points now enforce their accepted schemas before opening a transaction;
result accepts solver results and external evaluations, and the other methods
accept only their own artifact kind. Regression coverage exercises all five
entry points with mismatched, unknown, missing and non-object inputs and
requires zero transactions and rows. All 23 scenario tests pass, including the
existing complete governance workflows; workspace and website builds, packed
smoke without an API snapshot refresh, and the browser's bundled-documentation
link check also pass. The scenario reference documents this runtime boundary,
and a minor changeset records the intentional validation tightening.

Alias-judge reply review reproduced a false confirmation from `["[1]"]`:
the parser selected an inner bracket span instead of the complete JSON array.
Balanced, quote-aware array scanning now consumes valid outer arrays before
filtering numeric entries, while retaining recovery after malformed prose and
the last-well-formed-array rule. Regressions cover nested entries, escaped
quotes and backslashes, quoted closing brackets, later empty confirmations,
and incomplete prose. A real shell-judge CLI write regression verifies zero
appends and an unchanged full store export. All 92 shape tests, five focused
CLI suggestion tests, and workspace/website builds pass. The shape reference
and §27.4 specification clarify entry handling; public signatures and valid
book examples remain unchanged.

Alias-judge review reproduced evidence mixing one name's old city with the
other name's new city, although both city claims changed in one peer commit.
Prompt construction now holds one read snapshot across all current-claim
evidence reads and releases it before any external judge runs. Real read-only
WAL coverage verifies the original complete prompt and the next complete state;
read-failure cleanup, caller rollback and database-free empty prompts also have
regressions. All 91 shape tests and four focused CLI suggestion tests pass,
including shell-judge filtering and errors, as do the workspace and website
builds. The shape reference distinguishes consistent current evidence from
retained discovery scores/comments and the existing reserved history recheck.
Public signatures and book examples are unchanged.

Generated-client review reproduced a schema combining an older cardinality
with a newly committed inverse mapping. Declaration metadata was consistent,
but its read savepoint ended before relation lookup refreshed the verb registry.
Normalization now retains one read savepoint through both phases. A real
read-only WAL regression commits the inverse declaration and cardinality update
together; generation retains the earlier complete schema and observes both
changes on the next call. A separate injected read failure and caller rollback
check verify snapshot cleanup and transaction ownership. All 88 shape tests,
the workspace build, all ten unchanged performance thresholds and the production
website build pass. The imported shape reference explains this boundary; public
signatures and ordinary generated output remain unchanged.

Integration after the health, evaluation and declaration snapshot fixes, WASM
transaction checks and client field-identity correction passed the workspace
build and all 1,427 tests across 24 package summaries, with no failures,
cancellations or skips. Executable book sessions passed against the real CLI.
Packed smoke passed without an API snapshot refresh, all ten performance
measurements met unchanged thresholds, and the rebuilt production website
passed all 31 browser tests. The imported shape reference includes the snapshot
and field-identity explanations. This checkpoint leaves the remaining review
scope above open.

Client field identity joined type, kind and property names with NUL separators,
so two valid, distinct declarations could trigger a false conflict. Identity
now encodes the complete tuple as JSON. The regression failed before the fix
and all 86 shape tests now pass, including strict NodeNext compilation of the
generated module containing these names. The shape reference documents this
boundary; public signatures, ordinary generated output and book examples are
unchanged.

Declaration-only shape reads could mix an older declaration row with newly
committed qualifier edges, hiding an expectation even though both committed
states contained one. The shared metadata reader now wraps all three reads
in a read savepoint. A real read-only WAL regression revises cardinality and
qualifies the older row in one peer transaction; listing retains the earlier
expectation for its current call and observes the revised one on the next.
All 85 shape and 17 website runtime tests, the workspace build, and all ten
unchanged performance thresholds pass. The shape reference documents the
metadata boundary used by listing and client generation; public signatures
are unchanged.

Alternate-runtime snapshot verification exercises the real shape library with
the website's sql.js adapter. It confirms health/evaluation results, complete
export preservation after gate rejection and caller rollback, and usable writes
after malformed-declaration errors from both read APIs. All 17 website runtime
tests and the production build pass. The website reference identifies this as
adapter coverage, not a new playground control. No production or public API
change was needed.

Standalone shape evaluation concurrency review reproduced a false violation
when a peer revoked an expectation and added a typed instance between the
declaration and fact reads. Evaluation now uses a read savepoint for its whole
result. A real read-only WAL regression requires the earlier snapshot to remain
unchanged, then observes the revocation on the next call. Nested health-report
and gate paths retain their outer transactions. All 84 shape, 63 view, 33 action,
and 61 automation tests and the workspace build pass; all ten unchanged
performance thresholds pass. The shape reference documents the snapshot
boundary. Public signatures and valid book outputs remain unchanged.

Health consistency review reproduced a peer commit between shape evaluation
and coverage producing a report with old instance checks but newer entity and
row counts. Reports now share a read savepoint across all sections. A real
read-only WAL connection regression allows a peer to commit mid-report, requires
the original report snapshot unchanged, and observes the new violation on the
next report. Another regression checks release after malformed declarations
and nesting without committing a caller's pending writes. The first concurrency
test used rollback journaling and correctly blocked the peer commit; it now
explicitly enables WAL to exercise concurrent commits. The shape reference
documents this journal-mode distinction. All 83 shape and 63 view tests and
the workspace build pass. Public signatures and valid book outputs are unchanged.

Health/navigation integration passed all 1,421 workspace tests across 24
package summaries with no failures, cancellations, or skips, including the
executable book sessions. Packed CLI smoke passed without refreshing the API
snapshot, and all ten performance measurements met unchanged thresholds. The
production website rebuilt and all 31 browser tests passed, including article
fragment fallback/scope, repeated-section focus, and native new-tab behavior.
The package references and website guide retain the current health, gate, and
navigation contracts; valid book sessions require no source/PDF change.

Entity coverage now computes distinct mentioned and typed names from one
narrow current-belief read instead of separate subject/object and typing
queries. A regression covers duplicate actor series, quoted subject/object
literals, verb tokens, negative typings, and retired facts, preserving four
mentioned entities and one typed entity. All 81 shape and 63 view tests and
the workspace build pass. A local five-report run over 10,000 claims measured
245.4 ms after the change; prior observations for the separate reads were
337–354 ms, with ordinary run variability. The shape reference documents the
shared read and polarity rules; public signatures are unchanged.

Health coverage review found separate current-belief scans for each counter
and confidence mean. One aggregate now computes facts, positive/negative/
retracted counts, low-confidence count, and the mean; row totals and entity
coverage keep their separate reads. A mixed-history regression confirms only
current versions count, negative beliefs contribute to the mean and low-confidence
count, and retracted beliefs do not. Existing empty-store tests retain zero
counts and a null mean. Five local reports over 10,000 claims measured 406.7 ms
before and 337.3 ms after. All 80 shape and 63 view tests and the workspace
build pass. The shape reference documents aggregate semantics; public signatures
are unchanged.

Inactive-shape gate verification starts with a disabled historical expectation
and an existing instance. Reactivating it without the required value rejects
the batch, preserves the complete annotated export, and removes the batch's
new vocabulary declaration from the registry. Retrying with the required value
in the same batch succeeds and retains the vocabulary. All 79 shape tests and
the workspace build pass. The shape reference documents this gate boundary;
the existing production implementation needed no additional fix.

Inactive shape review reproduced fact snapshots even when every historical
expectation was currently disabled. Evaluation now validates current declaration
and qualifier metadata once, returning early if no active expectations remain.
A regression requires zero fact reads while disabled, observes reactivation
as a real violation on the next evaluation, then stops fact reads after another
retraction. All 78 shape, 33 action, and 61 automation tests and the workspace
build pass. The shape reference documents metadata-first early return and
fresh reactivation checks; active-shape query count and public signatures are
unchanged.

Article-link review confirmed existing click handling restores section focus
when a repeated link emits no hashchange and preserves native modified clicks.
A production regression repeats the current section link, requires focused
visible heading and stable route, then middle-clicks it and verifies the new
tab opens the same section while the original route is preserved. All seven
documentation/section browser checks pass. The website reference records the
behavior. No production change was needed.

Documentation fragment scope review reproduced a link matching the sidebar
filter ID moving focus there and setting its tabindex to -1. Lookup now accepts
targets only within the article, otherwise falling back to its heading. The
browser regression covers absent, malformed, and sidebar-control fragments,
requiring the destination heading to be focused and visible and the search
field to retain its tab sequence. All six documentation browser checks, 16
website unit tests, and the production build pass. The website reference
documents article-scoped fragment focus. No package API or book change applies.

Website keyboard review reproduced stale documentation section links leaving
focus in the sidebar after the destination article changed. Fragment scrolling
now falls back to the document heading when the section is absent or its URI
escape is malformed. A production browser regression clicks both kinds of
links and requires the destination heading to be focused and visible. All 30
browser tests, 16 website unit tests, and the production build pass, including
existing valid-section and browser-history focus checks. The website reference
documents the fallback; no language, package API, or book change is involved.

Snapshot/discovery integration passed all 1,417 workspace tests across 24
package summaries, with no failures, cancellations, or skips, including all
executable book sessions. Packed CLI smoke passed without an API snapshot
refresh. All ten performance checks remain within their unchanged thresholds.
The production website rebuilt and all 29 browser tests passed; built docs
contain the narrower shape snapshot, indexed rule lifecycle, and disabled
automation winner explanations. Review of architecture, implementation, and
book projections found no conflicting behavioral descriptions requiring edits.

Shape snapshots now select taxonomy/typing facts and slots named by active
expectations, canonicalizing inverse relation names to their primary verb.
Each candidate is checked against its complete claim-key history before
accepting current positive values. A regression adds 2,000 unrelated value
facts and reduces the materialized fact snapshot from 2,004 rows to three
without changing evaluation results. The first grouped selection regressed
the shaped benchmark to 16.91 s at 1,000 events; replacing grouping with
indexed latest-version checks measured 14.28 s, with all binding, shape, and
zero-quiet-write assertions passing. All 77 shape, 33 action, and 61 automation
tests and the workspace build pass. The shape reference records the selection
contract and local benchmark; query count and public signatures remain unchanged.

Shape-gate profiling completed all 100/500/1,000-event shaped benchmark checks
and quiet-cycle assertions. Aggregated self samples attributed about 52% to
shapeState, 10% to observedIndexes, and 9% to targetIndexes across 20.2 sampled
seconds. The snapshot percentage includes native synchronous database work
attributed to its caller. The shape reference persists the measurement and
design constraints subsequently implemented above: select only relevant facts, preserving
latest-version, inverse-slot, taxonomy, and qualifier semantics; do not assume
a cross-evaluation cache is safe without write/rollback invalidation. No
production or public API change was made in this profiling pass.

Indexed-discovery integration ran the real rule-to-automation-to-action benchmark
at 100, 500, and 1,000 events in both shape modes. All binding, firing, final
shape, and zero-quiet-write assertions passed. At 1,000 events, active/quiet
cycles measured 757.9/11.2 ms without shapes and 15467.9/14.2 ms with shapes
on Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3, macOS arm64. The automation reference records
the full table and its local-measurement limits; shape evaluation remains the
dominant populated-shape cost. Packed CLI smoke passed without an API snapshot
refresh, verifying the new private rule-discovery helper ships correctly.
The production website rebuilt, and the browser check of every bundled
documentation section target passed.

Automation discovery review found loading, listing, and retraction still
materialized unrelated current beliefs. They now query current declaration
series through indexed attributes (and subject for retraction), retaining
disabled rows until newest-actor winner selection. A regression forbids
whole-store current-belief reads, confirms a newer disabled series hides an
older active declaration, and verifies re-enabling followed by retraction
retires both active series. Ten empty listings over 20,000 unrelated claims
fell locally from 567.4 ms to 0.3 ms. All 61 automation tests and the workspace
build pass. The automation reference documents the retained ownership rules
and indexed discovery; public signatures and semantics are unchanged.

Rule lifecycle discovery now shares the indexed declaration query with
derivation. Listing still filters declarations without values, while retraction
retains its broader positive-declaration selection and write reservation.
Regressions forbid whole-store current-belief materialization, preserve latest
declaration ordering, hide retired versions, and require ambiguous retraction
to leave the complete annotated export unchanged. Ten empty listings on a
local 20,000-unrelated-claim fixture fell from 551.5 ms to 0.3 ms. All 37 rule
tests, 60 automation tests, and the workspace build pass. The rules reference
documents the shared path; the helper is private and public signatures are
unchanged.

Rule discovery performance review found every derivation materialized all
current beliefs before filtering declarations. Discovery now selects indexed
rule-attribute rows, requires each candidate to be the latest global row for
its claim key, and preserves declaration transaction ordering. In a local
20,000-unrelated-claim fixture without rules, ten derive calls fell from
580.6 ms to 22.3 ms; this is a bounded local measurement, not a general solver
speed claim. A regression forbids whole-store current-belief materialization,
keeps retracted rules disabled, and verifies active-rule firing and idempotence.
All 36 rule tests, 60 automation tests, and the workspace build pass. The rules
reference documents the discovery path. Public signatures and semantics are
unchanged. Listing and explicit rule retraction were reviewed in the follow-up
above.

Process bridge error review reproduced asynchronous execution returning raw
Node errors when spawn validation rejects malformed inputs, bypassing the
typed, redacted ProcessFailure contract. Synchronous throws from spawn are now
normalized before rejection. Regressions send NUL-bearing executable, argument,
working-directory, and environment values through both runners; each requires
a spawn failure, empty captured output, and no sensitive value in serialized
diagnostics. All 45 loop tests and the workspace build pass. The loop reference
explicitly includes spawn validation in its diagnostic contract. Public
signatures are unchanged.

Process output review confirmed capture joins raw buffers before decoding UTF-8,
so multibyte characters are not independently decoded at pipe chunk boundaries.
A real-child regression writes accented text and an emoji one byte at a time
to stdout and stderr, then requires exact text through both async and synchronous
runners with capture limits equal to the raw byte count. All 44 loop tests and
the workspace build pass. The loop reference now explains byte limits and
decode-after-join behavior. No production or public API change was needed.

The execution-limit integration checkpoint passed all 1,411 workspace tests
across 24 package summaries with no failures, cancellations, or skips, including
the executable book sessions. Packed CLI smoke passed without refreshing the
API snapshot. The production website rebuilt and all 29 browser tests passed;
the built documentation contains the rule validation, automation interval,
process deadline, and Z3-specific deadline contracts. The book's ordinary
examples remain accurate and require no source or PDF update for these limits.

The Z3 deadline follow-up found portable positive-safe-integer timeouts flowed
unchanged into both native settings and a JavaScript interrupt timer. The
adapter now rejects values outside 1..2147483647 with an unknown backend-error
result before compilation or native settings changes. This is adapter-specific:
portable limits retain their contract for other backends. A regression rejects
overflow and maximum-safe-integer deadlines, then solves with the largest
supported deadline to verify the runtime remains usable. The Z3 suite and
workspace build pass. The adapter reference documents the bound; public
signatures are unchanged.

Shared process deadline review reproduced a 2,147,483,648 ms timeout launching
then almost immediately killing a process through timer overflow. Both async
and synchronous runners now reject deadlines beyond 2,147,483,647 ms before
launching commands or bridge workers; zero retains its no-deadline behavior.
Regressions exercise both runners with overflow and maximum-safe-integer inputs,
require no launch marker, and verify the largest supported deadline completes
a real command. All 43 loop tests, the workspace build, and the action,
ingestion, evaluation, and automation consumer suites pass. The loop reference
documents the bound and TypeError contract; signatures are unchanged. Connector
watch timers were inspected and use fixed 200 ms debounce delays. The separate
solver deadline path is covered by the follow-up above.

Automation polling review confirmed with a local Node runtime probe that a
2,147,483,648 ms interval is clamped to 1 ms, and that a sub-millisecond
interval is also clamped. The CLI previously accepted both through its positive
finite seconds check. It now accepts 0.001..2147483.647 seconds, rejecting
out-of-range values before database opening. CLI regressions verify rejection
does not create a database and both supported endpoints plus an ordinary
fractional interval remain accepted. All 60 automation tests and the workspace
build pass. The automation reference and specification record the timer bounds;
public signatures and ordinary book examples are unchanged.

Automation limit review reproduced `settle` accepting zero, negative,
fractional, non-finite, and unsafe pass limits. The library now validates a
positive safe integer before any transaction or step, preserving its existing
early cancellation check; CLI validation uses the same bound before database
opening. A pending prompt regression verifies invalid limits call no completion
adapter and preserve the complete annotated export, then verifies a valid run
still claims that pending work exactly once. CLI regressions require that no
database is created. All 59 automation tests and the workspace build pass.
The automation reference and specification document the contract; public
signatures and valid book examples are unchanged.

Rule execution review found library derivation accepted non-finite or out-of-range
confidence floors and invalid pass limits. Derivation now validates a finite
0..1 floor and a positive safe integer pass limit before reserving its transaction;
CLI and MCP pass-count checks use the same bound. A real-store regression starts
with supported conclusions and watermarks, rejects invalid options, and requires
the complete annotated export to remain unchanged. Valid confidence endpoints
and the maximum safe pass limit still settle normally. CLI tests verify invalid
limits cannot create the database, and MCP tests verify tool errors preserve
stored state. All 35 rule tests, 90 CLI command tests, 94 MCP tests, and the
workspace build pass. Rules/MCP references and the specification document the
bounds. Public signatures and ordinary book examples are unchanged.

The connector concurrency integration checkpoint passed all 1,404 workspace
tests across 24 package summaries with no failures, cancellations, or skips,
including the executable book sessions. Packed-artifact smoke passed without
refreshing the API snapshot. The production website rebuilt successfully and
all 29 browser tests passed; the built documentation includes scalar-key
validation, pruning-phase atomicity, and the reserved digest recheck. Review of
the connector book chapter found its ordinary examples and lifecycle explanation
still accurate, so no book source or PDF update was needed for these fixes.

Connector refresh review reproduced two connections appending the same record
when a peer completed its refresh between the initial digest check and the write
reservation. Record and prelude writes now recheck their digest inside the write
transaction. Real two-connection regressions verify that identical records,
ordinary preludes, and lifecycle preludes skip without changing the peer's
annotated export; force still appends. Connector documentation and the extraction
specification describe the reserved digest check. All 107 connector tests and the
workspace build pass, as do all ten unchanged performance thresholds. Public
signatures and the book's ordinary examples are unchanged.

Connector transaction review reproduced pruning reading its digest list before
reserving a write transaction: a peer-added record could escape an empty-source
prune. Discovery and all disappearance retirements now share one transaction.
A regression uses two real database connections and injects the peer write just
before reservation; both records and their active digests now retract. A second
regression injects failure on the second digest retirement and requires the
complete annotated export to roll back. All 105 connector tests and the
workspace build passed. The README and specification describe pruning-phase
atomicity while retaining earlier successful per-record commits. Public
signatures and ordinary book output are unchanged.

Connector identity review reproduced object-valued keys being coerced into
colliding object-Object identities and non-finite numeric keys being accepted.
Keys now require usable string, finite-number, boolean or bigint scalars. A
real-store regression rejects objects, arrays, functions, symbols and non-finite
numbers, requires no mapping or pruning and an unchanged annotated export,
and preserves valid zero, false, exact bigint and string identities. Existing
sanitization and documented duplicate-key last-wins behavior remain intact.
All 103 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The README,
specification and minor changeset record the tightened key contract; public
signatures and valid book record keys are unchanged.

JSON selector review confirmed source loading already delegates to the shared
own-property field lookup. A loader-level regression now exercises local and
HTTP sources with explicit __proto__ and constructor arrays, exact dotted-key
precedence, and inherited Object/Array properties reported as missing selectors.
Four existing source tests also now register temporary-directory cleanup hooks;
previously they left fixtures behind on every run. All 102 connector tests and
the workspace build passed. The README explicitly connects --records to the
lookup contract. No production code or public signatures needed changing.

The CSV/documentation integration checkpoint passed all 1,398 workspace tests
with zero failures, cancellations or skips, including the book's executable
examples against the CLI. Packed smoke passed without an API snapshot update.
The website rebuilt successfully; emitted documentation contains duplicate-
header and row-width validation plus judge quote-recovery guidance. All 29
production browser tests passed against that build. A read-only changeset check
also confirmed all 209 pending entries name a public release owner; this is not
a claim that release publication or its external gates have completed. The full
system-review scope remains open.

Declared-source validation is now exercised through explicit pruning and
automatic assembly, using a real database with two previously imported records.
Truncated quotes, text after closing quotes, duplicate headers and excess cells
all leave the annotated export unchanged, including record digests and source
declaration metadata. Assembly reports a LocateError naming source/people.
Restoring the valid file skips both records, prunes none and adds no claims.
All 101 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The README documents
this refresh boundary; no runtime or public-signature change was needed beyond
the previously implemented shared CSV validation.

CSV row-width review reproduced values beyond the header width being silently
discarded. Such rows now fail source loading at their starting physical line,
including multiline CRLF records. Regressions preserve quoted delimiters and
missing-cell empty-string defaults and require an unchanged annotated store
export after a rejected --prune run. All 100 connector tests and the workspace
build passed. The README, extraction specification and minor changeset document
the tighter source contract; public signatures and valid book CSV examples are
unchanged.

CSV header review found an explicit last-column-wins policy that discarded
earlier source values under duplicate trimmed names. This policy is deliberately
tightened: source headers must now be unique, including header-only inputs and
SQL-backed loads. Regressions cover quoted and whitespace-normalized duplicates,
empty duplicate names, distinct case-sensitive names, SQL loading and an
unchanged annotated store export after a rejected --prune run. The previous
SQL parity expectation was updated to require rejection; harmless duplicate
names in a programmatic schema list still deduplicate as before. All 99
connector tests and the workspace build passed. The README, specification and
minor changeset record this source-validation change. Public signatures and
valid book headers remain unchanged.

CSV quote-boundary review reproduced stray quotes being accepted and text after
a closing quote being silently concatenated into the field value. Shared source
parsing now rejects both with the physical line number. Regressions preserve
valid doubled-quote escaping, cover multiline CRLF diagnostics, and rerun the
real connector with --prune to require an unchanged annotated store export for
each malformed input. All 98 connector tests and the workspace build passed.
The connector README and extraction specification document the tightened source
contract. Public signatures and valid book CSV examples are unchanged. The
website clipboard review preceding this work found existing denial, unavailable
API and pending-request regressions already matching the control's behavior;
no further clipboard change was warranted.

The documentation filename audit also found the edit footer interpolating raw
source paths into GitHub URLs. It now shares repository path-segment encoding
with documentation navigation. The filename regression verifies the decoded
edit pathname contains the complete source and has no accidental query or hash.
All 16 website unit tests, the production build and the browser sweep of all
bundled documentation section targets passed. The website README documents the
shared encoding; current source filenames and book artifacts are unchanged.

Website link-helper review reproduced encoded filenames containing literal
hash, question-mark and percent characters failing to match a bundled document;
using such a source as a relative-link base also interpreted filename text as
URL syntax. Source path segments are now encoded before URL resolution, and
matching decodes filenames while refusing encoded-slash path-boundary changes.
A regression covers inbound and same-document section links, relative siblings
and encoded separators. All 16 website unit tests, the production build and five
documentation browser checks passed, including every current bundled section
target. The website README records the encoding rules. Current document names
do not require renaming, and no book content changes are needed.

Follow-up judge-parser review found that an unmatched quote in malformed prose
could still hide a later answer after the string-aware scan was introduced.
The parser now also indexes literal bracket boundaries for recovery. Valid
outer JSON consumes its entire span before inner candidates are considered,
so a string containing another apparent answer is not reinterpreted. Regressions
verify quote recovery, ownership of valid-array strings and a later empty answer
overriding an earlier pairing. All 58 evaluation tests and the workspace build
passed. The README records recovery behavior; public signatures are unchanged.

Judge-response review reproduced brackets inside string entries corrupting
array detection, causing valid neighboring pairs to disappear. An unfinished
outer prose bracket also hid a balanced final answer. The parser now indexes
balanced spans with a stack and JSON-string escape awareness, then evaluates
candidates in authored order while consuming valid outer arrays whole. New
regressions cover bracket strings, escaped quotes/backslashes and 20,000
unfinished prefix brackets without repeated suffix scanning. Existing duplicate,
range and last-answer tests remain intact. All 57 evaluation tests and the
workspace build passed. The README documents the parser boundary; public
signatures and ordinary book examples are unchanged.

The integration checkpoint after ingestion batching, context lookup, HTML
extraction and evaluation cancellation/validation passed all 1,390 workspace
tests with zero failures, cancellations or skips. Packed-consumer smoke passed
without an API snapshot change, including the evaluation reconstruction baseline
and public import checks. The website rebuild passed, and the emitted Docs
asset contains the updated tolerance, batching, cancellation and HTML-extraction
guidance. These checks establish this integration checkpoint, not completion of
the full system review above.

Evaluation tolerance review reproduced NaN, infinity and out-of-range values
being accepted by the library despite its documented 0–1 contract. A shared
internal validator now runs before evaluation discovery and in direct value
agreement and comparison calls, including empty comparisons. Regressions verify
invalid settings never call an agent, reject across direct scoring surfaces,
and preserve the valid upper boundary. All 55 evaluation tests and the workspace
build passed. The eval README documents validation order and bounds. The CLI
already enforced this range; public signatures and valid book examples remain
unchanged.

Evaluation repetition review reproduced invalid library run counts being
accepted rather than rejected. The library now requires a positive safe integer
before suite discovery, and CLI validation uses the same bound and diagnostic.
Regressions cover zero, negative, fractional, non-finite and unsafe values,
confirm the maximum safe integer remains valid for an empty suite, and exercise
the command's option-error path without agent work. All 53 evaluation tests and
the workspace build passed. The README documents the bound and validation
order; public signatures and ordinary book run counts are unchanged.

Evaluation cancellation review reproduced ingestion aborts being converted into
ordinary failed-run reports, and pre-cancelled evaluations still discovering
suites. Evaluation now checks cancellation before discovery, cases, repetitions,
scoring and judge work; catch paths preserve the original abort reason, and
function-based reconstruction checks it around each completion. Regressions
cover cancellation during extraction, judging and reconstruction, no later
agent calls, pre-cancelled discovery and removal of throwaway databases. All 51
evaluation tests and the workspace build passed. The eval README distinguishes
cancellation from ordinary scoreable failures and documents cooperative function
adapters and the existing keep option. Public signatures and book examples are
unchanged.

Binary ingestion cancellation is now verified against a real local HTTP server
that starts but does not finish a source response. The regression waits for the
request before sending SIGINT, then requires normal exit code 130, empty stderr,
no agent-start marker and an immediately reopened target with identical export.
All 11 binary lifecycle tests and the workspace build passed. The CLI README
documents pending-URL cancellation and quiet signal exit. This complements the
library's staging-cleanup checks; it does not infer cancellation behavior solely
from an injected function or a passing unit-level signal check.

HTML ingestion review reproduced `<br>` elements disappearing during text
extraction, joining `First` and `Second` into `FirstSecond`. The shared DOM
flattening step now replaces breaks with newlines before ordinary block
whitespace is normalized. Regressions verify separated words in paragraph and
div content and preserved lines in preformatted content. All 50 ingestion tests
and the workspace build passed. The README explains the readable-text boundary:
digests and agent line anchors use extracted text, not raw HTML markup. Existing
book examples and public signatures are unchanged; affected pages may correctly
receive a new digest because their extracted content is no longer concatenated.

Prompt-context cost review reproduced repeated FTS searches for shared path
tokens, including searches after the related-claim budget was already full.
Context construction now deduplicates tokens in first-seen order and checks the
budget before each lookup. A real-store regression uses 1,000 distinct paths
sharing one useful token plus one unrelated path, checks identical prompt
context, and verifies zero searches at a zero budget, one at a filled one-claim
budget, and two at the default budget rather than 1,001 redundant lookups.
All 49 ingestion tests and the workspace build passed. The README records
lookup behavior; store-wide statistics and naming-anchor scans still occur,
so this does not claim that all prompt construction costs are bounded by the
claim limit. Public signatures and ordinary book output are unchanged.

Ingestion batching review reproduced fractional and infinite library batch sizes
being accepted, and invalid options losing precedence to missing-source errors
because validation happened after source reads. Shared batching now requires a
positive safe integer; selection validates with that contract before file reads
or URL fetches. The CLI also rejects unsafe integers before opening its database.
Regressions cover empty and populated batches, the maximum safe integer, missing
local sources, a fetch that must not run, and CLI database non-creation. All 48
ingestion tests and the workspace build passed. The README records validation
order and bounds. No public signatures or ordinary book examples changed.

Direct-write ingestion cancellation is now verified with agents opening a
second real database connection. Strict cancellation preserves the baseline,
publishes none of the agent's writes, and removes the staged database; lenient
cancellation retains direct target writes while withholding the interrupted
source's success digest. Both policies propagate the original abort reason.
All 46 ingestion tests passed, followed by all 1,378 workspace tests with zero
failures, cancellations or skips. Workspace and website builds passed; the
website's emitted documentation includes the new cancellation contract. The
existing README explains these ownership rules, so no additional syntax or book
change is needed. This checkpoint does not close the broader review scope.

The run-wide ingestion cancellation enhancement now covers source selection,
URL requests and body reads, shell processes, cooperative function agents,
batch boundaries and strict staged publication. Previously a pre-cancelled run
still selected sources, and a function agent could abort yet have its result
committed. Regressions now require the exact abort reason, no pre-cancel fetch
or agent call, no later batch, strict rollback of earlier staged claims and
digests, and preservation of earlier accepted lenient batches. A real HTTP
response-body regression and an injected pending-fetch regression verify signal
propagation. All 45 ingestion tests and the workspace build passed. Packed
smoke passed; the reviewed API snapshot delta contains only AgentContext.signal,
Web.fetchDocument's fourth argument, Web.select's signal option and their two
declaration fingerprints. The README documents cooperative adapter cancellation,
in-memory synchronous work boundaries and existing direct lenient writes that
cannot be undone. No existing book session uses these optional APIs.

Ingestion lifecycle review reproduced HTTP error responses leaving their
ReadableStream bodies uncancelled. URL fetching now cancels unread error bodies
before constructing the existing HTTP failure. A regression checks one cancel
call and retention of the original 503 message even when cancellation rejects;
the existing selection tests retain retry classification coverage. All 41
ingest tests and the workspace build passed. The ingestion README documents
cleanup ownership. The same review confirmed that Options.signal currently
documented shell-process cancellation only. That finding led to the run-wide
cancellation enhancement recorded above.

The integration checkpoint after the source-link, numeric-anchor and large-report
fixes passed the packed-consumer smoke suite without an API snapshot refresh.
It exercised public tarball imports under NodeNext and Bundler, CLI reports,
HTTP views, solver workflows and owned highlighter cleanup. The website rebuild
succeeded, and its emitted documentation asset contains the revised source-link,
safe-integer and report-assembly guidance. All 29 production browser checks
passed against that rebuilt site. This verifies these integration surfaces;
the full system-review scope remains open.

Large-report review reproduced argument-limit RangeErrors with a valid
150,000-line query fragment and a stored source locator containing 150,000
backtick runs. Report assembly now appends lines iteratively at both block
boundaries, and code-span delimiter selection scans runs without spreading
them into Math.max. Real-store regressions verify complete output line counts,
citation placement and delimiter content. All 63 view tests and the workspace
build passed. The view README explains the remaining in-memory assembly model;
this removes an accidental argument-count limit without promising unbounded
memory or changing report syntax, public signatures or ordinary book examples.

Report provenance review reproduced source labels passing Markdown emphasis,
code and HTML syntax through unescaped; escaping only brackets also mishandled
backslashes immediately before brackets. Labels now escape those delimiters,
and destinations encode ampersands as Markdown entities so source text such as
`&copy;` cannot become a different URL during rendering. A real-store regression
covers those characters. A separate check with the installed website
react-markdown/remark-gfm renderer verified the resulting link's exact text and
href. All 61 view tests and the workspace build passed. The view README records
literal rendering; public signatures and ordinary book examples are unchanged.

Source-line boundary review reproduced `L9007199254740993` being exposed as
`L9007199254740992`, silently changing the evidence location. Shared validation
now requires positive safe-integer endpoints for both formatting and parsing.
Regressions reject unsafe single lines and ranges, non-finite and fractional
values, and values that would format in exponential notation; the maximum safe
range still round-trips exactly. All 289 core, connect, view and ingest tests
and the workspace build passed. The core README and §9.8 document the JavaScript
API bound. Stored contexts remain ordinary metadata; this validation neither
rewrites stored evidence nor changes public signatures. The book's ordinary
source-line examples remain valid and need no generated-artifact change.

Provenance-link review reproduced existing URL escapes being encoded twice:
an original `%20` path became `%2520`, changing the cited resource. The shared
SourceSpan formatter now preserves existing percent triplets while encoding raw
spaces, Unicode and malformed percent text. Core regressions cover spanned and
unspanned references, encoded separators and query values; a report regression
checks the link after provenance passes through the real store. All 91 core and
60 view tests and the workspace build passed. Core and view READMEs explain the
behavior. This restores §9.8's source-identity contract without changing the
stored context encoding, public signatures or ordinary book examples.

HTTP request-boundary review reproduced malformed URLs returning 500 from the
view server's general exception handler. URL parsing now has a dedicated 400
response. A real HTTP regression sends malformed relative and absolute request
targets through GET and HEAD, checks no-store headers and empty HEAD bodies,
and confirms a subsequent overview request succeeds. All 59 view tests and the
workspace build passed. The view README documents this client-error boundary;
public signatures and the ordinary book sessions are unchanged.

The integration checkpoint after the three view fixes and installed-consumer
README import regression passed all 1,365 workspace tests, with zero failures,
cancellations or skips. A follow-up substitution review confirmed that report
bindings and automation prompts already use callback replacement; report
citation replacement uses generated numeric markers, not user data. Existing
report regressions exercise dollar tokens, variable-looking inserted text and
citation placeholders, so no additional substitution change was warranted.
The view README covers the affected browser behavior; no further specification
or book edits are needed for this verification checkpoint. The broader review
scope above remains open.

Page metadata review reproduced dollar replacement tokens in a database label
expanding into template text and duplicating HTML. Sequential replacement also
rewrote label text that resembled later metadata markers. The server now uses
one-pass callback substitution with HTML escaping. A real HTTP regression covers
dollar tokens, angle brackets and all marker spellings, verifies one script
block, and confirms API metadata still returns the original label. All 58 view
tests and the workspace build passed. The view README documents literal
substitution; public signatures and ordinary book examples are unchanged.

The read-only view's separate search handler reproduced premature navigation on
a composing Enter event. It now checks the native composition flag, matching the
playground behavior, and the search field has an explicit accessible name.
A regression executes the generated page's event code, keeps the route unchanged
during composition, verifies ordinary Enter encodes the completed search text,
and preserves the existing route for blank input. All 57 view tests and the
workspace build passed. The view README documents the behavior; this event-level
check does not claim manual verification of every operating-system input method.

The read-only browser view review found saved alias preference access outside
error handling, so unavailable storage could abort startup or prevent a toggle
from reloading the view. Preference reads now fall back to aliases off, and
failed writes leave the current toggle active and still route. A regression
executes the actual generated page's initialization/event code with throwing
storage operations, verifying both failures and continued routing. The view
tests and workspace build passed. Entity escaping and malformed-route recovery
were already implemented and were preserved.

The full-suite checkpoint after binding and highlighter changes passed all 1,361
tests. The concurrent documentation audit found stale installed-consumer import
examples in ten internal package READMEs. They now use the registry's published
`@cavelang/cli/*` replacements. A new registry-driven documentation test covers
both internal and non-published tooling workspaces; the migration guide's explicit
before/after example and contributor source imports remain valid and unchanged.
All nine documentation tests passed separately after the edits, and workspace
and site builds passed. DOCUMENTATION.md records the new projection check. This
closes the evidenced import drift, not the broader remaining review scope.

The owned-highlighter follow-through added a permanent installed-tarball smoke
check. It resolves the public browser factory and parser/grammar/query assets
from the scratch consumer, highlights a real claim, closes twice, and verifies
that spans and ANSI calls reject use after closure. The expanded `make smoke`
passed with the reviewed API snapshot and all existing CLI/solver/sync/backup
workflows. IMPLEMENTATION.md records the additional packaged lifecycle coverage.

Highlighting lifecycle review implemented explicit ownership for successful
factory-created highlighters. `OwnedHighlighter` extends the existing interface
with idempotent `close()`, releasing its parser/query and rejecting later use
before parsing. Core and browser factories return the owned interface; Node's
process-wide cache returns a wrapper without close so borrowers cannot invalidate
one another. The website cache remains page-owned. Initialized language/runtime
modules are not unloaded. All 16 highlighter tests, workspace/site builds,
packed smoke and two production browser checks (grammar retry and playground
WASM execution) passed. The generated API delta was reviewed: only the new type,
factory return types and their declaration fingerprints changed. The package
README documents ownership and the minor changeset records the new API; existing
book examples use the unchanged shared interface.

The query surface follow-through verified that the binding correction reaches
CLI JSON and text as well as MCP's text tool results. New regressions query a
real store through `queryCommand` and the MCP tool surface and retain the
`__proto__` name/value in each output. The targeted CLI test, MCP server tests
and workspace build passed. MCP query output is text content rather than a new
structured JSON projection; no serializer or public-format changes were needed.

The binding follow-through pass verified prototype-named variables across an
automation's two-premise trigger, substituted prompt, JSON firing report and
resulting claim, then confirmed a second settle does not fire again. Rule
regressions now also bind prototype-named variables in verb position. All 57
automation tests and 34 rule tests passed; the workspace build passed with the
new automation regression. The automation README records the verified binding
propagation. No further production change was required beyond the preceding
query and specialization fixes.

Downstream binding review reproduced rules with `?__proto__` producing no
solutions because specialization treated an inherited object property as a bound
term. Specialization now checks own properties for term and verb variables.
Regressions derive real claims through two-premise joins for `__proto__`,
constructor and toString, then verify idempotence. Action parameter grammar
already excludes leading underscores, so no parameter-grammar or binding-object
change was needed there; action argument lookup now requires own supplied
properties, tested with constructor/toString and inherited argument objects.
All 123 rule/action/automation tests and the workspace build passed. The package
READMEs document these boundaries; the changeset marks action-input tightening
minor and the rule correction patch. Public signatures and book examples are
unchanged.

Query binding review reproduced `?__proto__ IS service` matching a row but
returning an empty bindings object because ordinary assignment invoked the
prototype setter. Direct bindings now use own-property construction, and
transitive bindings use computed property names. A regression covers subject,
value and both transitive endpoints, preserves constructor/toString names,
verifies JSON serialization and retains ordinary object prototypes. All 96 query
tests, the workspace build and the fixed performance gate passed. The query
README documents variable-name preservation; exported signatures and valid book
examples remain unchanged.

SQL staging numeric review reproduced NaN becoming SQL NULL and infinities
passing through; structured values could also lose non-finite numbers through
JSON serialization. Staging now rejects non-finite inputs at both levels before
query execution. A regression covers NaN and both infinities as scalar, object
and array fields, while preserving explicit NULL and finite structured numbers.
All 97 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The package README and
structured-ingestion specification document the boundary, with a minor changeset
for invalid-input tightening. Public signatures and valid book fixtures remain
unchanged.

The follow-up SQL staging review reproduced a binding failure for heterogeneous
JSON records when one owns a `toString` field and another lacks it: the absent
field read an inherited function. Staging now binds NULL for absent own fields.
A regression covers missing and explicitly supplied `toString`, `constructor`
and `__proto__` values in the same record set. All 96 connector tests and the
workspace build passed. The README explains NULL staging; this restores missing
field behavior without changing public signatures or valid book examples.

Template field review reproduced missing `toString` fields resolving to inherited
functions and custom inherited values being read as record data. Field lookup now
requires own properties both for exact keys and every dotted-path step. A
regression preserves explicit `constructor`/`__proto__` JSON data and array-index
access, rejects inherited exact/nested fields, and verifies that a missing
optional `toString` field drops its claim instead of failing record formatting.
All 95 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The package README
documents the own-property boundary; the changeset treats lookup tightening as
minor. Public signatures and valid book examples remain unchanged.

Connector option review found delimiter length checked at CLI/declaration
boundaries but not in direct parser calls, and double-quote/line-break delimiters
were accepted despite conflicting with CSV syntax. The shared reader now rejects
these inputs before parsing, including an empty source. Regression cases cover
empty, multi-character, quote, CR and LF delimiters while retaining semicolon,
pipe and tab support. All 94 connector tests and the workspace build passed.
The package README and structured-ingestion specification state the validation;
the changeset treats invalid-input tightening as minor. Existing book examples
use supported delimiters and need no update.

JSONL diagnostics review reproduced syntax errors containing only a per-record
JSON parser message, without the source or physical line. The reader now adds
the path/URL and physical line while preserving the parser error as its cause.
A local/HTTP regression uses CRLF and blank lines and verifies that the malformed
record is correctly identified at line four. All 93 connector tests and the
workspace build passed. The README records the diagnostic contract; accepted
inputs, public signatures and book examples remain unchanged.

HTTP format review reproduced an `application/x-ndjson` response being parsed as
one JSON document and failing on its second record. The loader now recognizes
NDJSON/JSONL media types before generic JSON and normalizes casing and parameters.
A regression covers extensionless URLs, two records separated by a blank line,
physical spans, SQL projection and explicit format override precedence. All 92
connector tests and the workspace build passed. The source documentation and
connector README describe the detection rules; no public signatures changed.

The integration checkpoint after connector source handling, sync provenance and
website accessibility changes passed all 1,347 workspace tests, all 29 production
browser tests, and the packed smoke suite with the reviewed API snapshot. The
site was then rebuilt to include the latest imported connector documentation,
whose new source-validation text was verified in the generated Docs bundle.
The fixed performance gate passed after the other workloads finished. All 166
pending changesets at the start of this checkpoint had a fixed-group release
owner, and whitespace checks passed. These checks establish integration for the
current changes; they do not close the remaining review scope above.

HTTP connector review reproduced unread error responses being discarded without
cancelling their body streams. The loader now cancels the body before reporting
the URL and HTTP status. A regression uses real Response/ReadableStream objects
and checks exactly one cancellation both when cleanup succeeds and when its
callback throws; HTTP 503 remains the reported error in both cases. All 91
connector tests and the workspace build passed. The package README records this
cleanup behavior; success parsing, public signatures and book examples are
unchanged.

The neighboring CSV review reproduced silent loss of single-field quoted-empty
records (`""`), with or without a final newline. The parser now remembers whether
a row contains a quoted field, preserving explicit empty records while keeping
blank-line filtering. A regression interleaves blank and quoted-empty lines and
checks record values, physical source spans and SQL COUNT across absent/LF/CRLF
final line endings. All 90 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The
connector README documents the distinction; valid syntax and public interfaces
remain unchanged.

Connector CSV review reproduced acceptance of an unfinished quoted field as a
complete source. The shared CSV/TSV reader now rejects end-of-input while a field
is quoted and reports its opening physical line. Unit cases cover headers,
ordinary and multiline records, and a trailing escaped quote. A command-level
regression first connects two records, then requests pruning from a truncated
replacement and verifies nonzero exit plus byte-identical annotated store export.
All 89 connector tests and the workspace build passed. The connector README
documents rejection before mapping/pruning; the changeset marks this malformed
input tightening as minor. Valid book fixtures are unaffected.

Connector source review reproduced a range error when reading a direct SQLite
source containing a valid 64-bit integer outside JavaScript's safe range. The
existing bigint-to-text conversion never ran because the statement first tried
to produce numbers. Direct source statements now enable bigint reads, matching
the staged-record SQL path. A regression reads both signed 64-bit extremes via
table and SQL loading, verifies exact decimal text, and preserves safe integers
and fractional values as numbers. All 87 connector tests and the workspace build
passed. The connector README documents the consistent result conversion; public
signatures and book examples remain unchanged.

Playground response-order review found an existing worker promise queue that
serializes open, append and query requests; no additional scheduling layer was
introduced. The related website accessibility pass found unconditional loading
pulses, smooth scrolling and button transitions. A reduced-motion media rule now
disables those effects while retaining loading text and control behavior. A
production-browser regression delays the actual lazy route download to inspect
the loading state, then releases it and successfully runs a query. The targeted
browser check and production build passed. The website README documents the
preference; the immediately preceding full suite passed 28 browser tests before
this additional test was added.

Website keyboard review reproduced Enter dispatching a query while the native
keyboard event reports active input-method composition. The handler now waits
until composition is inactive. A production-browser regression counts actual
worker query requests: the composing event sent one request before the fix and
now sends none; ordinary Enter still sends one and renders results. The
production build and all 28 browser tests passed. The website README documents
the behavior. This checks the browser event boundary, not a manual session with
every operating-system input method.

The follow-up sync vocabulary review verified that imported reverse declarations
apply to merge records. A stored `RECEIVED-FROM` row with swapped endpoints is
the correct canonical form when it is the declared forward verb of `SYNCED-INTO`;
forcing a literal stored spelling would bypass ordinary vocabulary semantics.
A new database/text regression verifies original-direction queries, rejects the
opposite direction, checks stored comments and report text, and confirms an
unchanged repeat appends no record. All 43 sync tests passed. The test workspace
now declares its query dependency and TypeScript project reference. The README
explains this verified behavior; no production change or normative/book update
was needed.

Sync label review reproduced a quote or backtick in an origin label causing the
merge-count comment to become part of the persisted destination entity, despite
a successful report. Label normalization now replaces these literal delimiters
alongside existing whitespace/comment/metadata markers. A regression covers each
delimiter on the origin, destination and both sides for database and annotated
text merges, asserting stored subjects, objects, comments and report text.
All 42 sync tests and the workspace build passed. The sync README records the
normalization; the fix restores the existing provenance contract without changing
book examples or exported interfaces.

Sync file-identity review found that the self-sync guard compared real paths but
missed hard links to the same inode. A regression using a real hard link and an
attachment guard reproduced entry into SQLite attachment instead of the
documented no-op. The guard now also compares device and inode before attaching.
All 41 sync tests pass, including unchanged rows and a usable target after normal
and dry-run self-sync. A separate CLI regression exercises both modes without an
attachment mock and verifies the database bytes remain identical. The workspace
build passed. The sync README now states that self-sync includes symbolic and
hard links; normative merge semantics and book examples remain unchanged.

The integration checkpoint after the browser adapter, declaration snapshot and
automation changes passed all 1,338 workspace tests. Packed smoke initially
detected the schema snapshot's internal declaration change: the exported API
section stayed identical, while `shape/check.d.ts` changed and its newly
referenced `shape/constraints.d.ts` entered the declaration closure. The exact
delta was reviewed against emitted declarations before accepting the generated
snapshot. The refreshed smoke run passed all packed workflows, including
NodeNext/Bundler consumers and exact-byte backup/restore.

Release metadata inspection found 22 new changesets naming only private internal
packages, which would fail the fixed-group ownership check. Each now also names
the public CLI that bundles it, at the same release severity; release notes and
internal owners are preserved. All pending changesets were checked for a
fixed-group owner, and CLAUDE.md now explicitly covers bundled internal packages.
The actual release preflight correctly refuses this audit branch because it
requires main or a detached main commit; these local checks do not establish
release readiness or authorize publication.

Automation declaration profiling found one full current-belief read per
declaration, including unchanged declarations. The idempotence check now selects
the newest subject/attribute row directly; disabled rows remain eligible to win.
On a local in-memory fixture with 20,000 unrelated facts and 100 automations,
initial declaration fell from about 5.5 seconds to 96 ms and an unchanged repeat
from 5.3 seconds to 7 ms, with the same declaration counts and no problems
(Node 26.5, macOS arm64; diagnostic timings, not performance guarantees).
A regression covers newer changed, retracted and negated actor declarations,
then verifies re-declaration and idempotence. All 56 automation tests and the
workspace build passed. The README explains the lookup; this private optimization
changes no public interfaces, normative semantics or book examples.

Automation retraction review reproduced a second actor declaration surviving a
successful retraction when committed between declaration selection and write
