reservation. Selection now runs inside the transaction. A regression using two
real database connections inserts the second declaration immediately before the
reservation: it failed with one retracted series before the fix and now verifies
both series are retracted and no automation remains listed. All 55 automation
tests and the workspace build passed. The automation README documents the
reservation boundary and preserved firing history.

Schema reading now separates declaration metadata from ordinary fact indexes.
Expectation listing and client generation load only current EXPECTS rows, tags
and qualifier edges; generation reuses that tag snapshot rather than reading it
again. Full shape evaluation still loads the facts it needs. With one field and
50,000 unrelated instance facts, local generation fell from about 73 ms to 1 ms
with identical code SHA-256. The 10,000-field fixture now uses three SQL reads
and also preserves its exact code and schema hashes (Node 26.5, macOS arm64;
diagnostic timings only). All 162 shape/action/automation tests and the workspace
build passed. The package README records the final three-read design; public
interfaces, generated format and book examples remain unchanged.

Large-schema client generation review measured 10,004 SQL statements for 10,000
fields, plus repeated copies of growing per-type arrays. Constraint tags now
load in one declaration-scoped batch and groups append in place. The same local
fixture used five SQL reads and fell from about 227 ms to 129 ms; schema digest
and generated-code SHA-256 remained identical (Node 26.5, macOS arm64; diagnostic
only). All 76 shape tests, including generated TypeScript compilation and reader
execution, and the workspace build passed. The shape README records the query
and grouping design. Public API, schema format, examples and book are unchanged.

Documentation URL review verified encoded filenames, repository-root paths,
fragment-only links and query-bearing document links. Query parameters keep a
link on GitHub instead of silently disappearing into the site's hash router;
ordinary encoded paths still resolve to bundled documents. The existing resolver
already satisfied these cases, so production code was unchanged. A regression
now preserves the boundary, and all fifteen website unit tests passed. The
website README clarifies its previous overly broad statement that bundled
document links always remain internal. CLI, language and book content are
unaffected by this documentation/test update.

Browser editor accessibility review added a forced-colors fallback for its
transparent-textarea/syntax-mirror layering. The mirror is hidden and editable
text, background, caret and selection use native system colors. A production
browser test verifies computed text visibility and performs a real two-claim
rebuild in forced-colors mode. All 27 browser tests and the website build passed;
the targeted visual check also passed after framing the complete page from the
top. Screenshot inspection confirmed readable claims and result text. The
website README describes this mode; CLI, language and book content are unchanged.

Cross-adapter sensitivity review verified search at all four audience levels,
default-internal rows, malformed labels, mixed labels choosing the strictest
level, historical export and current-only suppression. A hidden replacement
does not resurrect an older public value, and a later public replacement becomes
visible again. The shared regression runs against real native FTS5 and sql.js
FTS4 engines; all 123 store tests and fourteen website unit tests passed.
No production defect was reproduced in these cases. The website README records
the added adapter coverage; semantics, CLI examples and book content are unchanged.

Browser adapter path review found its constructor discarded filenames and
silently opened transient memory stores. It now accepts only `:memory:` and
rejects filenames, empty paths and SQLite file URIs with an explicit persistence
error. The regression verifies rejection plus isolation between successive
memory opens. All thirteen website unit tests and the production build passed.
The playground already opens `:memory:`; its workflow is unchanged. The website
README records the adapter boundary, while CLI persistence, public package
signatures and book examples require no changes.

The consolidated post-fix workspace run passed all 1,332 tests, including CLI
and book checks. All ten fixed performance budgets passed on Node 26.5 / SQLite
3.53.3, macOS arm64; thresholds were unchanged. The remaining review scope now
appears before these evidence entries, with every prior finding retained.
The isolated doctor test also passed under the repository-managed pnpm runner,
confirming its earlier failure correctly identified an older pnpm on that
direct invocation's PATH. These results verify the exercised surfaces and do
not close the full review scope or unperformed interactive/platform checks.

Adapter write-result review found sql.js returned a hard-coded zero for every
`lastInsertRowid`. It now reads SQLite's `last_insert_rowid()` after execution
and captures affected rows before that read. A shared real-engine contract
checks reusable inserts, updates, ignored inserts and unmatched deletes, including
retention of the most recent insertion ID when no new row was inserted.
All 122 store tests, twelve website unit tests and the production website build
passed. The website README documents these results. Existing CAVE ingestion uses
explicit claim IDs and is unchanged; no public signature, CLI or book update is
needed for this browser-adapter contract repair.

SQLite WASM resource review confirmed reset statements remained owned by sql.js
until database close. In a local real-WASM diagnostic, 500 searches increased
tracked retained statements from 28 to 528. Executed statements now free their
native allocation in a finally block; reusable wrappers prepare again on the
next call while preserving eager SQL preparation at wrapper creation. The same
diagnostic held retention at seven statements, with 1,000-claim ingestion around
50 ms versus 45 ms before and 500 searches around 820 ms versus 860 ms before
(Node 26.5, macOS arm64; diagnostic timings, no guarantee). The regression covers
get/all/run, binding and SQL failures, exact cleanup and successful reuse.
All eleven website unit tests and the production build passed. The website
README records the preparation/retention tradeoff. Public adapter signatures,
CLI/book examples and generated artifacts are unchanged by this browser fix.
All 26 production browser regressions also passed with the new statement lifecycle.

Cross-adapter search review added a shared contract for literal phrase safety,
historical rows, limits and transaction rollback. It exposed an FTS4 mismatch:
`heap "dump"` returned no matches in sql.js while native FTS5 found both rows.
Literal search now encodes embedded quote separators for FTS4 instead of using
FTS5's doubled-quote escape convention. Raw syntax remains untouched and
engine-specific. All 121 store tests and ten website unit tests passed, including
the same contract against both actual engines; the workspace build passed.
Store and website READMEs record the portability boundary. Public signatures,
CLI examples and book sessions are unchanged by this literal-search repair.

Full-text search review confirmed its intended historical-row scope and found
the direct API passed unchecked limits to SQLite, where negative values mean
unlimited. Search now requires a supplied limit to be a non-negative safe
integer before issuing SQL. Zero retains empty-cap behavior, omission remains
uncapped, and CLI limits retain their existing stricter positive bounded range.
Regressions cover negative, fractional, non-finite and unsafe values on empty
and populated stores. All 120 store tests and the workspace build passed.
The package README records this deliberate input-contract tightening, released
as a minor changeset. CLI/MCP examples, signatures and book sessions remain
accurate and require no generated-document changes.

Website keyboard-navigation review found section links already focus their
targets, while whole documentation-page changes only scrolled and left focus on
the previous navigation link or document body. Page navigation now focuses the
new main heading with `tabIndex=-1` and no extra scroll; section navigation
retains its existing target focus. Filter edits do not rerun this effect.
Mobile and desktop browser regressions verify page-heading focus and restored
section focus through Back navigation. All 26 production browser tests and the
website build passed. The website README records the focus behavior; no CAVE
language, CLI, generated API or book changes are involved.

Snapshot publication review found forced backup replacement could leave old
destination WAL/SHM/journal files beside new snapshot bytes. Backup now shares
restore's stopped-destination check, including canonical directory aliases.
Restore additionally refuses destinations in its own source snapshot's sidecar
paths. A regression verifies every suffix leaves existing destination/sidecar
bytes unchanged, source sidecar paths absent, and the original snapshot checksum
unchanged; ordinary replacement works once destination sidecars are absent.
All 119 store tests and the workspace build passed. Store/CLI references,
implementation and the storage specification describe the force boundary.
Existing book workflows use separate stopped destinations and remain accurate;
no source/PDF or website-copy update is needed.
Packed-package/API/CLI smoke also passed. Its snapshot lifecycle coverage now
creates a backup from the installed CLI, independently hashes the snapshot,
checks reported SHA-256 and verification, rejects an incorrect digest, restores
identical bytes and compares full restricted-scope transaction-annotated exports
with the original store. This complements direct-store failure regressions with
the real packed command workflow. The implementation guide records the checks;
public interfaces, examples, website copy and book sessions are unchanged.
The expanded packed smoke passed, including the snapshot lifecycle checks;
shell syntax and whitespace checks also passed.

Snapshot verification review reproduced data loss: a live WAL database verified
with one row, while restoring its certified main-file bytes yielded zero rows.
Verification had read WAL-visible metadata but hashed only the main file.
It now rejects source WAL/SHM/journal sidecars, including through resolved source
paths. Live stores must use online backup to create a standalone snapshot first.
The regression checks rejection without creating a destination, then proves
online backup, verification and restore preserve the WAL-only row. All 118 store
tests and the workspace build passed. Store/CLI references, implementation guide
and the storage specification explain the same-content requirement. Existing
book sessions already verify backup-produced snapshots, so their source and PDF
remain accurate without changes.

Direct backup API review confirmed its source-identity guard omitted sidecars
and compared existing files only by real path, missing hard links. Backup now
protects the main source and WAL/SHM/journal paths before snapshot allocation;
shared path identity uses device/inode plus canonical parent resolution for
absent files. Restore likewise rejects hard links to its source snapshot.
A live-WAL regression covers forced and ordinary backup rejection, unchanged
WAL bytes and subsequent successful writes, plus restore identity rejection.
All 117 store tests and the workspace build passed.
The store README documents these file boundaries. This implements the existing
source-preservation contract without changing public declarations or examples;
book and website copy remain accurate.

CLI file-output review found that main-database overwrite checks omitted
SQLite WAL, shared-memory and rollback-journal paths. Export, report, generate
and backup now protect these physical source files before opening the store.
The guard resolves database symlinks and output-parent directories so absent
sidecars still compare correctly through `/var` versus `/private/var` aliases;
existing file aliases use device/inode identity. Content-based SQLite detection
keeps ordinary text-store sibling filenames available. A four-command regression
covers all three suffixes with direct and symlinked database paths and verifies
the source still queries afterward. All 87 CLI command tests passed from the
workspace root. A later isolated recheck explained the first direct invocation
from the package directory: doctor found pnpm 9.12.3, below the workspace's
11.9.0 requirement. That was an environment diagnosis, not a cwd-specific test
contract; use the repository-managed pnpm runner for its required toolchain.
The CLI README records sidecar protection. Existing valid CLI/book examples and
public signatures are unchanged; no generated-book update is required.

Generated-client verification now invokes the workspace TypeScript compiler
on a temporary emitted module in strict NodeNext mode. The fixture covers
special properties, numeric-leading type-name conversion, allowed value/type
namespace coexistence, unit typing, cardinality and inverse relations. Temporary
files are removed on success or failure, and the compiler has a 30-second bound.
All 76 shape tests passed. Existing runtime-reader tests remain necessary:
TypeScript compilation alone did not detect the earlier object-prototype bug.
The README explains this complementary verification. No production behavior,
public signatures, website copy or book examples changed in this test addition.

Generated type-name review reproduced successful generation followed by strict
TypeScript errors for CAVE types `store` and `cave-value`: their interfaces
collided with the emitted `Store` import and `CaveValue` alias. The existing
naming-conflict preflight now rejects both with deduplicated rename guidance,
before CLI output is written. Value-only bindings such as `QuerySql` remain
usable as interface names because TypeScript keeps those namespaces separate.
Two regressions cover rejection and that allowed boundary; all 75 shape tests
and the workspace build passed. The package README explains the reserved type
names. This restores the existing compilable-output/name-collision contract;
public signatures, valid examples, website copy and book content are unchanged.

Generated-client review reproduced JavaScript object-literal `__proto__`
semantics in reader results: the expected field became the object's prototype
instead of an own property. Readers now use computed property names for every
field. The executed-client regression verifies own-property presence, the
unchanged ordinary prototype and the exact stored value; it failed before the
fix. All 73 shape tests and the workspace build passed, and a generated client
containing the special field passed strict NodeNext TypeScript checking.
The shape README documents data-property behavior. Format version and schema
digest semantics are unchanged; the book only shows the unchanged generated
header, so no book source/PDF or website-copy update is needed.

Website asynchronous-state review found overlapping install-copy requests could
overwrite each other's completion status. A synchronous in-flight guard and
disabled/busy button now serialize clipboard attempts and show `copying…` until
completion; success and failure both release the guard. The browser regression
holds a clipboard promise open, checks that a second click adds no request, and
verifies a subsequent attempt works after completion. All 26 production browser
tests, nine website unit tests and the production build passed. The website
README records this behavior; language/CLI/book surfaces are unaffected.
The same review checked replaced-runtime guards in Playground and stale-source
guards in CaveCode. A proposed numbered-code scan optimization was dropped:
only the fixed homepage example uses line numbers, while editable claims use
the unnumbered path, so it would not improve long pasted files.

Editor token-boundary review now exercises the real extension provider with
the packaged WASM runtime/grammar and a small VS Code host double. Astral entity
letters, combining marks, emoji literals, CRLF lines and an unfinished quoted
value produce single-line, non-overlapping UTF-16 ranges; the following complete
claim still highlights. No production defect was reproduced for these cases.
The new integration test preserves that evidence alongside the existing grammar
and resource tests. Extension typechecking/build and the six preceding tests
passed, followed by the new integration test. The editor README explains the
coverage and its limitation: interactive host/theme rendering remains unverified.
Public behavior and examples are unchanged, so no book or website update is
needed for this test-only addition.

Highlighter lifecycle review found that parser setup failure leaked the already
compiled query and allocated parser. The shared Node/browser factory now frees
both on failure; a real-WASM test injects `setLanguage` failure and verifies
exactly one deletion of each resource. It failed before the fix and all 14
highlighter tests pass afterward, along with the workspace build. The package
README records setup cleanup and retained successful instances. This does not
add disposal of successful public factory instances; that lifetime remains an
open enhancement. Public signatures, highlighting output, specification and
book examples are unchanged, so no generated artifact update is needed.
The full workspace run covering the preceding shape changes completed with
1,317 passing tests, and packed-package/API/CLI smoke passed. That run began
before the highlighter cleanup edit; its subsequent targeted 14-test run and
workspace build provide the cleanup-specific validation.

Alias discovery previously scanned every textual value for each scored name
pair. Rare-value signals are now indexed once by unordered pair, preserving
their original traversal order and two-signal cap; candidate buckets append
without repeated copies. A 1,000-entity/1,000-distinct-value local diagnostic
returned the same empty result in 1.06 seconds versus 6.44 seconds before
(Node 26.5, macOS arm64; no timing guarantee). Candidate enumeration itself
can still be quadratic within broad blocks. A regression verifies the signal
cap and refreshed rarity after a third carrier appears. All 73 shape tests and
the workspace build passed. The README records the index and corrects its stale
three-read evaluation description to the current presence probe plus four
snapshot reads. Public API, scoring rules, examples and book remain unchanged.

Alias-suggestion evidence review reproduced truncated neighbor explanations:
`USES "shared database engine"` appeared as `both USES "shared`. Space-delimited
internal relation signatures were split without preserving literal boundaries.
Neighbor signatures now use JSON tuples, preserving complete inbound and
outbound terms in signal details and emitted comments. A real-store regression
covers text objects and code subjects containing spaces. All 72 shape tests and
the workspace build passed. The package README documents full-term evidence;
scoring and public types are unchanged, and existing specification/book examples
remain accurate, requiring no generated-document or website-copy changes.

Write-gate review reproduced a separator collision between violation identities
for entity `api\0service` / type `worker` and entity `api` / type
`service\0worker`. The second missing-owner violation was incorrectly accepted
as pre-existing. The shared `violationKey` now JSON-encodes its four components.
Real-store regressions verify checked ingestion and action execution reject the
new violation and roll back physical rows, including action lineage. All 71
shape, 32 action and 54 automation tests passed, as did the workspace build.
The shape README documents the key boundary. This restores the specified
new-violation rejection contract without changing public signatures; normative
skills, examples, website copy and book require no update.

Health-report boundary review reproduced a false alias disagreement between
structured context `prod\0west` and the two-context set `prod`, `west`.
Storage correctly kept them distinct, but report grouping joined contexts with
a NUL separator. Its key now JSON-encodes verb, slot and the sorted context
array. The regression verifies those scopes stay separate and that reordered
identical contexts still conflict across actor stamps. All 155 shape/action/
automation tests and the workspace build passed. The package README records
the implementation boundary; this restores the existing context-set contract,
so specification, examples, public types, website copy and book need no change.

Alias disagreement review found quadratic bucket copies and pair searches,
particularly costly when many actors agree. Buckets now append in place and
equality-based conflict detection scans for two names and two values/polarities;
that condition guarantees a differing cross-name pair. Report ordering and all
participating rows remain intact. A regression covers a fork under one name
followed by another name agreeing with the first actor. A local real-store check
of 10,000 agreeing actor claims returned zero disagreements in about 180 ms
(Node 26.5, macOS arm64; diagnostic only, no timing guarantee). All 154 shape,
action and automation tests and the workspace build passed. The public API
and examples are unchanged, so the book needs no update for this optimization.

Source hygiene review found four literal NUL bytes in shape checking/gating
TypeScript, causing normal text search to classify those files as binary.
They now use explicit `\0` string/template escapes with identical runtime
separator values. A scan of package, script and website source text found no
other literal NULs. This changes source readability only; public behavior,
API declarations, documentation examples and book content remain valid.
All 68 shape tests and the workspace build passed; ordinary `rg` now reports
the key expressions as text.

Wide-shape review found growing-array copies in taxonomy child grouping and
per-type expectation grouping. Both now append to evaluation-local arrays,
retaining order and fresh snapshots. A 10,000-child taxonomy with one target
measured 77.9 ms before and 23.8 ms after; 10,000 expectations on one type with
no instances measured 125.5 ms and 64.3 ms. Both experiments asserted their
exact expectation/check counts. These isolate group construction on Node
26.5.0/macOS arm64, not general automation throughput. The shape reference
records the linear-construction rationale; public APIs, gate semantics and
book examples are unchanged.
All 153 shape/action/automation tests, workspace and website builds, and packed
smoke passed with the existing public API snapshot.

Shape snapshots now restrict constraint tags and declaration-excluding edges
to the current `EXPECTS` IDs. A single bound JSON array avoids constructing a
parameter per declaration and preserves tag ordering. A regression combines
a qualified malformed expectation with unrelated malformed fact tags and a
valid unit requirement: only the valid declaration participates. All 68 shape,
31 action and 54 automation tests pass. The shaped 1,000-event benchmark
passed exact cardinality/owner and quiet-cycle checks at 15.99 s on this host;
this is an individual observation, not proof of resolved scaling. The shape
README documents the fresh restricted reads; no API or book contract changes.
Workspace/website builds, packed smoke with the existing API snapshot and all
ten fixed performance budgets passed.

The smoke follow-up replaced 18 remaining early-exit CLI output assertions
with consuming grep checks. This includes export/sync pipelines and ANSI
highlight output. Shell syntax validation passed. Explicit pipeline experiments
verified a two-megabyte matching producer exits zero, a producer exiting nine
still fails with nine despite matching output, and absent content fails with
one. IMPLEMENTATION.md records the complete-output contract; no public CLI
behavior, package signatures or book examples change.
Full packed smoke and the production website build passed. The published API
snapshot remains unchanged.

Registry replay now filters ordinary `IS` rows in SQL, retaining only the
`IS verb` rows its existing replay loop can use. Inverse/rename declarations,
transaction order, verb-shaped subject checks and qualifier exclusions retain
their previous behavior. The 1,000-event no-shape automation fixture passed
exact results and quiet-cycle assertions in 0.81 s, down from the earlier
2.49 s observation. All 116 store, 31 action and 54 automation tests pass,
including reopening and external declaration refresh. The workspace builds.
The store reference documents the optimization; public APIs, language and
book examples are unchanged. Populated-shape index rebuilding remains a
separate scaling cost.
Packed verification exposed a fragile HTTP check: `curl | grep -q` can close
the pipe before curl finishes, returning curl status 23 under `pipefail` for
a valid page. A local HTTP reproduction with a complete doctype response
returned 23 with the old pipeline and zero when grep consumed the response.
Smoke now consumes complete page/entity responses while retaining content
checks and transport failures. The original smoke failure did not preserve
curl's individual status, so this proves the pipeline defect rather than its
exclusive responsibility for that occurrence.
The final packed smoke run passed with the unchanged API snapshot, as did the
production website build and all ten fixed performance budgets. The HTTP
pipeline rationale is preserved in IMPLEMENTATION.md; no book command or
published API changed.
The shaped fixture also passed all 1,000 owner/cardinality checks and quiet
write assertions, measuring 17.33 s compared with the preceding 19.05 s run.

Populated-shape evaluation now separates narrow ordinary facts from full
declaration rows. Target/value indexes do not need the other stored columns;
declaration reports still retain their complete provenance rows. Filtering the
declaration source by verb before latest-series grouping preserves identity.
The populated-shape 1,000-event benchmark passed all exact result, cardinality
and quiet-cycle assertions in 19.05 s, compared with the prior 26.72 s local
observation. All 152 shape/action/automation tests and the workspace build pass.
The bounded query contract is now one probe plus four snapshot reads; metadata
preservation has a direct row-equality regression. Package references explain
the tradeoff. Public signatures and book semantics are unchanged. Scaling
remains unresolved: each action still rebuilds the current fact indexes.
The website build, all ten fixed performance budgets, and packed-package smoke
passed. Smoke initially detected a declaration import-format change; separating
the runtime SQL import from the original type-only import restored the existing
API snapshot without updating it.

`pnpm bench:automation --shapes` now exercises a live exactly-one owner
requirement on each handled entity, with every action writing both state and
owner. The 100/500/1,000-event run passed exact owner/entity sets, all final
shape checks, successful completion and write-free quiet cycles. Node 26.5.0 /
SQLite 3.53.3 on macOS arm64 measured 0.33/6.69/26.72 s active and
5.0/23.0/47.8 ms quiet. This confirms populated-shape scaling remains expensive;
the empty-shape fast path does not resolve it. The workload reports its mode
and check count separately from the default fixture. Root and automate
references document the new mode; no public runtime API or book example
changes. Next investigate incremental or narrower shape snapshots while
preserving full gate semantics, including taxonomy, new expectations,
cardinality, units, and rollback. Avoid caching an entire pre-action result
without accounting for changes between actions.

CPU profiling of the automation workload attributed most sampled time to shape
snapshot reads and index construction, with registry rebuilds another visible
cost. Shape evaluation now first probes for any historical `EXPECTS` row and
returns an empty report when none exists. It rechecks on every call; no cached
absence can bypass shapes introduced by a gated write. Existing declarations,
including disabled/qualified history, conservatively retain the full snapshot.
The 1,000-event benchmark fell from 22.23 s to 2.49 s with exact results and
zero quiet-cycle writes. All 67 shape, 31 action and 54 automation tests pass,
including first-shape rollback and declaration changes after an empty check.
Fixed query-count tests now expect one probe plus four snapshot reads after
the narrower-fact follow-up, rather than the original three reads alone.
Package references document
the path and measured scope; public contracts and book examples remain valid.
Further scaling work must cover stores with populated shape declarations and
remaining registry refresh costs, rather than extrapolating this no-shape case.
The full workspace suite passed all 1,310 tests. Workspace/website builds,
packed-package smoke with the unchanged API snapshot, and all ten fixed
performance budgets also passed.

The new `pnpm bench:automation` diagnostic exercises real derivation,
automation triggers and actions at 100/500/1,000 events. All three runs passed
exact entity-set, firing-count, successful completion and quiet-cycle/no-write
checks. Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3 on macOS arm64 measured active times of
0.45 s, 10.05 s and 39.59 s; quiet times were 4.2/19.6/37.6 ms. The observed
near-quadratic growth is unresolved. Named action attributes now use targeted
latest-row queries; an isolated repeat reduced 1,000-event time to 22.23 s,
with exact outcomes and write-free quiet cycles preserved. All 30 action and
54 automation tests pass, including fresh hook changes and cross-source
retractions. Continue profiling registry/shape work and remaining action
enumeration, which still materializes current beliefs. Preserve declaration
refresh, transactional checks and source-series semantics when optimizing.
The diagnostic is intentionally separate from the fixed-budget gate and
excludes external hooks/agents. Root and automate references document its
command, timing scope and findings; existing public APIs and book sessions
need no changes. The measurement requirement now has evidence, but automation
scaling improvement remains required work in this review.
The targeted-lookup change passed the workspace and production website builds
and packed-package smoke with the unchanged API snapshot. The act README
records why selecting the newest raw row preserves current-series semantics
and why disabled rows must participate; no book or public API change is needed.

The performance gate passed all ten recorded workloads on Node 22.18.0 /
SQLite 3.50.2 and Node 26.5.0 / SQLite 3.53.3, on this macOS arm64 host.
Reports now include actual runtime/platform metadata separately from the
baseline's `node-22` label. The root README clarifies that view timings cover
their recorded call counts and that fixed in-memory fixtures do not establish
production disk throughput or larger automation performance. Thresholds were
not changed. Resolution measured about 21 ms against its 500 ms budget on both
runtimes; the 5,000-row cold scoped view measured 56 ms and 52 ms against 2,500
ms. These are individual local observations, not cross-platform guarantees.
Runtime report metadata is a developer diagnostic addition; package contracts,
CLI examples, specification and book sessions need no corresponding edit.

Homepage copy review found an uncaught clipboard rejection with no recovery
feedback. Copy now catches denied and unavailable clipboard access, announces
the failure, and provides a read-only command field that selects all text on
focus. A later successful retry removes the fallback and announces success.
Browser regressions cover both failure modes, keyboard selection, exact copied
text, successful retry, and absence of page errors. The website README records
the interaction; language, CLI/package APIs and book content are unaffected.
The production build, all nine website unit tests and all 25 browser tests
passed. Both clipboard tests also passed after refining their screenshot
capture. Visual inspection at 320px confirms the fallback message and selected
command fit the viewport with a visible keyboard-focus outline.

Website navigation review found that page destinations used buttons with hash
assignment callbacks, preventing native link menus and new-tab navigation.
Header, homepage, footer and documentation destinations now use anchors, with
the existing button appearance where appropriate. Action controls remain
buttons. Browser coverage follows link semantics and adds a middle-click
regression that verifies a document opens in another tab without navigating
the original page. The website README records the interaction contract;
language, CLI, package API and book content are unaffected.
The production build, all nine website unit tests and all 23 browser tests
passed. Visual inspection of the 320px homepage and 1280px documentation page
confirmed the retained layout and navigation styling. Native middle-click
opened the requested document in another tab while preserving the original
overview page.

Keyboard review reproduced a missing focus outline on the playground dataset
selector: its local `outline: 0` overrode the shared focus-visible rule.
Removing that reset restores the common two-pixel outline. The production
browser regression reaches the selector with Shift+Tab and checks both focus
and computed outline style/width. The website README includes this control in
the documented keyboard coverage; language, package APIs and book behavior
are unaffected.
The production website build and all 22 browser tests passed. The focused
toolbar screenshot was inspected and shows the selector's outline clearly.
The regression failed against the previous build with computed outline style
`none`, then passed with `solid` and width `2px` after the reset was removed.

The playground review found that editing claims and then querying removed the
only transient explanation that queries still use the stored database. The
query panel now persistently identifies unapplied edits, with an accessible
description on the query input. Successful rebuild/append records the submitted
text; failures keep the previous applied text, and restoring it clears the
notice. Browser regressions exercise query, undo, append, and failed/successful
rebuild behavior. The website README documents the enhancement; no language,
package API, CLI, or book contract changes.
The production website build, all nine website unit tests, and all 22 browser
tests passed. The new 390px screenshot was visually inspected: the notice fits
above the query button without clipping. Automated accessible-description
checks pass; this does not constitute manual assistive-technology testing.

Runtime follow-up passed all 104 solver/adapter tests on Node 24.0.0 and all
27 adapter tests on Node 22.18.0, complementing the 77 portable solver tests
already checked on Node 22. Both versions then passed three large forced-GC
cycles each on this macOS arm64 host: all twelve large checks were unsatisfied,
and all six subsequent recovery optimizations returned exact optimum `3000`
with every assignment verified. The runtime CI matrix now includes both
solver suites and the large diagnostic, with a five-minute step timeout.
The workflow parses, all five existing runtime-contract checks pass, and the
production website builds. The benchmark reference now distinguishes its
historical measurements from current configured coverage. Package and
implementation references describe the new gate; no user-facing model/CLI or
book behavior changes. Hosted Linux/Windows and pinned matrix executions remain
to be verified after CI runs; local version checks do not establish those OS
results. This turn changes CI coverage and documentation, not runtime code.

Deep explanation input rendering failed on Node 22.18.0 with a native
`JSON.stringify` stack overflow, while the same regression passed on Node 26.
Text rendering now serializes validated payloads iteratively. Regressions cover
20,000-level records and arrays in value/authored-value fields and compare
ordinary mixed JSON output with native serialization. The solver README and
implementation guide document the supported-runtime rationale; existing book
examples, model API and website flows need no corresponding contract changes.
All 77 solver tests passed on Node 22.18.0 and Node 26.5.0. The workspace and
production website builds and packed-package smoke passed with the unchanged
public API snapshot. This adds two regressions after the preceding 1,305-test
full-workspace run; that full suite was not repeated for this focused change.

The Z3 memory investigation reproduced incorrect optimization and native AST
cleanup crashes with `test:memory-stress --large`. The adapter now defers native
reference cleanup during its asynchronous checks and drains it on settlement,
including rejection. Three independent guarded runs passed all nine cycles:
18 large-model checks and nine exact recovery optima of `3000`, with every
assignment verified. Repeats ran alongside workspace tests and packed smoke.
The removed bug's lasting cause and ownership rationale live in the solver
README and IMPLEMENTATION.md, and the large diagnostic remains a reproducible
regression. This prevents the observed cleanup race; it is not a promise to
recover from arbitrary native corruption. No model API, CLI, website flow,
or book contract changed. Cleanup ordering/rejection tests and all 27 adapter
tests passed. The final workspace suite passed all 1,305 tests; workspace and
production website builds and packed-package smoke passed with the unchanged
public API snapshot.

The partial-policy follow-up reproduced a wrong winner when a claim combined
a negative-precedence source with an unmatched source. SQL aggregation ignored
the unmatched NULL instead of applying neutral precedence `0` per source.
Ranked and resolved SQL now apply defaults before aggregation, consistent with
the JavaScript policy scoring path. A real-store regression checks both the
score and the winner. The store README records the explicit-policy boundary;
the built-in policy and CLI/book examples already include a root entry, so
their documented behavior and public API signatures are unchanged.
All 116 store tests and 95 query tests passed, as did the workspace build,
production website build, and packed-package smoke with the existing API
snapshot. The preceding full-workspace run remains the 1,302-test baseline;
this follow-up adds one focused regression.

The calendar range review confirmed that validity uses the end of the right
period, as specified in §32.2; a right period whose start precedes the left
anchor can still form a nonempty range. Tightening that check to compare
period starts would incorrectly reject supported overlapping periods.
The resolution review reproduced invalid SQL from the exported helpers with
an empty explicit policy. They now emit an empty policy relation and retain
neutral precedence `0` and reliability `1`; a regression exercises both ranked
and resolved rows against a real store. The store README documents this
low-level contract. Store-level defaults, CLI, website copy, specification,
and book behavior are unaffected and need no corresponding text changes.
Validation passed all 1,302 workspace tests, the workspace and production
website builds, and packed-package smoke checks with the existing API snapshot.
This includes the mixed-range trajectory regression from the preceding review.

At the start of the review, `pnpm test` reported 1,088 passing tests and
`pnpm build` passed on Node 26.5.0. This establishes a local baseline only;
other supported runtimes, packaged artifacts, and external release state need
separate evidence. The representative performance gate also passed all ten
budgets locally, covering import/export, resolution, shapes, bounded and
transitive queries, and sensitivity-scoped views.

The website review found and fixed narrow-screen grid/navigation overflow,
destructive failure during playground rebuilds, and documentation section
links that navigated to the home page. Production-browser regressions now cover
these paths, and documentation link checks visit every bundled document.
The live behavior and rationale belong in `website/README.md`,
`ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `DOCUMENTATION.md`.

The connector failure-path review added coverage for missing-key pruning,
unkeyed formatting failures, and declared-source transitions with mixed valid
and failed records. Pruning now waits for reliable identities, and declaration
replacements commit only when all records succeed. The connector's 86 tests,
CLI failure reporting, and Chapter 14 examples pass; the book PDF was rebuilt
with pinned Typst 0.15.0 and the affected pages inspected. These checks cover
those failure paths, not all ingestion and synchronization invariants.

The diagnostics review added a read-only `store.search` check for missing,
duplicate, orphaned, and stale FTS content entries, and removed private paths
and source details from text-store failure reports. Doctor regressions cover
both human and JSON output and verify that database bytes remain unchanged.
Chapter 28 examples and the rebuilt PDF were checked.

`make smoke` passed against packed npm artifacts: public API snapshots, ESM
imports under NodeNext and Bundler, optional Z3 execution, parser/store/query
round trips, actions, reports, connectors, MCP initialization, derivation,
resolution, reconstruction/evaluation, sync and branching, automation, HTTP
views, highlighting, and the demo. This establishes installed-layout coverage
on the local runtime; deeper invariant review and the other CI platforms remain
separate work.

The action review fixed a race between precondition checks and write-lock
acquisition, including revoked action declarations, and stale inverse
vocabulary on already-open connections. Regression tests use two real store
connections with a deterministic boundary interleaving; a separate test proves
standalone hooks see committed effects. Chapter 18 examples pass. Caller-owned
transaction hooks are now guarded using the store callback's `outermost`
context: configured hooks that would fire reject and roll back only the action
savepoint, while no-op, dry-run, and hook-free actions remain nestable. Tests
cover outer commit and rollback, preserving earlier caller writes, and shared
transaction-context behavior on Node SQLite and browser SQLite WASM. The
synchronous hook result contract and the rejection rationale are documented in
the specification, action/store references, architecture, and book.

The derivation review reproduced and fixed firing a rule revoked immediately
before its write reservation, plus stale inverse vocabulary on an already-open
connection. Rule selection, watermarks, registry refresh, and derived writes
now share a write reservation. All 31 rule tests and 31 automation tests pass,
as do the root and website builds and Chapter 17 examples. The specification,
rule reference, architecture, and rebuilt book document this behavior; the
affected PDF pages were inspected. Rule lifecycle and broader automation
concurrency still need review.

The rule-retraction review also reproduced a declaration added just before the
write reservation surviving a successful retraction, and a newly ambiguous
digest prefix still retracting a rule. Declaration selection and ambiguity
checks now run inside the retraction transaction. Two real-connection
regressions pass with all 33 rule tests, and the root build passes. The rule
reference, specification, architecture, and rebuilt book describe the boundary;
the affected PDF page was inspected.

After both rule fixes, the full workspace test suite and production website
build pass. The workspace suite includes the executable book sessions and
CLI integration checks; this remains local-runtime evidence rather than a
substitute for the remaining system review or cross-platform CI.

The automation review reproduced duplicate claims by competing settlers,
firing a declaration revoked during an earlier prompt, stale inverse vocabulary
when derivation is disabled, and external execution inside caller-owned
transactions. Each batch now reloads its declaration and vocabulary, evaluates
triggers, and commits its watermark under one write reservation before running
steps. Settling rejects caller-owned transactions before deriving or claiming
anything. All 36 automation tests pass, including a peer-connection check that
agent execution sees the committed watermark and allows another writer to
claim a later event without replaying the first. The package reference,
specification, architecture, and rebuilt book document the crash and revocation
boundaries; the affected PDF pages were inspected.
An initial implementation repeatedly parsed all declarations for each batch;
checking the database version inside the reservation now permits reuse until
another write occurs. A local scaling probe with derivation disabled measured
500 inactive automations at about 71 ms, down from 4,785 ms in the initial fix
(100: 12 ms versus 232 ms). These are local measurements, not portable budgets.
The final implementation passes the full workspace suite (1,109 tests), root
build, and packed-artifact smoke checks. The production website build also
passes, and the full suite replays the book sessions.

Automation completion reporting now distinguishes a quiet final pass from
pass-limit exhaustion. `complete` is explicit in reports and the packed API;
`settled(report)` requires it, text output says `incomplete`, and `--once`
returns nonzero when work remains. Regressions cover JSON and text, resumption
without replaying steps, and a long rule derivation completed with a higher
derivation limit before retrying. All 40 automation tests and the root build
pass; packed-artifact smoke checks pass with the updated API snapshot. The
specification, package and CLI references, architecture, and rebuilt book
describe the behavior, and affected PDF pages were inspected.
The full workspace suite then passed all 1,113 tests, including book sessions
and CLI integration checks; the production website build also passed.

The cancellation review reproduced ignored pre-cancellation, recording a late
agent reply and running later steps after cancellation, and a busy watch loop
starving shutdown callbacks. `settle` now accepts `signal` and checks it before
work and between execution boundaries; `watchCycle` yields between settles.
Startup cancellation exits without starting polling. All 44 automation tests
pass, including a daemon integration test that leaves an unclaimed event for
the next run. Documentation records the committed-watermark boundary, custom
callback cancellation responsibility, and the distinction between bounded
settle calls and a watch cycle that keeps running while writes continue.
The full workspace suite passed all 1,117 tests, including real CLI process
cancellation and cleanup. Root and production website builds, packed-artifact
smoke checks, and API snapshot verification passed; the book was rebuilt and
the affected pages visually inspected.

The rule-error propagation review reproduced successful automation results and
zero `--once` exit codes despite malformed stored rules. Enabled derivation now
adds those errors to the structured problem list, so both JSON and text report
failure while valid declarations continue. Tests cover disabling derivation and
recovery after removing the bad rule; all 47 automation tests and the root build
pass. Packed-artifact checks and the production website build pass, and the
updated book page was visually inspected.

The declaration-prelude review fixed failed-input caching across rules,
actions, and automations. Each API now refreshes stored vocabulary and validates
the whole prelude before consulting even a legacy digest. Invalid preludes
reject the call without appending prelude rows or declarations. Six shared
regressions cover atomic failure, repeated errors, unchanged successful retries,
corrected input, registry isolation, and legacy cached failures. CLI regressions
also caught and fixed successful exit codes despite rule-file declaration
errors in both text and JSON. The fixed bug entry was removed; the failure
contract is documented in the specification, package references, architecture,
and all three relevant book chapters. Packed-artifact checks and root/website
builds pass; changed book pages and their following pages were inspected.
The workspace run exercised 1,128 tests and found one legacy assertion expecting
success despite rule-file errors. That assertion was updated to require failure
and verify that a valid sibling rule still fires; all 108 CLI tests then passed.
Every other workspace test had passed in the full run.

The synchronization review reproduced database-file merges throwing on detach
inside caller-owned transactions after copying rows, and dry runs leaving the
source attached. Database-file sync now checks transaction ownership before
attaching; self-sync remains a no-op, and annotated-text sync remains nestable.
All 25 sync tests pass, including preserving earlier caller writes, no leaked
attachments, standalone retry, and text commit/rollback/dry-run behavior. Root
and website builds and packed-artifact smoke checks pass. The specification,
package reference, architecture, and rebuilt book explain SQLite's attachment
constraint and the supported text-sync alternative; changed PDF pages were
visually inspected. Identity-collision handling still needs review as part of
the broader sync audit.

Text sync now reserves its transaction before refreshing vocabulary,
canonicalizing input, and validating annotations. Two real-connection
regressions reproduced inverse relations stored in the wrong direction after
peer vocabulary writes, including writes immediately before reservation.
The fix shares one reservation through replay. All 28 sync tests pass, including
dry-run restoration of the prior registry, unchanged rows, preserved UUID state,
and the existing nested-text-sync contract. Root and website builds and packed
smoke checks pass; the updated book pages were visually inspected.

The general store ingest review reproduced the same stale-vocabulary issue
with ordinary appends, including a peer commit immediately before lock
acquisition. Ingest now canonicalizes inside the write reservation and uses
SQLite's data-version counter to refresh only after peer commits. Rollback
restores the registry and version marker together, preventing strict failures
from hiding peer vocabulary on retry. Regression coverage includes Node
interleavings plus shared Node/WASM strict and nested rollback behavior. All
1,139 workspace tests, all ten performance budgets, root and website builds,
and packed-artifact smoke checks pass. The specification, store reference,
architecture, and rebuilt book document the boundary and the responsibility
of pre-canonicalized-result and raw-SQL callers; changed PDF pages were inspected.

The text-sync identity review reproduced a reused ID naming different content
being silently skipped while new lineage attached to the existing row. Text
replay now compares canonical interchange content against existing target rows
before any replay; equivalent raw spellings and reordered metadata remain
accepted. Regressions cover changed facts, confidence, contexts, tags, comments,
and legitimate added lineage. All 1,141 workspace tests, root/website builds,
and packed checks pass; updated book pages were inspected. The follow-up confidence regressions reproduced rounding changing small positive
beliefs to retractions, near-certain beliefs to certainty, and distinct same-ID
content to equal text. Canonical emission now uses the new `Confidence.formatExact`
API, while presentation formatting retains its rounding. Parsing shifts decimal
text before its single numeric conversion. Tests cover 500 deterministic finite
binary values, computed and subnormal values, plain import, exact replicas, and
same-ID precision conflicts. All 1,144 workspace tests, root/website builds, and packed smoke checks pass.
The public API snapshot includes `formatExact`; the rebuilt book pages were
visually inspected. Database-source identity verification now rejects differing claim data,
contexts, tags, and explicit provenance before any rows or edges copy. It
accepts reordered metadata, raw spelling differences, inferred provenance,
and legacy stores without dimension tables. Regressions exercise atomic
failure, dry runs, JSON/text CLI errors, incremental edges, and text replay.
The root/website builds and packed smoke pass; updated book pages were inspected.
A local 5,000-row repeat sync with metadata completed in 24 ms. The book's ingestion session exposed an integration failure: strict ingestion
staged through lossy text and ignored a rejected final merge. It now uses an
exact SQLite snapshot and checks that report, with regressions for preserved
provenance and an agent changing an existing identity. The adjacent provenance review reproduced explicit dimensions disappearing in
annotated exports. Transaction annotations now carry an optional JSON object
when context inference cannot reconstruct stored dimensions. Replay validates
complete dimension sets, rejects unknown or malformed data and identity
mismatches before writing, and preserves empty sets. Legacy bare annotations
retain inference; plain import ignores annotation metadata. Database copying
now preserves a present dimension table exactly and infers only when absent.
Regressions cover actor/evidence ambiguity, explicit runs/domains, lineages,
repeated IDs, plain imports, dry runs, reopening, and database interoperability.
The public parser/canonical payload readers and provenance parse/normalize
helpers are included in the packed API snapshot. MCP export remains plain
canonical text; annotated replication uses store export or CLI `--tx`.
All 1,154 workspace tests pass, with additional focused provenance-object and
Unicode-label checks. Root/website builds and packed smoke pass; updated book
pages were rendered and inspected.


The read-side audit verified that text-backed stores deliberately retain plain
import semantics, including ignoring transaction/provenance annotations;
identity-preserving materialization uses sync. Live SQLite query connections,
however, reproduced stale inverse and lifecycle vocabulary after another writer
committed. Registry access and inverse reads now check `data_version` and
refresh on external commits without writing. Regressions use normal and
read-only connections and preserve rollback of staged declarations while
retaining committed peer vocabulary. All 1,156 workspace tests and ten
performance budgets pass, as do root/website builds and packed smoke. The book
was rebuilt and visually checked, including keeping its chapter summary on
one page.

The historical-query audit verified boundary-specific vocabulary reconstruction
and resolution policy. It reproduced paginated empty snapshots bypassing syntax
and temporal-option validation. Empty pages now use ordinary bounded compilation
and validation; API and CLI regressions cover malformed patterns, invalid time
anchors, inverse attributes, and incompatible options on empty and populated
stores. A separate real-sync probe reproduced repeated results when older IDs
arrive below a cursor's transaction cutoff. Pagination now guards its historical
universe using counts and rowid tails for claims and touching lineage, checked
before and after page materialization. Stale or obsolete cursors fail with a
restart instruction; wholly future appends remain compatible. Regressions cover
real database/text sync, new edges without new historical rows, writes during
record projection, cursor validation, and CLI text/JSON and MCP error surfaces.
The cursor encoding is version 2 while the public page envelope stays v1.
All 1,164 workspace tests and ten performance budgets pass, together with
root/website builds and packed smoke; updated book pages were inspected.

The identity-format audit verified that query boundary parsing normalizes UUID
case while annotated replay requires canonical lowercase storage. Low-level
`insertResult({ ids })` nevertheless accepted malformed IDs and observed valid
future IDs before discovering later failures. It now validates every used ID
before insertion or receive-clock observation. Shared Node/WASM regressions
verify rows, vocabulary, and generator state remain unchanged after rejection.
Database sync now validates every source row's canonical UUIDv7 and `id = tx`
identity before copying, including dry runs. All 1,167 workspace tests, ten
performance budgets, root/website builds, and packed smoke pass; updated book
pages were rendered and inspected.

Historical vocabulary now bounds qualifier parents at the same boundary as
its declarations. A later WHEN/VIA/BECAUSE parent previously removed an older
inverse from earlier queries; the regression reproduced this before the fix.
Shared Node/WASM tests cover verb declarations, inverse pairs, renames, whole-day
exclusive upper bounds, and exact parent-transaction inclusion. Pagination's
touching-lineage guard remains conservatively broader than vocabulary alone.
All 1,170 workspace tests, ten performance budgets, root/website builds, and
packed smoke pass; regenerated book pages were inspected.

The playground accessibility review found that asynchronous results and errors
had no live-region semantics, and local CSS removed focus outlines from the
claims editor and query input. Results now have a named polite live region and
a keyboard tab stop; all three workbench controls retain visible focus, with
inset outlines on clipped surfaces. The recovery browser regression checks the
live-region contract, keyboard order, and computed focus styles alongside real
worker results and errors. The production build, all 13 browser tests, and all
eight website runtime tests pass. The in-app browser was unavailable; actual
screen-reader announcements have not been manually verified. Website README
and changeset document the behavior; no language, API, CLI, or book contract
changes are involved.

The HTTP view review found a navigation race: an older request could replace
the current entity, search, or history page after the URL had changed. The
shipped page now guards successful and failed responses by navigation generation;
malformed fragments render an escaped error and allow subsequent navigation.
A regression executes the actual shipped routing code with deliberately reordered
responses and checks both recovery and stale-error suppression. HEAD API responses
now preserve GET cache-protection headers, and rejected methods receive the same
no-store policy as other errors. HTTP regressions cover GET/HEAD success and error
parity. All 53 view tests, the full workspace suite, root/website builds, and
packed smoke pass. Live references and the book were updated; changed PDF pages
were rendered and inspected. Lifecycle cleanup and remaining view/report edges
remain part of the broader review.

Report and automation substitution now scan original template tokens once.
The earlier sequential replacements reinterpreted variable-like text inside
inserted values; automation additionally treated `$&`, `$$`, and related text
as JavaScript replacement directives. Real report queries and an automation
firing now verify that these values survive unchanged. Report citation placement
is resolved before inserting bindings, so stored `[^?]` text remains data even
for uncited transitive results and default bullets. Generated footnote labels
skip labels occurring in the original template, including case variants and
code examples, preserving authored references and reusing labels for repeated
row citations. The view and automation focused suites, root/website builds, and
packed smoke pass; live documentation and regenerated book pages were checked.
The full workspace run also passes all 1,175 tests with no failures.

## Completion evidence matrix

This section retains earlier review passes and the matrix used at that
checkpoint. Its “review still required” column is historical planning evidence;
the active scope and verification map are maintained at the top of this file.
Later fixes and checks are recorded above. This matrix is not a completed
requirement-by-requirement audit of the current worktree.

Scenario snapshot metadata now uses the same `QuerySql.asOfBoundary` parser as
binding queries. Regressions reproduced rejection of valid year/month boundaries
and verified calendar-date rejection even for zero-binding definitions, plus
whole-day and case-normalized exact-UUID behavior. A separate regression caught
inherited overlay lookups for valid names such as `constructor`; missing entries
now require own keys. All 19 scenario tests, root/website builds, and packed
smoke pass. Live references and the book were updated; both affected PDF pages
were rendered and inspected.

Scenario definition policy validation now checks snapshot modes, cardinality,
many-value reductions, expected value kinds, all four input policies, and the
Boolean override flag before database access. Unknown choices previously fell
through to other behavior. A closed-store regression verifies typed
`invalid-definition` failures before any read, and its failure without the new
guards was confirmed after correcting test cleanup. All 20 scenario tests,
root/website builds, and packed smoke pass; the changed book page was inspected.
Scenario materialization now guards peer commit revisions and local change
counts around its reads, accounting separately for the overlay's rolled-back
inserts. A reproduced race previously paired a null snapshot head with claims
that arrived after capture. The fix returns `snapshot-changed` before evaluation;
tests cover peer and local writes, a backdated peer commit after overlay
rollback, retry success, and stable binding on a read-only connection. All 22
scenario tests and all 1,186 workspace tests pass, along with root/website
builds and packed smoke. The public error contract, references, and book were
updated; affected PDF pages were inspected.

Scenario recording now validates the full generated claim before either a
write or predecessor lookup. A regression first demonstrated that a newline in
a caller-supplied ID could introduce two valid CAVE claims; the writer accepted
the first without checking the complete parse. Records now require exactly one
claim, no edges, the exact intended entity subject, and the expected artifact
payload. Tests verify rejection without writes, preservation of a valid existing
result, successor-record validation, and ordinary slash-separated IDs. All 15
scenario tests, root/website builds, and packed smoke pass. The package reference,
architecture, and book were updated; the changed PDF page was inspected.
The subsequent scenario history regression reproduced reuse of a retracted
result ID for different content. Writers now validate every payload in the
claim series inside the write transaction. Retraction still makes the record
absent to reads and predecessor checks; an explicit identical-content write
can restore it. Tests cover conflicting reuse, idempotent restoration, and
contradictory older history hidden by a matching latest payload. All 16 scenario
tests, root/website builds, and packed smoke pass; the changed book page was
rendered and inspected.

The canonical artifact serializer review reproduced silent sparse-array
conversion to null and loss of non-JSON object contents. It now validates dense
JSON arrays and plain objects, rejects cycles with a path-specific TypeError,
and preserves shared non-cyclic references. Optional undefined object fields
remain omitted, keys remain sorted, and reordered equivalent JSON remains
idempotent. Regression failures were confirmed before the fix; all 17 scenario
tests, root/website builds, and packed smoke pass. The package reference,
architecture, and book were updated, and the changed PDF page was inspected.
The full workspace run passes all 1,181 tests with no failures.

Scenario explanation conversion previously accepted a changed binding query
when scenario ID and model digest remained unchanged. The regression reproduced
that mismatch before adding `definitionDigest` to frozen inputs. It covers the
complete authored definition and is itself covered by the input-record digest.
Explanation conversion verifies both digests before attaching queries to evidence;
tests reject changed queries/policies, edited values, and missing bindings while
preserving JSON round trips. Legacy artifacts remain readable but require
rebinding for this conversion; new evaluations use new run IDs. All 1,181
workspace tests, root/website builds, and packed smoke pass. The public API
snapshot includes the new required digest field, with a minor changeset and
documented migration. Updated book pages were rendered and inspected.

Fusion boundary regressions first reproduced invalid-confidence acceptance,
non-finite means, inherited unit-name conversion, and intermediate overflow.
The library now validates every estimate and all conditional/hypothesis
probabilities, restricts duration conversion to own table entries, and uses
normalized square-root precision factors. Multiplying those factors separately
preserves a tiny weight's representable contribution from a large mean.
Posteriors whose positive precision or spread cannot be represented fail with
a range error; an MCP regression checks that this becomes a tool error.
All 1,178 workspace tests passed, followed by final arithmetic checks (18 fusion
tests), 73 MCP tests and four focused fusion-tool tests. Root/website builds
and final packed smoke pass. Specification, references, architecture, and the
book were updated; the changed PDF page was rendered and inspected.

Runtime compatibility was exercised locally on macOS arm64 with the exact
Node 22.18.0 minimum and the CI-pinned Node 24.18.0. Each passed 548 tests:
all loop, store, query, sync, action, rule, automation, and view test files,
plus `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts` and `runtime-contract.test.ts`. The binaries
were selected with `pnpm dlx node@<version>` and their versions checked first.
Node 24's first run, concurrent with Node 22, failed the missing-store doctor
test after approximately its three-second pnpm-probe budget. That test passed
in isolation; the complete selection then passed with `--test-concurrency=1`.
This is evidence of a load-sensitive probe, not proof of a runtime defect.
Its assertion now preserves the diagnostic JSON when it fails. These runs do
not establish Linux or Windows execution results for this uncommitted worktree.
Grammar artifact verification, the incremental TypeScript no-op check, and the
default website's solver-asset exclusion check also pass on the current tree.

The shape review aligned runtime readers and transaction gates with generated
clients: reserved cardinality/unit tags now reject duplicates, invalid values,
and units on relation expectations. The shared validator retains duplicate tag
rows instead of silently selecting one. This is an intentional semantic
strengthening, recorded as a minor changeset. All 57 shape tests pass, including
malformed declaration and atomic rollback regressions; root/website builds,
packed smoke, and the pinned book build pass. The changed PDF pages were
rendered and inspected, and the normative specification and live references
were updated together.

The first workspace run after the shape change reported one cancellation-test
failure: its descendant marker existed. That test passed 20 isolated repeats.
The old fixture wrote the marker 700 ms after startup, which does not establish
whether the write preceded cancellation, and announced readiness before spawning
the descendant. The fixture now waits for descendant readiness and enables its
survival probe only after CLI exit. No production process-cleanup defect was
established by the original ambiguous observation; the ordered probe retains
coverage of surviving descendants. The final workspace run passed all 1,188
tests, including the ordered cancellation regression and book sessions.

Further shape review found a silent 32-hop taxonomy cutoff. Regression tests
proved that evaluation omitted deep instances and the write gate accepted them
without required fields. Traversal now reaches every descendant with a visited
set to terminate cycles. An 80-level cyclic taxonomy checks each instance once,
and a deep incomplete append rolls back. The deterministic benchmark still
uses three SQL reads for 10,000 checks (4.544 ms in this local run).

The standalone append gate also read baseline violations before reserving its
transaction. A deterministic two-connection regression proved that a peer
could repair a violation in that gap, after which the gate allowed reintroducing
it as supposedly pre-existing. Baseline evaluation now runs inside the same
reserved transaction as ingestion and the final check. All 60 shape tests pass.
Both changes have patch changesets, updated normative and package references,
architecture explanations, and rebuilt book pages inspected at pages 42–43.
The final workspace run passes all 1,191 tests. Root and website builds,
packed smoke, and all ten performance budgets pass.
Remaining shape review includes health-report aggregation and alias discovery;
these targeted fixes do not establish those separate contracts.

Health-report review reproduced a stack overflow with a 12,000-link alias
chain, then a SQLite parameter-limit failure with 33,000 links after the
recursive walk was removed. Health and discovery now share iterative path
compression; health aggregation loads non-alias rows once and groups them in
memory, retaining transaction order and avoiding a parameter per member.
Group construction appends in place rather than copying the growing array.
A real 33,000-link regression retains the disagreement between the endpoint
names; a separate 12,000-link discovery regression preserves exclusion through
infrastructure names. The original discovery regression already passed; the
confirmed stack failure was in health reporting. All 62 shape tests pass.
The specification, package reference, architecture, and book explain the
complete closure behavior; the rebuilt PDF pages 43–44 were inspected.
The final workspace run passes all 1,193 tests. Root and website builds
and packed smoke pass.
A numeric-unit probe also confirmed that differing units remain visible in
stored value text and already produce a health disagreement; no fix was needed.
Remaining review includes report option validation, scope aggregation, and
alias-discovery candidate scoring, ordering, and write lifecycle.

Shape reader option review found that the CLI rejected malformed thresholds
and stale horizons while the library silently accepted them. Discovery now
requires a finite 0..1 score and a positive safe-integer limit; health reporting
requires a finite non-negative stale-day horizon and a finite clock result.
Validation precedes database reads, including empty or closed stores. The CLI
also rejects unsafe suggestion-limit integers. The stricter library contract
has a minor changeset and aligned references; fractional stale-day horizons
remain supported. All 64 shape tests and four focused CLI tests pass. The
aliases chapter now describes candidate selection rather than claiming that
every possible entity pair is scored. Root and website builds and packed smoke
pass; the final workspace run passes all 1,195 tests. Rebuilt PDF pages 41
and 43 were rendered and inspected. Discovery ordering and write lifecycle,
and health scope aggregation, remain to be reviewed.

Alias write lifecycle review reproduced revival of a retracted suggestion
from a retained proposal list. Suggestion writes now reserve their transaction
before checking pair history in both directions, skip any recorded review, and
deduplicate input pairs. Regressions cover retained proposals, a real peer
review committed immediately before reservation, reverse-direction history,
and duplicate input. The history recheck deliberately preserves pair decisions
without rerunning candidate scoring or an external judge on changed evidence.
This boundary is documented in the specification and package reference.

The CLI also returned JSON before processing `--write`, silently suppressing
the requested append. Combined `--json --write` now writes and returns selected
`suggestions` plus the actual `appended` count, including a zero-result rerun;
plain JSON remains an array. A CLI regression checks database state after the
combined flags, and the changed output contract has a minor changeset. All 66
shape tests and four focused suggestion CLI tests pass. The CLI help/reference,
architecture, and aliases chapter were aligned, and the rebuilt book page 41
was inspected. The final workspace run passes all 1,198 tests; root and
website builds and packed smoke pass.
Remaining discovery review includes candidate scoring and
ordering; health scope aggregation remains open.

Release source review found that publish preflight checked committed manifests
but accepted unstaged, staged, deleted, or untracked package source content.
Isolated Git fixtures reproduced all four cases. Publish mode now requires
clean tracked files and no non-ignored untracked files; ignored build products
remain allowed. The publish script repeats validation after preparation and
before npm mutation, in addition to its initial and final-tag checks. Workflow
contract coverage pins that ordering. No package or tag was published in this
review; the fixtures use local bare remotes.

Manual Marketplace republication also checked out a release tag while requiring
HEAD to equal the newer workflow GITHUB_SHA. A detached-tag fixture reproduced
the failure. Manual publish validation now accepts an explicit CAVE_RELEASE_TAG,
requires that tag to identify HEAD and match the committed release version,
and retains all main-reachability/version-commit/cleanliness checks. Other
workflows still require SHA equality and reject the tag override. The dispatch
workflow extracts the validator from its own workflow commit into RUNNER_TEMP,
then validates the tag checkout through CAVE_RELEASE_ROOT; old tags therefore
do not keep running their obsolete validator. Tests cover the manual target,
a missing target, push-event rejection, and unchanged ordinary SHA checks.
Contributor instructions, implementation/architecture references, changesets,
and the book were updated; PDF page 84 was rendered and inspected. Hosted
Marketplace execution and registry publication were not exercised. All 1,205
workspace tests, root/website builds, packed smoke, shell syntax and workflow
YAML checks pass. Remaining
release review includes registry-probe retry/error cases and artifact identity
across publication retries, with external Changesets work separately tracked.

Registry-probe tests reproduced three release classification failures: a
successful npm command with unexpected/empty output was treated as absence;
an npm failure exiting 4 collided with the missing-package sentinel; and zero
attempts performed no request yet also reached the unpublished path. Probes
now fail closed in all three cases. Attempts must be positive safe integers,
and initial delays integer seconds in 0..60, validated before requests and
normalized as decimal values. Only recognized missing responses use the
absence status; transport exit codes map to probe failure.

The new Bash-helper harness executes the actual functions with mocked npm and
sleep functions, without invoking the publish entrypoint or a registry. It
covers matching and unexpected replies, immediate absence, transport failure,
status collision, delayed post-publish visibility, capped backoff, decimal
leading zeros, zero delay, and malformed retry settings. The four probe tests
and 18 workflow-contract tests pass. Release instructions, architecture,
implementation notes, and the book were updated; rebuilt PDF page 84 was
inspected after tightening the prose to keep the invariant list on one page.
All 1,209 workspace tests pass. Root and final website builds, packed smoke,
and Bash syntax checks pass.
Remaining release review includes registry-error recognition and
artifact identity across publication retries; live publication is untested.

Registry-error recognition review reproduced a false absence when a connection
failure mentioned an e404 package URL. The probe now extracts explicit npm
error-code records (modern `npm error` and legacy `npm ERR!`), recognizing
absence only when the sole distinct code is E404. Prose, URL fragments, and
conflicting codes remain errors and follow the transport retry path. The npm
command explicitly selects plain, colorless output at error log level. Local
npm formatter/config source confirmed the code-record and formatting controls;
regressions cover both supported prefixes and misleading diagnostics. All five
registry-helper tests and 18 workflow-contract tests pass. The updated book
page 84 was rendered and inspected, and the owning release references were
aligned. All 1,210 workspace tests, root and final website builds, packed smoke,
and Bash syntax checks pass.
No registry publication was performed. Artifact identity across
publication retries remains a separate release-review item.

Publisher-root review reproduced a validation bypass through inherited
CAVE_RELEASE_ROOT: a dirty target checkout validated a separate clean fixture,
then reached preparation and recovery tagging. The entrypoint now exports its
own resolved root for all child commands, keeping initial checks, preparation,
publication, and final validation bound to the same checkout. Standalone
validator root overrides remain available for isolated fixtures and manual
Marketplace tag validation.

The entrypoint regression uses two real local Git repositories with local bare
remotes and mocked npm/pnpm. It verifies rejection before any registry probe
for initially dirty source, then verifies that preparation-induced source drift
prevents the recovery tag even when the inherited override names a clean tree.
All 49 release-validation, registry-probe, and workflow-contract tests pass.
Release instructions, implementation/architecture references, and the book
were updated; rebuilt PDF page 84 was inspected. No registry or Marketplace
publication was performed. All 1,211 workspace tests, root and website builds,
packed smoke, and Bash syntax checks pass. Registry artifact identity across interrupted
publication remains to be reviewed separately, including whether incremental
builds can retain altered ignored output and whether the clean-command
documentation matches the paths its implementation removes.

Release-output review reproduced an altered ignored JavaScript artifact
surviving the actual TypeScript incremental compiler during release
preparation. The fixture also planted an obsolete emitted file, which ordinary
incremental compilation cannot remove. The publisher now runs pnpm clean
