before grammar generation and compilation. The entrypoint regression uses the
real compiler and clean script, with mocked registry/package-manager surfaces,
and verifies both source-correct output and removal of the obsolete file on
the recovery path.

The real workspace clean, pinned grammar regeneration, and full TypeScript
build also pass; tracked grammar artifacts remain unchanged. The implementation
guide incorrectly said cleaning removed generated tree-sitter files: it removes
compiler outputs, bundles, VSIX files, staged legal files, and build metadata,
while committed grammar sources/Wasm remain and are regenerated by the release
build. All 1,212 workspace tests, packed smoke, final website build, and Bash
syntax checks pass after the clean rebuild. All 13 production browser tests
also pass, covering the rebuilt site, navigation, documentation links, and
playground recovery. The guide, release instructions, architecture, and book now state that
boundary. Rebuilt PDF page 84 was inspected. No npm or Marketplace publication
was performed. Registry metadata identity and publication retries remain to be
assessed separately from local artifact freshness.

Interrupted-release review confirmed that the publisher could invoke recursive
publication for an older version after a newer root version was committed on
origin/main. The local npm CLI contains an older-version guard, but that does
not establish pnpm behavior: the primary pnpm documentation states that v11+
publishes natively and defaults to latest (https://pnpm.io/cli/publish). The
fixture reproduced the CAVE entrypoint reaching publication; it did not perform
or establish a real registry dist-tag downgrade.

The publisher now checks the freshly fetched origin/main version after
preparation and before publishing missing versions. Superseded versions fail
that gate, while fully published older versions retain recovery tagging. A
local-Git/mocked-registry regression covers both refusal and successful old-tag
recovery without republishing. The automatic latest path deliberately does not
perform archival publication of missing superseded versions; release recovery
instructions explain finishing the newer release instead. The rationale and
primary source link are persisted in IMPLEMENTATION.md; release instructions,
architecture, and the book are aligned. Rebuilt PDF page 84 was inspected.
All 1,213 workspace tests, root/website builds, packed smoke, and Bash syntax
checks pass. Registry artifact metadata identity remains a separate review boundary.

This matrix defines the remaining review work by subsystem. A passing command
establishes only the behaviors its tests exercise; it does not replace source
review of the listed boundaries. Fix any defect established by that review,
update its live references, and rerun the affected gate. Existing backlog items
retain their own completion criteria; reviewing release automation does not
silently authorize publishing a release.

| Area | Evidence already obtained | Review still required |
|---|---|---|
| Core, parser, canonicalization | Workspace suite; lossless confidence and explicit replay identity regressions; grammar corpus verification | Review numeric and uncertainty boundaries, token/literal round trips, registry lifecycle rules, and malformed-input coverage in the owning tests. |
| Store and query | Node/WASM adapter contract; cross-connection reservations; historical vocabulary and cursor regressions; ten performance budgets | Review remaining alias, resolution, sensitivity, trajectory and valid-time edge cases against their specification sections. |
| Fusion, shapes, scenarios, solvers | Fusion numerical/probability boundaries; scenario artifact syntax, history and serialization review; workspace suite and packed Z3 smoke | Review shape health/alias boundaries, remaining scenario input binding, solver capability/error states, and explanation provenance; assess whether existing tests establish these contracts. |
| Connect, ingest, sync | Atomic source replacement, exact staging, text/database replay, and provenance regressions | Review remaining source lifecycle and history behavior; match connector-specific malformed input tests to supported formats. |
| Rules, actions, automation | Reservation, rollback, hook ownership, cancellation, exhaustion, declaration and prompt regressions | Review lifecycle history and provenance across firings, and measure a representative larger automation workload. |
| CLI, MCP, view, reports | CLI/book tests, MCP and HTTP packed smoke; audience projections; navigation and report regressions | Review remaining argument/error scope, server cleanup, MCP session teardown, report source references, and data projection boundaries. |
| Website and editor | Production browser tests at seven widths; document anchors; worker recovery; keyboard focus; native grammar verification | Review remaining editor/highlight failure behavior. Manual assistive-technology testing is unavailable and must remain an explicit validation limitation. |
| Build, packages, release | Packed API contract, incremental-build verification, solver-free website bundle verification | Inspect release-validation and publication failure/retry paths; compare supported runtime evidence with the CI matrix. Changesets v3 remains separately tracked. |
| Documentation and completion | Live references and book updated with each fix; book sessions replayed; affected PDF pages inspected | Reconcile each row with final worktree evidence, review examples and reference projections, and preserve final findings outside this temporary audit file before removing it. |

## Earlier review checkpoints

These entries preserve earlier observations, including issues described as open
at the time. For example, the native Z3 cleanup issue mentioned below has a later
fix and stress-test entry above. These notes do not reopen that issue or replace
the current remaining scope. Consult the owning live references and current
regressions for the resulting contract.

Numeric-token boundary checks passed for bare numbers/multipliers with final
line terminators; no parser change was needed for that investigated case.
Temporal ambiguity review then reproduced interpolation of a claim carrying
both closed and open ranges because range selection ignored open ranges.
Selection now rejects any open range and still allows point/opaque contexts
alongside the single closed range. The regression fails before the fix and
checks both context orders. A query regression preserves valid-time visibility
while retaining textual trajectory values. All 90 core and 95 query tests and
the workspace build pass. Core/query/implementation references document the
boundary; §32.3 and book chapter 10 already require open or multiple ranges to
remain textual. Broader temporal/subsystem review and the native Z3 Wasm issue
remain open.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Programmatic-claim review reproduced `Claim.of` accepting non-finite scalar and
trajectory fields plus confidence outside finite `[0, 1]`. The constructor now
rejects those values with `RangeError`, alongside its existing uncertainty
checks. The regression fails before the fix and covers metric/attribute values,
all non-finite forms, confidence bounds and valid finite extremes. All 89 core,
81 parser and 114 store tests and the workspace build pass. Core/implementation
references document early rejection; existing valid book/spec examples remain
accurate. This validates constructor inputs, not arbitrary objects assembled
without the constructor. Broader subsystem review and the native Z3 Wasm issue
remain open.
The full workspace suite passes all 1,299 tests. Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke
and the production website build also pass.

Decimal-scale review reproduced `1.001K` differing from `1001` and tiny
significands becoming zero before a multiplier could make them representable.
Parsing now applies a decimal exponent before one numeric conversion; nonzero
scaled magnitudes that still round to zero follow the atom fallback. Regressions
fail before the fix and cover all multipliers, signs, true zero, subnormals,
trajectory endpoints, units, approximation and stored numeric/text projections.
All 88 core, 81 parser, 114 store and 94 query tests and the workspace build
pass. Core and implementation references document the boundary; ordinary book
and grammar examples remain accurate. Remaining numeric/programmatic-value
and broader subsystem review and the native Z3 Wasm issue stay open.
The full workspace suite passes all 1,298 tests. Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke
and the production website build also pass.

Numeric parsing review reproduced oversized scalar/trajectory literals exposing
infinite normalized values. Scalar parsing now requires finiteness after
multiplier expansion, so those forms follow the existing atom fallback with
authored text intact. The regression fails before the fix and covers signs,
units, multipliers, approximate values and either trajectory endpoint; maximum
finite values remain numeric. A storage regression confirms text retention with
NULL numeric projection. All 86 core, 81 parser, 113 store and 94 query tests
and the workspace build pass. Core/implementation references record the runtime
boundary; grammar and ordinary book examples remain accurate. Programmatic
value construction, underflow and the remaining subsystem matrix still need
review, and the native Z3 Wasm issue remains open.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Trajectory review reproduced finite opposite-sign endpoints overflowing their
difference and endpoint arithmetic losing the exact declared value. Interpolation
now returns clamped endpoints directly and uses a weighted sum across signs.
A related regression reproduced four-digit display rounding overflowing near
the finite maximum; formatting now retains the unscaled finite value if rounding
or multiplier expansion would overflow. Both regressions fail before their fixes.
All 85 core and 94 query tests pass, with a final focused check covering both
signs and multiplier-form display values. Package/implementation references
document these safeguards; §32's linear interpolation semantics and book
examples remain accurate. The wider numerical, valid-time and subsystem reviews
remain open, as does the native Z3 Wasm issue.
The full workspace suite passes all 1,293 tests. Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke
and the production website build also pass.

Worker-send review reproduced pending-request retention when `postMessage`
throws: 100 failed sends left 100 resolver entries. The client now deletes only
the failed operation before rejecting it. A worker-double regression fails
before the fix and checks that earlier pending work survives, failed entries
are released, and a later request succeeds on the same worker. The website test
command now includes this client test alongside runtime tests, retaining direct
Node execution without a module-replacement loader. All 9 website tests and 21
production browser tests pass, as does the production build. Website reference
documents send failure semantics; package/book contracts need no changes.
Broader review and the separate native Z3 Wasm issue remain open.

SQLite-startup review reproduced Rebuild reusing a rejected initialization
promise after a failed WebAssembly download. Inspection of installed SQL.js
confirmed it caches that failure internally too, so clearing only CAVE's cache
would not recover. Initialization errors now carry a fatal worker response;
the client retires the worker and the existing rebuild path creates a new one.
The browser regression fails before the fix and proves a new download plus
edited-source retention after recovery. All 21 production browser tests, 8
runtime tests and the website build pass, including atomic-ingest retention
regressions. Website reference records why a fresh worker is required; existing
book/package contracts remain accurate. Broader review and the separate native
Z3 Wasm failure remain open.

Route-loading review reproduced failed lazy Docs/Playground downloads removing
the whole application, including navigation. A route error boundary now keeps
the header available and offers reload; changing route families resets the
boundary while normal document navigation retains filter state. Both download
regressions fail against the old production build and prove home navigation
plus successful reload recovery. All 20 production browser tests, 8 runtime
tests and the website build pass. Focused phone/desktop recovery checks pass,
and both screenshots were visually inspected without overflow. Website reference
documents recovery; book/package contracts remain unchanged. Broader review and
the independent native Z3 Wasm issue remain open.

Playground startup review reproduced a synchronous Worker-construction failure
escaping the effect and unmounting the page. Construction now occurs inside
the open/rebuild error boundary, which can create a runtime when none exists.
The browser regression fails against the previous production build and proves
visible startup failure, retry with edited claims, and no uncaught page error.
All 18 production browser tests, 8 runtime tests and the website build pass.
Website reference documents initial-startup recovery; existing package and book
contracts remain accurate. Broader website/system review and the independent
Z3 Wasm failure remain open.

Playground worker review reproduced a crash leaving the UI marked ready and
Rebuild reusing a closed worker. Runtime failures now immediately mark the UI
as errored, disable database operations, and explain rebuilding. Rebuild creates
a replacement using current editor contents, and unmount closes the currently
owned worker. The browser regression fails against the old build and verifies
edited-source retention, successful queries after recovery, and termination of
both failed/replacement workers after navigation. All 17 production browser
and 8 runtime tests pass; the final cleanup assertion passes in a focused rerun.
Website build and diff checks pass. Website reference records the distinction
between fatal worker failure and atomic-ingest failure retaining a healthy
database. Existing book and package contracts remain accurate. Broader website
and subsystem reviews and the separate native Z3 Wasm bug remain open.

Documentation-filter review found a placeholder-only input without an
accessible name and blank navigation for unmatched queries. The filter now has
an explicit name, result-status text, slug matching, and a clear action that
restores focus. Current-page navigation exposes `aria-current`. The new browser
regression fails against the old production build and covers empty recovery,
focus restoration, slug lookup and current-page semantics. All 16 production
browser and 8 website runtime tests pass, as does the website build. The mobile
empty-state screenshot was inspected and remains readable. Website reference
documents the behavior; manual assistive-technology announcement verification
remains unavailable. Book and package contracts need no change for this UI-only
improvement; broader review and the Wasm bug remain open.

Website route review reproduced unknown document slugs silently displaying the
overview, nested document paths being truncated, and unrelated routes rendering
home (or matching the broad `docs` prefix). Route matching now preserves full
document paths, shows explicit missing-page/document messages, and provides
history-preserving recovery links. The regression fails against the previous
production build. All 15 production browser tests pass, with the extended
recovery test passing separately at phone/desktop widths; screenshots were
visually inspected without horizontal overflow. Website build and runtime tests
pass. Website reference documents recovery behavior; package contracts and book
examples need no changes. Broader website/editor and subsystem review remains
open alongside the recorded Wasm issue.

Text-scope review confirmed explanations omitted snapshot alias/resolution
policies, minimum confidence and scenario overlay identity. The renderer now
shows supplied policies (including zero confidence) and labels both input and
overlay digests. It does not invent defaults for omitted metadata. The regression
fails before the fix and distinguishes changed thresholds/overlays; all 75
solver and 22 scenario tests and the workspace build pass. Package and
implementation references document the projection. The book describes the same
evidence scope without a literal output fixture, so its existing text remains
accurate. Deep payload rendering is covered by the cross-runtime regression
and iterative serializer above; the broader subsystem matrix remains open.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Explanation-metadata review reproduced acceptance of invalid snapshot policy
names, non-finite/out-of-range confidence, and malformed scenario identifiers.
Shared preflight now validates those fields in reports and before backend
execution, retaining opaque external labels and the separate model-digest
identity check. Regressions fail before the fix, verify zero backend calls,
and preserve confidence endpoints plus external digest labels. All 74 solver
and 22 scenario tests and the workspace build pass. Package and implementation
references document the distinction between metadata shape and external
snapshot verification; existing book context examples remain valid. The deep
input rendering gap is addressed above; remaining report projection review
and the wider subsystem matrix stay open.
The full workspace suite passes all 1,288 tests. Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke
and the production website build also pass.

Explanation-payload review reproduced reports accepting non-finite numbers,
cycles and other values that JSON changes or cannot serialize. Authored and
normalized input payloads now use iterative JSON validation before cloning and
backend execution, rejecting invalid primitives, sparse/undefined array
members, non-plain objects and custom serializers. Shared records and optional
undefined record properties remain supported. The regression fails before the
fix and verifies zero backend calls through solve and workflow entrypoints;
all 72 solver and 22 scenario tests and the workspace build pass. Package and
implementation references document the boundary; existing book examples are
valid. Snapshot/scenario context metadata and deep payload rendering remain
separate review work, as does the wider subsystem matrix.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Explanation-binding review reproduced acceptance of duplicate input IDs and
malformed source lists. Shared validation now rejects ambiguous identities,
non-object/sparse inputs, non-string queries, and invalid source-list members
with `TypeError` in report construction and before explanation/workflow backend
execution. External IDs remain opaque, and authored/normalized JSON payload
validation remains a separate review boundary. The regression fails before the
fix and verifies zero adapter calls across invalid contexts. All 70 solver and
22 scenario tests and the workspace build pass. Package and implementation
references document the contract; existing valid book bindings remain accurate.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Explanation-input review reproduced authored-only bindings rendering as
`undefined`, with authored values and input-level evidence/scenario references
omitted from text output. Input lines now retain both representations and
sorted source references, and distinguish missing values from explicit JSON
null. The regression fails before the fix; all 69 solver and 22 scenario tests
and the workspace build pass. Package and implementation references describe
the projection. The book's existing evidence/explanation contract remains
accurate without a source change. Remaining explanation review includes
malformed context and provenance binding validation, alongside the wider matrix.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Runtime-lifecycle review reproduced `create()` returning the closing runtime,
which would reject a caller's next solve. Creation now waits for the pending
shutdown and converges on one new singleton. Each runtime shares one close
promise; repeated closes cannot clear a replacement. A real child-process
regression fails before the fix and checks queued work drains, concurrent
creation shares a usable replacement, closed-runtime solves are rejected,
and all workers terminate. All 25 adapter tests and the workspace build pass.
Package and implementation references document the lifecycle; existing book
shutdown guidance remains accurate. Native cleanup synchronization is handled
separately by the guard documented above.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Wasm failure investigation did not reproduce the recorded corruption in three
consecutive full adapter runs (24 tests each), ten optimization cycles under
forced collection, or ten memory-limit/recovery cycles under forced collection.
The latter experiment is preserved as `test:memory-stress`, which validates all
3,000 assignment values and the exact objective after each expected resource
failure, logs runtime metadata, and closes workers on assertion failures.
The smaller diagnostic does not cover the original large-model case. The
subsequent large-mode regression and native cleanup guard documented above
address that gap. The package reference documents both modes; no book change
is needed for this development-only command.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Optimality review reproduced a false proof of optimality for an unbounded real
objective. Every explicit objective now retains its optimizer handle and must
have equal finite rational lower/upper bounds attained by the returned model.
The before-fix regression reports `optimal` for an unbounded objective; after
the fix both directions and strict unattained bounds return
`unknown/indeterminate`. Regressions also preserve attained exact one-third
optima and check later lexicographic objectives. Package and implementation
references describe the boundary; the book's disjoint result/proof contract
remains accurate. Soft-only optimization and remaining backend error states
remain in the solver review scope, alongside the wider subsystem matrix.
The workspace build, packed smoke and website build pass. An initial final
adapter run encountered an intermittent Wasm memory-access failure in the
large-variable test, cascading into later requests; the isolated rerun passed
all 24 tests. The later large diagnostic reproduced corruption and established
the native cleanup repair documented above; that repair is supported by
repeated forced-GC regressions rather than the original isolated retry.

Tracker-identity review reproduced a false proof of infeasibility: a Boolean
variable named `cave.constraint.policy` collided with the tracker for constraint
`policy` when unsat-core extraction was enabled. Trackers now use Z3's fresh
Boolean symbols with the existing map back to portable IDs. The regression
fails before the fix, confirms satisfiability with and without core extraction,
and checks original IDs in the core of a truly contradictory extension. All
21 adapter tests and the workspace build pass; the final extended core check
also passes separately. Package and implementation references preserve the
finding and semantics. Book descriptions of tracked IDs remain accurate.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Variable-bound review reproduced argument-list overflow after validation
accepted 75,000 bounded integer variables. Generated bounds now enter both
Solver and Optimize in batches of at most 1,024 assertions. The integration
regression fails before the fix and proves the final variable's lower bound is
retained in feasibility and optimization. All 20 Z3 tests and the workspace
build pass. Package and implementation references document batching; the book's
existing semantics remain accurate. Backend error states and explanation
provenance remain in review, alongside the wider subsystem matrix.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Boolean-width review reproduced `unknown/backend-error` from a conjunction
with 99,999 operands, within the default 100,000-node limit. Both Boolean
operators now compile in associative groups of at most 1,024 arguments.
The current binding's AstVector overload also spreads internally, so merely
switching overloads would not remove the limit. The regression fails before
the fix and checks both operators with a decisive final operand after the
last full group. All 19 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass. Package and
implementation references document the boundary; book examples and semantics
remain accurate. Raised variable limits still need review because adding all
generated domain bounds uses a separate spread call. Backend error-state and
the wider subsystem reviews remain open.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Real-backend depth review reproduced Z3 returning `unknown/backend-error` for
a valid constraint with 20,000 nested negations because JavaScript compilation
overflowed. Compilation now traverses explicitly and caches expressions per
model. Integration regressions prove deep solving, repeated shared-factor
semantics, isolation across requests, and bounded rejection of cycles passed
directly to the adapter. All 18 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass. Package
and implementation references document the change; the book's compilation
semantics and examples remain accurate without source changes. Remaining
resource review includes broad expression fan-out and backend error states;
the subsystem matrix above continues to define the wider audit scope.
The full workspace run passed 1,274 tests; the final cycle guard was then
covered by the 18-test adapter rerun and a fresh workspace build.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Linear-depth review reproduced call-stack exhaustion on a valid objective with
20,000 nested negations in both its affine numerator and exact constant divisor.
Classification and constant evaluation now use explicit stacks and per-model
caches. The regression fails before the fix; a shared-factor regression confirms
that caching does not incorrectly classify a square as affine. All 68 solver
and 15 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass. Package and implementation
references document the behavior; the book's existing linear-subset contract
remains accurate without a source change. Real backend expression compilation
still uses recursive traversal and remains the next depth boundary to verify.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build also pass.

Explanation-depth review reproduced valid deep hard/soft constraints being
reported as indeterminate because evaluation caught a recursive stack overflow.
Evaluation now uses an explicit stack of suspended expression evaluations,
retaining lazy Boolean/conditional branches and exact arithmetic. The deep
regression fails before the fix; short-circuit regressions preserve skipped
undefined arithmetic and still report selected undefined arithmetic as
indeterminate. All 66 solver and 15 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass.
Package/implementation references and book describe the boundary; rebuilt page
87 passed visual inspection. Deep linear analysis and real backend compilation
remain in the resource review scope.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed as well.

Canonical-depth review reproduced recursive conversion failing after deep-model
validation succeeded. Expression conversion and JSON rendering now use explicit
stacks; commutative ordering compares canonical token streams lazily instead of
eagerly rendering whole subtrees. Tests cover 20,000-level identities and an
unknown-result explanation, 10,000-level reversed products, and a captured
pre-change fixture digest. A separate seeded comparison of 300 varied shallow
models matched the original canonicalizer's bytes and digests exactly. All 64
solver and 15 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass. Package and implementation
references describe the unchanged format; CLI/MCP contracts and book examples
remain valid and were reviewed without edits. Deep-tree feasible-result
evaluation, linear analysis, and real backend compilation remain to review.
The complete workspace suite passed all 1,268 tests. Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3
smoke and workspace/production website builds passed as well.

Copy-compatibility review found that the new iterative helper could evaluate
getters twice when falling back, change accessor order, and invoke proxy traps
instead of producing native clone rejection. Descriptor/proxy preflight now
selects one native clone of the whole graph before evaluating accessors; only
portable data properties take the iterative path. All three regressions fail
before this correction. All 60 solver and 15 Z3 tests and the workspace build
pass, including the existing deep-submission test. Package and implementation
references explain the selection boundary. CLI/MCP contracts and book examples
remain unchanged and were reviewed without additional edits.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed as well.

Deep-copy review reproduced native structured-clone stack overflow between
successful model validation and adapter execution. Portable record/array copies
now use an explicit queue and identity map throughout Solve and Workflow inputs.
A 20,000-level model reaches a test adapter as an independent deeply frozen
submission while caller objects stay editable. Additional copy tests preserve
sharing, cycles, sparse-array shape, data keys, and native fallback behavior for
nonportable containers. The deep-submission regression fails before the fix.
All 57 solver and 15 Z3 tests and the workspace build pass. Package and
implementation references document copying; public APIs, CLI/MCP contracts,
and book examples are unchanged and were reviewed without edits. Deep-tree
canonicalization, linear analysis, explanation evaluation, and real backend
compilation remain in the resource review scope.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed as well.

Capability traversal review reproduced stack overflow on 20,000 nested products
and found repeated subtree walks for variable dependence. Discovery now uses
an explicit stack, detects active-node cycles, and reuses completed-node results
within each expression root. Variable dependence is computed bottom-up, while
two occurrences of one variable-bearing factor still make a product nonlinear.
Both regressions fail before the fix. All 54 solver and 15 Z3 tests and the
workspace build pass. Package and implementation references document graph
reuse separately from validation's per-occurrence accounting. CLI/MCP contracts,
CAVE syntax, and book examples are unchanged and were reviewed without edits.
Deep-tree canonicalization, cloning, linear analysis, and adapters remain in
the resource review scope.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed as well.

Raised-depth validation review reproduced stack overflow despite sufficient
configured limits. Expression inference now uses an explicit post-order stack
with lazy child traversal, preserving entry budget checks and per-occurrence
statistics/diagnostics for shared objects. A 20,001-node deep expression validates
under a matching depth limit; the depth regression fails before the refactor.
All 52 solver and 15 Z3 tests pass. Package and implementation references explain
the traversal contract; public APIs, book examples, and CLI/MCP contracts are
unchanged and were reviewed without edits. Deep-tree handling in downstream
canonicalization, cloning, capability analysis, and adapters remains to review;
this evidence establishes validation traversal only.
The complete workspace suite passed all 1,256 tests. Workspace/website builds
and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke passed as well, establishing these gates for
the accumulated worktree while the broader source review remains open.

Expression-budget review reproduced post-traversal enforcement allowing a
20,000-level expression to overflow the call stack and an over-budget child to
be inspected. Node/depth checks now run at each traversal entry. Regressions
cover deep and cyclic input under default limits and a child whose getter must
never run once the node budget is exceeded; both fail before the fix. All 50
solver and 15 Z3 tests pass. The package and implementation references explain
first-exceeded-boundary reporting; existing book examples and CLI/MCP contracts
remain valid and were reviewed without edits. Host recursion interactions at
very high caller-selected depth limits remain part of the resource review.
The workspace and production website builds and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke
passed after correcting the deliberate malformed fixture's TypeScript cast.

Portable-sort review reproduced unknown variable sorts and non-Boolean Boolean
literals passing validation, plus unknown literal sorts falling through to
variable lookup when supplied a matching ID. Validation now explicitly rejects
these malformed values. The regression fails before the fix. All 48 solver and
15 Z3 tests, workspace/website builds, and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke pass
afterward. The package and implementation references preserve the boundary;
CAVE syntax, CLI/MCP contracts, and valid book examples are unchanged and were
reviewed without additional edits. The changeset records this restoration of
the portable model's existing sorts.

Enum-domain review reproduced non-string members, missing array elements, and
string containers passing model validation, allowing backend enum values to
violate the portable string contract. Validation now requires a nonempty dense
array of distinct primitive strings. Empty strings, Unicode, and spaces remain
valid members; enum members are distinct from declaration identifiers. The
regression fails before the fix. The package and implementation references
document the boundary; existing CAVE syntax, CLI/MCP references, and book examples
remain valid and were reviewed without further edits.
All 47 solver and 15 Z3 tests, the workspace and production website builds,
and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke passed after the fix.

Solver declaration-ID review reproduced trailing line terminators and coercible
objects passing the identifier regex. Validation now requires primitive strings
matching the entire grammar for all five declaration types. The regression
fails before the fix; all 46 solver tests and the workspace build pass afterward.
The package reference and implementation guide preserve the identity boundary.
This restores the existing identifier grammar without changing CAVE syntax or
book examples; those surfaces were reviewed and need no edit for this fix.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed as well.

Exact-number review reproduced coercible non-Integer values being accepted and
decimal zero failing while expanding an unused enormous power of ten. Integer
parsing now requires primitive safe numbers or whole integer strings, and zero
normalizes after exponent validation but before power expansion. Full-match
checks also reject final line terminators that JavaScript's `$` anchor permits.
The initial two regressions fail before the fix; a third covers integer/decimal
strings ending in CR, LF, CRLF, or Unicode line separators. All 45 solver and
15 Z3 tests pass, as does the workspace build. Package and implementation
references document these library contracts. CAVE lexical syntax, CLI/MCP
references, and existing book examples are unaffected and were reviewed; no
book source/PDF edit is needed for this change. A minor changeset records the
stricter accepted input types and string boundary.
The packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and production website build passed as well.

The remaining linear-analysis limit review confirmed that `Linear.model` could
not classify a larger valid model under caller-selected bounds. It now accepts
optional validation limits, matching canonical analysis and solve configuration.
A 1,001-variable regression fails before the enhancement, retains rejection
under default/insufficient limits, and produces the same classification under
different sufficient limits. All 42 solver tests and the workspace build pass.
The package reference and implementation guide document the optional argument;
CAVE language, CLI/MCP contracts, and book examples remain unchanged and were
reviewed for this library-only API extension. A minor changeset records it.
Packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and the production website build passed. The
packed API delta was inspected and contains only the optional `Linear.model`
parameter and its declaration fingerprint.

Linear-subset review reproduced computed zero divisors being accepted as
affine: `0.3 - (0.1 + 0.2)` is exactly zero in portable rational arithmetic.
Recognition now evaluates constant denominators exactly, rejecting computed
zero and undefined nested divisors while accepting a nonzero `1e-400` offset.
General SMT validation deliberately retains its separate totalized-arithmetic
contract; this fix changes LP/MIP classification only. The regression fails
before the fix. All 41 solver and 15 Z3 tests pass, as does the workspace build.
The package reference and implementation guide preserve the rationale. The
book was updated and its growing explanation section split into readable
paragraphs; rebuilt page 87 passed visual inspection.
The packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and production website build passed as well.

Custom-limit review reproduced accepted models failing during explanation or
workflow hashing because canonical identity revalidated with default limits.
`Canonical.serialize` and `Canonical.digest` now accept explicit validation
limits; solve/workflow identity and replay paths pass their configured limits.
Limits remain outside canonical content. Three regressions fail before the fix,
covering a 1,001-variable model, explanation/replay, and feasibility/sensitivity
reports; sufficient limits produce identical serialization and digest. All 40
solver and 15 Z3 tests pass, as does the workspace build. The package reference,
implementation guide, and book explain the boundary; rebuilt page 87 passed
visual inspection. A minor changeset records the optional API parameters.
The packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and production website build passed. The
packed API snapshot delta was inspected: only the two canonical function
signatures and their shared declaration fingerprint changed in this step.

Solver option review reproduced silent defaults for misspelled limits, truthy
non-Boolean core flags, and unknown sensitivity modes. Entry points now reject
unknown option/limit keys, malformed option/limit containers, and non-Boolean
`unsatCore` values before defaulting. Sensitivity accepts only its two documented
operations. Three regressions fail before the fix; all 37 solver and 15 Z3 tests
pass afterward, as does the workspace build. Live references and book document
the stricter runtime contract; rebuilt page 87 passed visual inspection. A
minor changeset records the input tightening. Validation covers the portable
Solve and Workflow entry points; direct adapter implementations retain their
typed Request contract.
The complete workspace suite passed all 1,241 tests after these accumulated
solver changes. The packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke and production website build
also passed. The broader source-review requirements remain open.

Workflow scope review reproduced a report claiming Boolean-only reasoning for
a constant integer-division constraint. Scope theories previously inspected
variable declarations alone. They now use the shared capability analysis,
including literals, division, enum domains, and rational soft weights; domains
still describe declared variables only. The regression fails before the fix.
All 34 solver and 15 Z3 tests pass afterward, as does the workspace build.
The package reference, architecture, implementation guide, and book explain the
distinction; rebuilt page 87 passed visual inspection. This fixes report accuracy
without adding a new solver theory or changing the model schema.
The production website build and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke passed as well.

Workflow ownership review reproduced caller edits changing sensitivity's later
bindings, options, and evidence, despite each individual solve's snapshot.
All four workflow entry points now copy model/options/context before awaiting;
sensitivity copies its request once for the whole sweep. Replay-digest mismatch
is checked before backend execution in the shared workflow runner. Seven
regressions cover snapshot stability and early rejection; the initial four
failure regressions failed against the prior implementation. All 33 solver and
15 Z3 tests pass, as does the workspace build. The package reference,
architecture, implementation guide, and book record the contract; rebuilt page
87 passed visual inspection. Broader workflow result and scope semantics remain
in the solver review scope.
The production website build and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke passed as well.

The solver explanation review reproduced mutable caller inputs crossing an
asynchronous adapter boundary: an edit during execution changed the model and
evidence later used by the report. It also found replay-digest mismatch was
checked only after backend execution. Solve calls now pass a copied, deeply
frozen validated model and frozen limits; explanation calls snapshot context
and check replay identity first. Caller objects remain editable. Both regressions
fail before the fix; all 26 solver and 15 Z3 tests pass afterward. The workspace
build passed, and rebuilt book page 87 passed visual inspection. Public/library
references and architecture document the ownership boundary, with a minor
changeset for the stricter adapter input contract. Workflow-level ownership
across multiple solves is covered by the subsequent workflow review above.
The production website build and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke also passed.

Solver capability review found that division returns an exact real in both
portable validation and Z3 translation, but capability discovery inspected
only declared/literal numeric sorts. Integer-only division could therefore
cross into a backend without rational support. Every division now requires
`rationals`, including nested hard/soft constraints and objectives. A regression
fails before the fix and verifies preflight rejection without adapter invocation
afterward. All 24 solver and 15 Z3 tests pass, as does the workspace build.
The package reference, implementation guide, and book state the capability rule;
rebuilt book pages 86–87 passed visual inspection. This restores existing exact
division semantics rather than introducing a new portable operation.
The production website build and packed-package/API/CLI/Z3 smoke also passed.

The ANSI renderer review reproduced two custom-input defects: an unknown capture
such as `constructor` resolved an inherited Object property as an ANSI style,
and malformed/overlapping ranges silently duplicated or truncated source text.
`paint` now uses own theme entries and rejects unordered, overlapping,
non-integer, reversed, or out-of-bounds ranges with `TypeError`. Adjacent and
empty ranges remain supported, with documented UTF-16 offsets. Both defect
regressions fail before the fix; all thirteen highlighter tests and the workspace
build pass afterward. The package reference and implementation guide contain
the contract; this library-only change does not alter CAVE syntax, the CLI/MCP
reference, or book examples. A minor changeset records the stricter input contract.
The complete workspace suite subsequently passed all 1,227 tests, and the
packed-package/API/CLI smoke passed. This verifies the accumulated worktree
through these gates; the broader source-review requirements below remain open.

The shared-highlighter failure review reproduced permanent rejected-promise
caching in Node and the website. A failed grammar load rejected every future
Node request and kept the playground unhighlighted after subsequent edits.
Both loaders now clear rejected initialization while sharing in-flight and
successful loads. The Node regression and the production-browser regression
(one grammar HTTP 503, then restored service and a source edit) fail before the
fix and recover after it. Plain source remains visible during failure; there
is no background retry loop. Ten highlighter tests and both workspace and
website builds passed. The live package/site references and architecture explain
the recovery boundary; CAVE syntax, CLI/MCP surfaces, and book examples are
unchanged by this loader fix.
All fourteen production browser tests and the packed-package/API/CLI smoke
passed after the fix, including real grammar highlighting from the installed
tarballs. No public declaration snapshot change was needed.

The editor lifecycle review found that activation allocated a Tree-sitter parser
and query without registering either for disposal. The extension now unregisters
its semantic-token provider and releases both resources exactly once, including
on failed setup; per-document trees are released even when captures fail.
Five lifecycle regressions fail against the original source and pass after the
fix. Extension typechecking, the production bundle, and all six extension tests
passed. The resource contract is recorded in the extension README, architecture,
implementation guide, and book. These tests use host/resource doubles for failure
injection plus the real packaged grammar test; an interactive VS Code host
session is not established by that evidence.
The real VSIX package passed archive verification, the production website built,
and the rebuilt book's changed page 84 passed visual inspection without overflow.
The public/browser highlighter factory lifetime and remaining editor token
boundaries still need review; this fix establishes extension ownership only.

The 2026-09-07 publication audit queried all twelve public packages at 0.35.0:
each exposed archive integrity and provenance metadata, and none exposed
`gitHead`. An isolated installation with lifecycle scripts disabled verified
43 registry signatures and 27 attestations across that dependency tree.
These findings describe the published version, not the uncommitted audit fixes.
`pnpm release:audit` now makes that check repeatable. Presence probes remain
separate from cryptographic verification and local rebuild equality; requiring
optional `gitHead` or universal provenance would reject legitimate publication
paths. The lasting contract is recorded in `IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
The implemented command reproduced the 43-signature/27-attestation result.
All 93 MCP/tooling tests, including five audit orchestration and failure-cleanup
tests, passed; the workspace and production website builds passed. This adds
a developer command without changing CAVE CLI/MCP contracts or book examples;
those documentation surfaces were reviewed and need no further edit for it.
